articles.title: À Miami, l'atterrissage raté d'un Boeing aux couleurs d'Amazon fait plusieurs morts et blessés
articles.text:
Un Boeing 767, qui assurait une liaison Prime Air pour Amazon, a raté sa piste à l'aéroport de Miami ce week-end avant de s'embraser dans un champ voisin. Cinq morts et cinq blessés sont à déplorer, et une enquête fédérale vient de démarrer.
Dimanche après-midi, le vol cargo Prime Air 7598 a fini par quitter la piste de l'aéroport international de Miami, en provenance de Porto Rico. L'aéronef, un Boeing 767-300, a percuté plusieurs véhicules avant de s'immobiliser en flammes. Les pompiers ont dû mener une opération de désincarcération pour libérer des automobilistes piégés, tout en extrayant l'équipage piégé dans le cockpit alors que les moteurs brûlaient. Amazon, la compagnie 21 Air et les autorités fédérales ont depuis multiplié les déclarations. Sur place, les autorités ont ouvert une enquête pour déterminer les causes de cet accident.
Un avion-cargo d'Amazon s'écrase à Miami, cinq morts à déplorer
Peu avant 14 heures dimanche heure locale, le vol Prime Air 7598 atterrit à l'aéroport international de Miami après avoir décollé de San Juan, à Porto Rico. L'appareil, un Boeing 767-300 exploité par la compagnie de fret 21 Air, qui opère pour le géant du e-commerce, roulait encore à près de 210 km/h en quittant la partie utilisable de la piste 30, selon les données de Flightradar24, avant de traverser une route, faucher plusieurs véhicules et finir sa course, en flammes, dans un champ adjacent à l'aéroport.
Le bilan communiqué par la maire du comté de Miami-Dade, Daniella Levine Cava, est assez lourd, puisqu'il fait état de cinq décès et cinq autres blessées, dont trois dans un état critique. Sur place, les pompiers ont mené une opération de désincarcération complexe pour libérer des automobilistes piégés, avant d'extraire le pilote et le copilote, piégés dans le cockpit alors que les moteurs de l'appareil étaient la proie des flammes.
Près de 200 pompiers et plus de soixante unités du Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, les soldats du feu locaux, ont été mobilisés pour circonscrire l'incendie, en recourant à une mousse spéciale pour venir à bout des flammes. Des équipes spécialisées en matières dangereuses ont ensuite coupé le moteur endommagé pour juguler une fuite de kérosène, toujours active plusieurs heures après l'accident. Présente sur le tarmac, la maire Daniella Levine Cava a elle-même fait état, sur X, d'un point de situation reçu de la FAA, l'agence gouvernementale américaine qui assure la régulation de l'aviation civile, à mesure que les opérations se poursuivaient.
Amazon, Boeing et 21 Air réagissent au drame
La FAA et le NTSB (Conseil national américain de la sécurité des transports) ont ouvert une enquête pour déterminer les causes de cette sortie de piste. Le NTSB a dépêché une équipe dirigée par sa présidente, Jennifer Homendy, et doit tenir une conférence de presse à Miami dès ce lundi. On a par ailleurs appris que les échanges avec la tour de contrôle ne font état d'aucune déclaration d'urgence de la part des pilotes avant l'atterrissage. Pour l'heure, aucune hypothèse, qu'elle soit technique, humaine ou météorologique, n'a été formellement privilégiée.
Par contre, près de 200 vols ont été annulés dimanche, et seules deux des quatre pistes de l'aéroport ont rouvert dans la soirée. Le secrétaire américain aux Transports, Sean Duffy, a prévenu les voyageurs de s'attendre à d'importants retards, voire à de possibles annulations, encore ces prochaines heures. Un nouveau coup dur pour l'aviation américaine.

articles.title: „Wir wollen, dass Google uns sagt, was da los ist“: Algorithmwatch entdeckt bedenkliche Muster in KI-Übersichten
articles.text:
Undurchsichtige KI-Übersichten zu Landtagswahlen: „Wir wollen, dass Google uns sagt, was da los ist“
Algorithmwatch hat im Juli 2026 untersucht, wie Googles KI-Übersichten mit Fragen zu wahlbezogenen Inhalten umgehen. Die Ergebnisse legen nahe, dass wahlbezogene Inhalte in den KI-Übersichten womöglich nicht immer neutral sind. Sie deuten darauf hin, dass Google bewusste Entscheidungen darüber trifft, wann eine KI-Übersicht überhaupt angezeigt wird, welche Quellen zitiert werden und wie die Inhalte formuliert sind.
Algorithmwatch hat die Landtagswahlen 2026 in Sachsen-Anhalt und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern sowie die Abgeordnetenwahl in Berlin für ihre Untersuchung in den Blick genommen. Sie haben Zugang zu Googles „Search Researcher Result“-Softwareschnittstelle erhalten und so knapp 4.500 Suchanfragen zu den Wahlen gestellt. Die Ergebnisse wurden mit Blick auf die KI-Übersichten selbst sowie deren Quellen hin ausgewertet.
Unklar, wann Google eine KI-Übersicht anzeigt und wann nicht
Die Organisation erstellte zunächst einen Datensatz mit unpolitischen Suchanfragen zu Vergleichszwecken. Enthalten waren etwa Anfragen zu Reisezielen und was man in Land X unternehmen kann. „Bei Suchanfragen zu den Landtagswahlen im Jahr 2026 zeigte Google in 39,1 Prozent der Fälle eine KI-Übersicht, während es bei nicht-politischen Anfragen in 65,3 Prozent der Fälle so war“, heißt es.
Eine KI-Übersicht wurde nie angezeigt, wenn das Team lediglich den Namen und die Partei eines Kandidaten in die Suchleiste eingab. Fast immer spielte Google KI-generierte Übersichten aus, wenn explizit nach politischen Standpunkten einer Person gegoogelt wurde. Sie fragten etwa danach, wofür Sven Schulze (CDU) politisch steht oder was die Ansichten von Claudia Müller (Bündnis 90/Die Grünen) sind. Außerdem fällt auf, dass der Anteil von KI-Übersichten zu den Landtagswahlen in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern etwa 15 Prozent höher ist als der zu denen in Sachsen-Anhalt.
Auf Nachfrage von Algorithmwatch habe Google bestätigt, dass KI-Übersichten nicht bei jeder Suchanfrage ausgespielt würden, „sondern nur, wenn das Unternehmen der Ansicht ist, dass sie für Nutzer:innen einen Mehrwert bieten und die Qualität der Antworten gesichert ist“. Google habe allerdings nicht transparent gemacht, auf welcher Basis diese Entscheidung gefällt werde. „Man könnte jetzt anfangen zu spekulieren. Das wollen wir aber nicht. Wir wollen, dass Google uns sagt, was da los ist“, sagt Clara Helming, Senior Policy Managerin bei Algorithmwatch und Projektleiterin der Untersuchung.
Geringe Vielfalt bei zitierten Quellen
Algorithmwatch stellte im Rahmen ihrer Analyse eine geringe Vielfalt der zitierten Quellen fest. „Fast die Hälfte aller angezeigten Links stammt von nur zehn verschiedenen Domains“, schreiben sie. Zu den häufig zitierten Domains zählen etwa öffentlich-rechtliche Medien, Zeit Online und Seiten der Landtage in Sachsen-Anhalt und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
Noch seien die zitierten Quellen in den KI-Übersichten von Google in Ordnung, sagt die Projektleiterin. „Aber wir befinden uns mit dieser Entwicklung erst am Anfang. Es ist nicht garantiert, dass die Qualität so bleibt, da Google auch jetzt schon das Informationsökosystem untergräbt.“
Auffällig ist außerdem, dass der Analyse zufolge Youtube die am häufigsten zitierte Domain ist. Die Dominanz von Youtube zeigt sich in der Untersuchung vor allem bei Fragen zu den Kandidaten. „Auch damit haben wir Google konfrontiert. Sie bestreiten eine Bevorzugung der eigenen Plattform.“
Wie neutral werden Politiker beschrieben?
„Politische Positionen von Kandidat:innen werden in KI-Übersichten häufig nicht neutral beschrieben“, heißt es in den Ergebnissen. Stattdessen werden die Haltungen der Kandidat:innen mit positiven Formulierungen wiedergegeben, die eher an Selbstbeschreibungen erinnern. Wenig präzise, aber positiv konnotierte, Adjektive wie „bürgernah“ und „stabil“ tauchten häufig auf. „Die politischen Ansichten von Steffen Krach (SPD) zeichnen sich durch einen pragmatischen, bürgernahen und umsetzungsorientierten Kurs aus“, führt Algorithmwatch als eines von vielen Beispielen an.
Folgen für politische Meinungsbildung und Demokratie
„Menschen sind auf verlässliche und neutrale Informationen angewiesen, wenn sie sich etwa zum Thema Wahlen informieren wollen“, meint Helming. Bekommen sie diese verlässlichen und neutralen Informationen nicht, habe das wiederum einen negativen Effekt auf die Demokratie.
Helming sieht ein Grundproblem in der mangelnden Transparenz und der fehlenden Aufsicht von großen Tech-Unternehmen wie Google. „Das ist problematisch, denn Googles Produktentscheidungen beeinflussen wichtige Vorbedingungen der Meinungsbildung in der Demokratie: den Zugang zu verlässlichen Informationen und vielfältigen Quellen.“
Durch die KI-Übersichten sei der Anreiz für User:innen gering, noch die Originalquelle aufzusuchen, wodurch Google eine große Verantwortung zukomme. „Das Unternehmen hat sich den Medienhäusern vorgeschaltet und sich journalistische Inhalte angeeignet – ohne direkte Erlaubnis“, sagt Helming.
Immerhin gibt Google in den KI-Übersichten an, aus welchen Quellen es sich bedient hat. Dass diese nie objektiv sind, da jede Chefredaktion einen speziellen Meinungskorridor bedient oder aber bestimmte Inhalte hinter Paywalls verriegelt und so von der Suche ausschließt, kann man m.E. nicht Google vorwerfen. Im übrigen bieten etliche Medien die Eintragung als bevorzugte Quelle an, so dass man auch als Nutzer einen gewissen Einfluss auf das Ergebnis nehmen kann.

articles.title: BigBear Microsoft 365 phishing service bypassed MFA at 258 organizations
articles.text:
A phishing-as-a-service framework called BigBear 2.0 has been used to bypass multi-factor authentication at 258 organizations and steal more than 5,000 Microsoft 365 credentials.
Researchers at cybersecurity company CloudSEK gained administrator access to the control panel and found that the service managed 42 VPS nodes, all configured to target Microsoft 365 as part of the observed operation.
According to the researchers, the campaign uses an Evilginx2-based adversary-in-the-middle framework to intercept passwords and authenticated session cookies, allowing attackers to hijack accounts after victims complete the multi-factor authentication (MFA) process.
BigBear uses a configuration called “offy” that sets up a man-in-the-middle (AiTM) proxy between the victim and Microsoft’s legitimate authentication infrastructure.
This allows the attacker to capture credentials, including MFA, and session cookies and replay them through an API to hijack the victim’s authentication session.
Microsoft 365 is Microsoft's cloud productivity and identity ecosystem, incorporating services such as Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Entra ID authentication.
Compromising an authenticated Microsoft 365 session can expose email and files while potentially providing access to other applications connected through single sign-on.
According to CloudSEK, BigBear proved to be sufficiently successful to compromise hundreds of entities and capture thousands of cookies.
“The panel has exfiltrated 5,137 credential records - including 474 complete MFA-bypassed authentications, 1,032 plaintext passwords, and 4,148 session cookies - affecting 3,331 unique victim IPs across 40+ countries with the operation still active at the time of writing,” CloudSEK says in a report shared with BleepingComputer.
“The multi-user PhaaS panel is leased to at least five affiliate operators identified through live Telegram exfiltration bots, each receiving stolen credentials in real time.”
While 461 organizations appeared in the broader targeting dataset, CloudSEK clarified that 258 distinct organizations had at least one completed MFA-bypass compromise.
CloudSEK has also found that BigBear uses custom JavaScript that interferes with FIDO2/WebAuthn authentication, disabling the browser functionality that accommodates it to force targets toward weaker authentication methods.
To increase its effectiveness, the platform uses geo-matched residential proxies for 69 countries, matching the victim’s location with a residential IP address so that Microsoft’s authentication servers don’t flag the activity as suspicious.
CloudSEK said it notified law enforcement and several affected organizations and included credentials in responsible-disclosure reports.
At the time of writing, the administration panel remains online, while the phishing infrastructure has been offline for nearly three weeks.
Organizations that were potentially affected by BigBear activity should reset exposed passwords, revoke active sessions, refresh tokens, and force re-authentication for high-privileged accounts.
It is also advisable to enforce phishing-resistant FIDO2/WebAuthn and use Conditional Access policies that require managed devices rather than relying on geo-location signals.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Isar Aerospace ha hecho historia con su cohete Spectrum. Europa occidental ya tiene acceso propio al espacio
articles.text:
La carrera espacial privada europea acaba de dar un gran paso adelante con el lanzamiento exitoso del cohete Spectrum desde el centro espacial de Andøya, en Noruega. La compañía alemana Isar Aerospace ya había hecho un intento en marzo de 2025. Sin embargo, terminó cayendo de nuevo a Tierra poco después de su lanzamiento. Ahora, se ha logrado llevar sin problemas a su destino, de modo que se ha convertido en el primer cohete puesto en órbita desde Europa Occidental. En el pasado, se lanzaron muchos cohetes desde el lado ruso, pero esta parte de Europa había necesitado siempre plataformas de lanzamiento mucho más lejos de su territorio.
Lanzamiento y despliegue exitosos. El lanzamiento de Spectrum tuvo lugar el pasado 5 de septiembre, a las 22:12, hora local de Noruega. Se logró lanzar con éxito el cohete de Isar Aerospace y también ponerlo en órbita. No obstante, la misión no se dio completada hasta que se desplegaron los cinco cubesats que llevaba a bordo junto a un experimento no desplegable.
Los tiempos. El cohete tardó solo 7 minutos en colocarse en una órbita elíptica alrededor de la Tierra. Aquí, como señalan en Space, ya se grabó su nombre en los libros de historia, pues ningún cohete había logrado nada igual desde suelo de Europa occidental. Pero la órbita final del cohete alrededor de la Tierra no debía ser elíptica, sino circular. Por eso, después se pasó a lo que se conoce como combustión de circularización. Esto consiste en, una vez en el punto más alto de la órbita elíptica, desacelerar la nave para redondear la órbita. Ya colocado en su órbita circular, el cohete desplegó los cubesats, dando por finalizada su misión. El proceso total tomó unas dos horas.
A la de muchas va la vencida. Isar Aerospace había intentado lanzar Spectrum por primera vez en marzo de 2025. Lo cierto es que lo consiguió. Sin embargo, no pudieron colocarlo en órbita. Con el tiempo se supo que el cohete había vuelto a Tierra por la apertura accidental de una válvula de ventilación y la pérdida del control de actitud en la maniobra de alabeo. Una vez estudiados los errores que pudieron conducir a este problema, se planeó un nuevo lanzamiento en enero de 2026. Sin embargo, un nuevo problema con una válvula, esta vez de presurización, obligó a posponerlo hasta marzo. Hubo varios intentos ese mes, pero la meteorología no estuvo de parte de Spectrum. También hubo un barco no autorizado en las inmediaciones de la plataforma de lanzamiento que frustró otro de los intentos.
Con todo esto, los lanzamientos se pospusieron una y otra vez hasta llegar a abril. El tiempo dio una tregua el 9 de abril, pero una fuga en un tanque presurizado obligó a llevar a cabo una nueva cancelación. El 15 de junio hubo otro intento, pero un comportamiento anómalo en los sistemas de fluidos del cohete impidió el lanzamiento. Y así llegamos hasta este 5 de septiembre. El lanzamiento se ha hecho de rogar; pero, por fin, Spectrum ha llegado a su destino.
El primero de muchos. El objetivo de Isar Aerospace es que este lanzamiento sea el primero de muchos. Con 28 metros de alto y la capacidad de transportar una tonelada de carga útil, Spectrum podría ser una herramienta muy útil para el lanzamiento de satélites y otros instrumentos a la órbita terrestre baja sin tener que salir de Europa Occidental. Según la compañía, en su planta de fabricación de Múnich se podrían llegar a construir 30 de estos cohetes al año. De momento, habrá que ver si los lanzamientos pueden repetirse sin tantos altercados en el camino. Si se logra agilizar todo, desde luego que será una herramienta esencial en la carrera espacial privada europea.

articles.title: Decoding India’s new-age consumer: Cashfree, Consumer Collective by Atrium to host The Consumer Circle in Gurugram
articles.text:
Cashfree
View Brand Publisher
Decoding India’s new-age consumer: Cashfree, Consumer Collective by Atrium to host The Consumer Circle in Gurugram
Cashfree and Consumer Collective by Atrium are bringing together a select group of founders, operators, and investors in Gurugram on September 20 for The Consumer Circle, a closed-door discussion created to put hard-earned experience, real business challenges, and practical lessons on the table.
Indian consumers are no longer following a predictable path to purchase. A shopper can compare three products on price in the morning, discover a founder-led brand on Instagram in the afternoon, and pay a premium for it that evening because the brand feels relevant to them.
Discovery may happen through a reel, validation through a WhatsApp group, and purchase through quick commerce. The decision to buy again could then come down to something as simple as how quickly a refund reaches the customer.
For consumer brands, that means the product is only part of the equation. Understanding why consumers buy, what they value, and what makes them return has become a more complicated part of building a business.
That is the conversation Cashfree and Consumer Collective by Atrium want to bring into the room through The Consumer Circle, a full-day, invite-only gathering in Gurugram on September 20. The event will bring together founders, operators, and investors building and backing consumer brands in India for four sessions focused on the questions shaping the next phase of D2C growth.
When useful conversations happen behind closed doors
The consumer industry has no shortage of public conversations about growth. But some of the most useful lessons tend to be shared privately.
Founders may talk publicly about GMV, launches, and fundraising. But the conversations between peers can look very different. They are about what remains after discounts, returns, shipping, and marketing; what a new channel actually costs once platform economics and advertising are included; what happens to conversion when discounts stop, and how to find investors who can contribute more than capital.
The Consumer Circle is built around creating a setting where those conversations can happen. Nothing said inside the sessions will be attributed outside the room, allowing participants to discuss the decisions, challenges, and numbers behind their businesses more openly.
The consumer is changing faster than the playbook
The need for these conversations comes as consumer behavior itself changes. Deloitte India’s January 2026 fashion report found that additional consumer spending is going toward upgrading essentials and improving quality rather than simply increasing the number of products purchased. For consumer brands, that makes understanding perceived value critical.
Premiumization is also spreading beyond India’s largest cities, with Tier II and Tier III consumers becoming meaningful contributors to premium demand. This is changing how brands think about assortment, pricing, and communication. Meanwhile, Gen Z is bringing different expectations around culture, identity, and inclusion. A brand increasingly needs to mean something to its customer beyond the product inside the box.
For founders, the challenge is to understand these shifts while continuing to build a business that can scale.
Four sessions on building what comes next
The Consumer Circle will explore these questions across four sessions, beginning with breakfast and continuing through lunch before closing with hi-tea and networking at 3:30 pm.
D2C Veterans will look at the journey from idea to growth to scale, including the decisions and challenges that emerge at each stage.
AI Unlock for D2C will focus on where AI is creating a genuine advantage for consumer teams and where it is simply adding another layer of noise. The session will look at what teams are using and shipping, with industry experts joining the conversation.
The Growth Playbook will examine the strategies, shifts, and lessons behind high-speed growth and what consumer brands need to rethink as the market becomes more competitive.
Fundraising Maze will take a different approach to the traditional investor panel. Investors from Consumer Collective by Atrium, Fireside Ventures, Hyperscale Ventures, and Recur Club will lead rapid-fire breakout groups on what they are looking for in consumer businesses and the early signals that can make a brand stand out.
Bringing consumer experience into the room
The gathering will include Hitaysh Dhingraa, Co-founder and CEO, Puresta | The Man Company; Mohit Sadaani, Angel Investor and Co-founder, The Moms Co; Gaurav Khatri, Co-Founder and CEO, Noise; Niharika Joshi, Co-founder and CMO, Cumin Co; Bharanidharan Viswanathan, Co-founder and CEO, The Crux; and Aakriti Rawal, Founder, House of Chikankaari, alongside more founders and operators from the consumer ecosystem.
The problems behind the numbers
For Cashfree, the conversations also reflect challenges it sees while working with consumer and D2C businesses. A brand can spend heavily to acquire a customer and still lose that customer at checkout through payment failures, retries, or a cumbersome payment experience. Sale and festive periods create another challenge, with sudden traffic spikes exposing problems that may not appear during an ordinary week.
Moving customers from cash on delivery to prepaid payments can affect working capital and return-to-origin costs. Refund speed can also influence whether a customer chooses to buy from the brand again.
“Working closely with consumer brands, we’ve been seeing that it is harder to create differentiation and ensure scale. As consumer behavior continues to shift, change, and evolve, it's important to understand little nuances that bridge the gap between a casual consumer and a brand loyalist,” said Akash Sinha, Co-Founder and CEO, Cashfree.
“Over the last decade, we have been up close with merchants, understanding their key pain points and creating avenues to help them rise. This is one such avenue, and we are looking forward to meeting many bright folks shaping the next era of the D2C ecosystem,” he added.
Cashfree has served more than 1 million businesses since its inception, including D2C brands, giving the company a view into the payment and operational challenges businesses face as they scale.
Consumer Collective by Atrium comes to the conversation from the operating side. Founded in 2025 by Atrium VC along with 40+ founders and operators, including founders from The Man Company, Noise, Wakefit, and mCaffeine, the Collective backs consumer founders at the -1 to 1 stage.
“Consumer Collective by Atrium was built on a simple belief: founders shouldn’t have to learn every lesson the hard way,” said Nikita Dhingra, Founding Partner, Consumer Collective by Atrium. “The people who have built and scaled consumer brands carry years of hard-earned operating experience, from hiring and distribution to product and growth. Consumer Circle is an extension of that philosophy, bringing this lived experience to a much broader community of founders and helping the ecosystem learn from those who have built before them.”
For both organizations, the reason to convene the Circle is the same: the ecosystem compounds when the people building in it are willing to say the specifics out loud. The value on offer is access, while tactical sales conversations stay outside the sessions.
Making experience more accessible
The Consumer Circle is ultimately about giving founders access to experience that they may otherwise spend years acquiring themselves. A founder could arrive with a question about margins, distribution, growth, or fundraising and leave with a perspective from someone who has dealt with the same problem. An investor can hear what founders are working through before those lessons become polished into a pitch deck.
The value of a small room is that the conversation can continue beyond the day itself. Entry is invite-only and subject to review, with Sign Up Link available for those interested in attending.

articles.title: Acheter une voiture électrique d’occasion devient moins stressant avec cette petite révolution pourtant toute simple
articles.text:
Avec la montée des prix des carburants et l’augmentation du parc de véhicules électriques en France, le marché de l’occasion pour ces voitures a le vent en poupe. De plus en plus de Français optent pour une voiture électrique d’occasion, un geste en faveur du climat, mais aussi de leur pouvoir d’achat. Toutefois, acheter une voiture d’occasion comporte des risques. Plusieurs professionnels ont donc signé un accord pour davantage de transparence, en affichant l’état de santé de la batterie de leurs voitures électriques vendues d’occasion.
Une donnée essentielle lors de l’achat
L’état de santé de la batterie d’une voiture électrique, aussi appelé SOH, pour « State of Health », est l’une des données les plus importantes. En effet, elle permet de mesurer le vieillissement de la batterie : un score de 80 % signifie que la batterie a perdu 20 % de sa capacité totale. Ce qui joue directement sur l’autonomie.
Et quand on sait qu’une batterie de voiture électrique peut rapidement coûter plus de 10 000 euros à remplacer, mieux vaut connaître cette donnée quand on achète une voiture électrique d’occasion.
Votre production solaire dépasse votre consommation ? Le SolarFlow 2400 AC+ stocke automatiquement votre surplus dans vos batteries. 100 % compatible avec la grande majorité des installations solaires en toiture, il permet de faire évoluer votre système simplement et à moindre coût.
Toutefois, rares sont les vendeurs à afficher clairement cette donnée. L’achat d’une voiture électrique d’occasion reste un véritable loto, dans lequel les acheteurs espèrent faire la meilleure affaire avec une batterie la moins dégradée possible.
Il existe plusieurs moyens de réaliser ce test, avec un boîtier OBD, en passant en concession ou parfois soi-même, avec l’application du constructeur ou l’écran central du véhicule. En revanche, ce test peut être long, c’est un peu plus complexe que sur un iPhone donc. Sur une Tesla, il peut demander toute une nuit d’analyse, ce qui rend difficile sa réalisation avec le vendeur d’une voiture d’occasion.
Plusieurs enseignes optent pour la transparence
C’est dans un post LinkedIn de Monique Barbut, ministre de la Transition écologique, que l’on apprend que plusieurs acteurs de la filière automobile ont signé un accord visant à rendre transparent le niveau de SOH d’une voiture électrique d’occasion.
Parmi les signataires de cet accord, on retrouve Aramis Auto, mais aussi Renault et Stellantis, ainsi que la CSIAM, la PFA (Plateforme Automobile) ou encore Mobilians. Ce qui donne du poids à cette décision.
Les voitures électriques d’occasion vendues par Stellantis, Renault ou Aramis Auto afficheront donc clairement, sur l’annonce, l’état de santé de la batterie. Une donnée qui devrait rassurer les acheteurs.
Cet affichage tombe à point nommé : depuis le 1er septembre 2026, une nouvelle aide financée par les fournisseurs d’énergie (via les certificats d’économies d’énergie) accorde jusqu’à 400 euros pour l’achat ou la location d’une électrique d’occasion immatriculée entre 2017 et 2023. Encore faut-il que la batterie affiche un SOH d’au moins 80 %. Sans accès à cette donnée, impossible de prouver qu’on y a droit.
En revanche, on ne sait pas s’il s’agit d’une véritable obligation demandée par le ministère. La liste exhaustive des vendeurs signataires de cet accord tend à nous laisser penser que les autres vendeurs n’auront, pour l’instant, aucune obligation d’afficher le niveau de santé de la batterie.
Toutefois, l’Union européenne prévoit d’instaurer un passeport batterie à partir du 18 février 2027. Il s’agit d’un QR code ou d’un format accessible numériquement permettant d’avoir accès à toutes les informations concernant la batterie du véhicule, y compris le SOH. Ce passeport batterie doit arriver sur les voitures neuves, puis progressivement sur le marché de l’occasion.

articles.title: Nigeria’s GDP growth is creating output, not enough jobs
articles.text:
This is Follow the Money, our weekly series that unpacks the earnings, business, and scaling strategies of African fintechs, financial institutions, companies, and governments. A new edition drops every Monday.
Nigeria’s economy is growing faster than it has since the second quarter of 2021. But beyond the headline growth rate, Nigeria’s economy is not growing evenly.
A growing share of economic expansion is coming from telecommunications and the service sector, while some of the sectors that employ the most Nigerians are growing much more slowly.
This helps explain why stronger gross domestic product (GDP) growth has not necessarily translated into better living standards for many Nigerians. An economy can produce more without creating enough employment to materially improve living standards. About 139 million Nigerians still live below the national poverty line, the World Bank said in July.
Nigeria’s gross domestic product grew by 4.43% in real terms in the second quarter of 2026, up from 4.23% a year earlier. Real GDP strips out the effect of rising prices. In an economy experiencing high inflation, nominal output can increase simply because goods and services cost more. Real GDP growth is therefore a better measure of whether the economy is actually producing more.
GDP measures the total value of economic activity in a country, making its growth rate a useful indicator of whether the economy is expanding or contracting. But the headline number does not tell where that expansion is happening, how broad it is, or whether the sectors employing the most people are growing quickly enough to change household incomes.
A 5-Year High for Nigeria’s GDP
Nigeria’s economy grew 4.43% in Q2 2026—the fastest quarterly growth rate since Q2 2021. Tap across the timeline to see the five-year trajectory.
Nigeria’s growth slowed sharply after the 2021 post-pandemic recovery, spending much of 2023–2024 trapped in the 2–3% range. The steady acceleration throughout 2025 and into Q2 2026 marks a meaningful aggregate improvement.
The economy is growing, but not everything is growing equally
Nigeria’s services sector, which accounted for 56.62% of GDP, grew by 4.60% in Q2. The industry sector grew by 3.96%, down from 7.46% a year earlier, while agriculture grew by 4.39%.
Telecommunications and information grew by 10.38% in Q2, more than twice the pace of overall GDP growth. Trade grew by 2.40%. Manufacturing grew by 3.24%, while real estate grew by 3.76%.
Agriculture, which remains one of the country’s largest sources of employment, grew by 4.39%.
What Is Holding Nigeria’s Growth Back?
Nigeria’s economy grew 4.43% in Q2 2026. But some of its biggest sectors are still constrained by problems that growth alone cannot solve. Pick a sector to see what’s holding it back.
WHAT’S HOLDING IT BACK?
THE RESULT
THE BIGGER PROBLEM
Nigeria can digitise parts of its economy. It cannot digitise away the infrastructure needed to grow the sectors that produce food, goods and mass employment. Telecoms can expand digitally. Agriculture, manufacturing and trade still depend heavily on physical infrastructure.
Growth in agriculture has picked up, supported by government efforts to promote mechanisation and dry-season farming, as well as improved weather conditions in parts of the north-west, north-east and south-west, according to the World Bank.
But the sector continues to face structural constraints that limit how much it can expand. Conflict and insecurity disrupt production in key regions. Farmers also face limited access to quality seeds and fertilisers, climate risks such as flooding, high costs of imported inputs and machinery, limited access to finance, and poor logistics infrastructure.
Across most non-oil sectors, including manufacturing, inadequate infrastructure—particularly electricity, transportation and logistics—limited access to credit, high input costs and shortages of skilled labour continue to constrain growth, according to the World Bank.
Telecoms is becoming an increasingly important engine
Nigeria’s economy was worth ₦121.26 trillion ($91.78 billion) in Q2 2026.
Telecommunications and information services contributed ₦12.04 trillion ($9.11 billion) to that output. Only trade, at ₦27.38 trillion ($20.72 billion), and crop production, at ₦14.37 trillion ($10.88 billion), contributed more among the activities reported by the NBS.
Telecoms is now the third-largest contributor to the economy as the demand for connectivity in the country continues to grow.
MTN Nigeria, the country’s largest telecom operator by subscriber count, reported that average data usage per subscriber increased by 15.2% in the first half of 2026, while total data traffic rose by 25.8%. Smartphone penetration reached 66.4%. The company’s service revenue increased by 25.9% to ₦2.99 trillion ($2.26 billion) in the first half of 2026.
Across the country, data consumption grew 46.75% year-on-year in June 2026. With broadband penetration still below 60%, there is still room for the sector to expand further as it moves toward 100%.
Telecoms can therefore continue to add economic output as more Nigerians come online, businesses become more dependent on digital infrastructure, and existing users consume more data. That growth can also create opportunities for indirect job creation across the wider digital economy. But its impact on direct employment is likely to remain limited because many jobs in this industry require specialised skills, while the number of available roles tends to narrow as the industry becomes more efficient and technology-driven.
The problem is jobs
Telecoms can generate enormous economic value without employing as many people as agriculture, trade, manufacturing, or construction. As industries become more productive, they can generate more output without increasing their workforce at the same pace.
Between 2001 and 2010, Nigeria ranked among the world’s 15 fastest-growing economies, averaging 8.2% annual growth, according to the World Bank. Sectoral reforms in banking and telecoms also unlocked private sector development.
GDP per capita almost quadrupled during that period, from $568 in 2001 to $2,280 in 2010.
But the growth failed to produce significant job creation.
“The expansion of good quality non-farm jobs—a feature that characterised East Asia’s growth in the 1980s and 1990s—was absent in Nigeria,” the World Bank said. “Meanwhile, industries in the formal sector, such as financial services and hospitality, were either not very employment-intensive, or have added labor from a very low base, hence failing to make a significant difference in wage employment growth.”
Companies, especially those in the service sector, can become more valuable without becoming proportionately more labour-intensive.
For instance, the United Bank for Africa Plc (UBA) had 12,770 employees in 2015 and spent ₦57.45 billion ($43.48 million) on employee benefits. By 2025, its workforce had fallen to 10,821, while employee benefit expenses had risen to ₦123.49 billion ($91.68 million).
Between 2020 and 2025, MTN Nigeria’s direct employee count increased by 8.51% to 2,001.
Since 2001, the telecoms industry has created more than 500,000 direct jobs, as of 2025, while also creating an extensive ecosystem of indirect employment and economic activity. The telecom sector’s contribution to GDP, directly and indirectly, was estimated at ₦33 trillion ($24.98 billion) in 2023.
But 500,000 direct jobs is still small relative to the size of Nigeria’s labour force.
In 2023, agriculture alone employed more than 25 million people in farming, forestry and fishing activities, accounting for 30.1% of total employment, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).
Nigeria Is Growing. But Where Are the Jobs?
Nigeria’s economy grew 4.43% in Q2 2026. But growth is not reaching workers evenly. Compare four major sectors to see why GDP growth does not always translate into broad-based job creation.
Telecoms is growing much faster than the economy—but it does not need millions of workers to do it.
DIRECT EMPLOYMENT
THE GAP
Telecoms is one of the fastest-growing parts of Nigeria’s economy. But because the sector is capital- and technology-intensive, more output does not require proportionately more workers. It can lift GDP without becoming a mass employer.
THE BIGGER PROBLEM
Nigeria needs growth that does more than increase GDP. It needs growth that can absorb the millions of people entering the labour market.
Yet agriculture’s growth rate is less than half the telecoms’ growth rate. Manufacturing, another major source of employment and productive capacity, generated ₦9.38 trillion ($7.09 billion) in real output across its 13 subsectors.
The sectors producing some of the fastest growth are not necessarily the sectors capable of translating that growth into enough jobs and higher household incomes.
Telecoms will keep growing as Nigerians consume more data, and more economic activity moves online. But telecoms cannot carry the entire economy indefinitely.
Nigeria’s next phase of economic expansion needs manufacturing to expand, agriculture to become more productive, and construction to boom. These sectors not only add to GDP when they grow, but create productive jobs at a scale that services such as telecoms cannot.
The World Bank expects Nigeria to average real GDP growth of 4.2% between 2026 and 2028. However, infrastructure gaps, security challenges, and weak agricultural productivity are likely to constrain diversification and job creation, limiting gains in per capita incomes despite steady aggregate growth.
For now, the numbers show that Nigeria’s economy is growing, but it is not yet broad or deep enough to translate into real income growth for the average Nigerian.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks.

 À 599 €, le Galaxy S25 Edge perd plus de la moitié de son prix
Pendant les French Days, Fnac/Darty propose le Galaxy S25 Edge à 599 €. Il retrouve ainsi son tarif le plus bas depuis sa sortie et devient même moins cher que le Galaxy S26 FE, pourtant présenté comme une porte d'entrée plus abordable vers le haut de gamme Samsung et affiché à 799 €.
Cette baisse change sérieusement son rapport qualité-prix. Avec seulement 5,8 mm d'épaisseur et 163 g sur la balance, le S25 Edge se fait presque oublier en main, là où de nombreux smartphones premium franchissent désormais les 200 g.
Sa finesse ne l'empêche pas d'accueillir un grand écran Dynamic Amoled 2X LTPO de 6,7 pouces. Lumineux et confortable, celui-ci affiche une définition QHD+ de 3120 x 1440 pixels et peut monter jusqu'à 120 Hz pour rendre les animations et le défilement particulièrement fluides.
Un vrai smartphone premium malgré quelques concessions
Samsung n'a pas bridé les performances. La puce Snapdragon 8 Elite de Qualcomm associée à 12 Go de mémoire vive permet de lancer sans difficulté les apps les plus exigeantes. Cette puissance peut toutefois entraîner une certaine chauffe lorsque l'appareil est fortement sollicité.
La batterie de 3900 mAh pouvait également inquiéter sur un terminal aussi mince. Elle a pourtant dépassé les 19 heures d'autonomie lors des tests d'endurance réalisés par la rédaction des Numériques. La puissance de charge est cependant moins impressionnante puisque Samsung la limite à 25 W.
Côté photo, le S25 Edge mise sur un module principal de 200 mégapixels, capable de produire d'excellents clichés, complété par un ultra grand-angle de 12 Mpx. Une caméra selfie de 12 Mpx complète l'ensemble. Cette configuration demeure moins polyvalente que certains concurrents, notamment faute de téléobjectif.
À 599 €, ces défauts deviennent toutefois bien plus faciles à accepter. Il existe encore des alternatives moins coûteuses, comme le Pixel 10a proposé à moins de 490 €, mais le Galaxy S25 Edge offre désormais une combinaison assez rare entre grand écran, puissance haut de gamme et poids plume. Une formule qui avait du mal à convaincre à 1249 €, mais qui devient autrement plus intéressante avec plus de 600 € de remise.

articles.title: CXMT Officially Starts Mass Production of LPDDR6 Memory
articles.text:
Monday, September 7th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
CXMT Officially Starts Mass Production of LPDDR6 Memory
CXMT has achieved the remarkable feat of officially beginning high-volume manufacturing of LPDDR6 memory. This positions CXMT's LPDDR6 memory modules as some of the first in the industry, with South Korean memory makers on a similar timeline for volume production of this next-generation technology. Reportedly, Xiaomi is the first customer for CXMT's domestic LPDDR6 memory, set to feature in the upcoming Xiaomi 18 Fold smartphone. Since the Xiaomi 18 Fold is scheduled to launch in September, CXMT's LPDDR6 memory will need to be delivered before the end of the month, indicating that customer shipments are already underway. This news follows recent reports that CXMT is conducting risk production of LPDDR6, suggesting a very high yield in production.
CXMT's LPDDR6 memory will operate at speeds of up to 12.8 Gbps, with the base speed of LPDDR6 being 10.7 Gbps. LPDDR6 builds on where LPDDR5X left off, which could reach speeds of up to 10.7 Gbps when highly overclocked. However, the new standard aims for significantly higher speeds, with the first generation of LPDDR6 from CXMT's fabs reaching 12.8 Gbps. Additionally, CXMT is producing these chips with a 16 Gb capacity, equivalent to 2 GB, and the memory IC is housed in a package-on-package (POP) casing, featuring about 1,295 pins in a ball grid array.Update, 14:55 UTC, September 7th : CXMT's official website confirmed mass production, with Alibaba Cloud, ByteDance, Tencent, Lenovo, Transsion, Honor, Vivo, and Oppo as customers.
We also learned that SK hynix is close to mass production. The South Korean memory giant announced earlier that its LPDDR6 memory modules would feature a 16 Gb capacity on the sixth-generation 10 nm node, known as 1c, running at up to 14.4 Gbps. Although these SK hynix modules might operate faster, all these speeds fall within JEDEC's official specification for the LPDDR6 standard. We can expect even faster memory chips as technology and manufacturing capabilities continue to advance.
		
		Source:
				Ice Universe

We also learned that SK hynix is close to mass production. The South Korean memory giant announced earlier that its LPDDR6 memory modules would feature a 16 Gb capacity on the sixth-generation 10 nm node, known as 1c, running at up to 14.4 Gbps. Although these SK hynix modules might operate faster, all these speeds fall within JEDEC's official specification for the LPDDR6 standard. We can expect even faster memory chips as technology and manufacturing capabilities continue to advance.
10 Comments on CXMT Officially Starts Mass Production of LPDDR6 Memory

articles.title: Java News Roundup: TornadoVM 6, JReleaser, LangChain4j, Java Operator SDK, JHipster, Yupiik Fusion
articles.text:
This week's Java roundup for August 31st, 2026, features news highlighting: the GA release of TornadoVM 6.0; point releases of JReleaser, LangChain4j, Java Operator SDK, JHipster, Kotlin Toolchain and Yupiik Fusion; and maintenance releases of Micronaut and GraalVM Development Kit.
JDK 27
Build 35 remains the current build in the JDK 27 early-access builds. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JDK 28
Build 14 of the JDK 28 early-access builds was also made available this past week featuring updates from Build 13 that include fixes for various issues. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
For JDK 28 and JDK 27, developers are encouraged to report bugs via the Java Bug Database.
TornadoVM
The release of TornadoVM 6.0.0 delivers bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: a full replacement of the Java Native Interface with the more modern Foreign Function & Memory API used in the backends and library tasks; the removal of the experimental JVM Compiler Interface (JVMCI) in favor of "sourcing all compiler metadata through a reflection + ASM + Unsafe layer, and makes that the single, uniform path on every supported JDK (21, 25, 26, 27);" and an expansion of the CUDA Backend. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes. InfoQ will follow up with a more detailed news story.
Micronaut
The Micronaut Foundation has released version 5.1.3 of the Micronaut Framework, based on Micronaut Core 5.1.13, featuring patch updates to modules: Micronaut SQL Libraries; Micronaut Micrometer; Micronaut OpenAPI/Swagger; Micronaut OpenSearch; Micronaut Email; Micronaut Reactor; Micronaut Data; and Micronaut AWS. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
GraalVM Development Kit
Oracle Labs has released version 5.1.3 of the Graal Development Kit (GDK) featuring alignment with the aforementioned Micronaut 5.1.3. This new release features the ability to generate and build GDK apps with JDK 25 when creating apps using the GDK Launcher and GDK CLI. Formerly known as Graal Cloud Native, the Graal Development Kit for Micronaut provides a curated set of Micronaut framework modules that simplify cloud application development. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JReleaser
The release of JReleaser 1.26.0 ships with bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: improved support of Snapcraft with the addition of the platforms node in the generated snapcraft.yml file and a deprecation of the runOn() method, defined in the SnapPackager class, in favor of the buildFor() method; and a new option to skip tagging the JBang packager repository to resolve the potential for incorrect JBang tags. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
LangChain4j
The formal release (along with the thirtieth beta release) of LangChain4j 1.20.0 provides bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: experimental support for non-blocking and reactive, for AI service methods that call a thread for an entire interaction, that now return a CompletableFuture<T> and Flow.Publisher<T>; and opt-in support for JSON SPIs against Jackson 3. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Java Operator SDK
The release of Java Operator SDK 5.6.0 delivers notable changes such as: a new InformerPool interface where informers are now shared between controllers and event sources instead of one informer per event source; and a change in configuration of the EventRecorder interface from the RegisteredController interface to the eventRecorder() method defined in the ConfigurationService interface. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JHipster
The release of JHipster 9.3.0 ships with bug fixes, dependency upgrades and new features such as: full support for Spring Boot 4, Jackson 3 and Angular 22; reactive applications that are now built with Vite; and consistent use of the Spring Boot @ServiceConnection annotation on integration tests using Testcontainers. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Kotlin Toolchain
The JetBrains team has released version 0.12.0 of Kotlin Toolchain, a unified entry point utility into the Kotlin programming language. Along with bug fixes and dependency upgrades, new features include: expansion of published Kotlin libraries, originally limited to JVM libraries, that now include multiplatform libraries; the ability to execute Wasm apps using the kotlin run command; and improvements to the Terminal UI and IDE. More details on this release, including breaking changes, may be found in the release notes.
Yupiik Fusion
Version 1.1.0 of Yupiik Fusion, the lightweight Java stack for building microservices and APIs, provides bug fixes, dependency upgrades and new features such as: a new JsonSchemaService class that implements the Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema specification; a new CurlLoggerListener class designed to force all exchanges to be logged; and the addition of a snapshot deployment workflow. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.

articles.title: CEE’s biggest checks: 10 standout startup raises of 2026 | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Europe’s startup ecosystem continues to produce ambitious companies tackling some of the biggest challenges across defence, artificial intelligence, robotics, biotechnology, and digital infrastructure.
As preparations are well under way and tickets selling for the inaugural MeOut Summit, taking place in Budapest on 25–26 November 2026, attention is turning once again to the founders and startups shaping Europe’s next wave of growth.
The event will bring together more than 1,000 founders, investors, corporates, and ecosystem builders for two days of networking, discussions, and collaboration.
Against this backdrop, we focus in on 10 standout funding rounds raised by companies based in central and eastern Europe. From defence technology and AI infrastructure to robotics and health innovation, these companies highlight the breadth of talent and ambition driving Europe’s startup landscape forward.
Frankenburg Technologies
Founded in 2024 and headquartered in Tallinn, Estonia, Frankenburg Technologies is a DefenceTech company developing missile defence and rapid response systems. The company focuses on radar, sensor fusion, tracking, and guidance technologies designed to detect and intercept incoming threats.
In February 2026, Frankenburg Technologies raised €30 million in Series A funding. The round brought the company’s total funding to approximately €35.5 million as it continues developing advanced defence capabilities for contested environments.
Saltz
Launched in 2022 in Vilnius, Lithuania, Saltz is building a consumer platform that connects customers directly with farms, fishing boats, and regional suppliers to source premium seafood and meat.
The company secured €20 million in Series A funding in March 2026. The investment is supporting Saltz’s expansion of its direct-to-consumer food marketplace and supplier network.
ABZ Innovation
Based in Szentendre, Hungary, ABZ Innovation was founded in 2021 and specialises in drones and drone-related technologies, combining engineering expertise with industrial applications.
The company raised €7 million in venture funding in January 2026. The funding is helping ABZ Innovation accelerate the development and production of its drone platforms and related accessories.
BottleCap AI
Founded in 2025 and operating from Prague, Czechia, BottleCap AI is an artificial intelligence startup developing efficient large language models designed to improve reasoning performance while reducing computational requirements.
The company raised €6.38 million Seed funding in January 2026 to advance its architecture-first approach to AI model development.
Allonic
Founded in 2025 and based in Budapest, Allonic is a robotics hardware startup developing a new manufacturing platform for producing safe, dexterous, and assembly-free robotic bodies. The company is building technology around 3D Tissue Braiding to simplify robotic manufacturing.
Allonic secured €6 million pre-Seed funding in February 2026 to further develop its robotics manufacturing platform.
Copla
Established in 2023 and headquartered in Vilnius, Lithuania, Copla provides cybersecurity-as-a-service solutions designed to help businesses protect their data, assets, and digital infrastructure.
The company raised €6 million in Series A funding in February 2026. The investment will support the growth of its cybersecurity platform and services for enterprises and technology organisations.
Axiology
Founded in 2023 in Vilnius, Lithuania, Axiology is developing regulated distributed ledger technology infrastructure for tokenised securities, covering issuance, trading, custody, and settlement.
The company raised €5 million in Seed funding in February 2026 to expand its digital securities infrastructure and support adoption of blockchain-based financial services.
Rainbow Weather
Founded in 2021 and based in Warsaw, Rainbow Weather uses artificial intelligence to deliver faster and more accurate weather forecasting through its mobile applications.
The company raised €4.68 million in Seed funding in January 2026 to continue developing AI-powered forecasting technology and expanding its weather intelligence platform.
Pioneera Biosciences
Founded in 2024 and headquartered in Vilnius, Lithuania, Pioneera Biosciences is a biotechnology company developing immune orchestration platforms aimed at improving access to next-generation cell and gene therapies.
The company secured €4.5 million in Seed funding in February 2026 to advance its biotechnology platform and develop more accessible therapeutic solutions.
Rollo Robotics
Founded in 2025 in Tallinn, Estonia, Rollo Robotics develops autonomous monowheel security robots using gyroscopic stabilisation technology for security and monitoring applications.
The company raised €3.7 million in pre-Seed funding in January 2026, supporting the continued development of its autonomous robotics systems.
In summary
From missile defence systems and AI models to robotics platforms and next-generation biotechnology, these 10 startups demonstrate the diversity of Europe’s emerging innovation landscape.
While funding sizes vary, each company reflects a broader trend: investors are increasingly backing deep technology, specialised infrastructure, and solutions designed to address complex global challenges.
Ready to join us? Secure your ticket to the MeOut Summit 2026 today!

articles.title: The Download: the hunt for underground hydrogen and more rogue OpenAI agents
articles.text:
The Download: the hunt for underground hydrogen and more rogue OpenAI agents
Plus: OpenAI agents hijacked a German website before the Hugging Face hack.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
How much hydrogen awaits us underground?
A flurry of exploration efforts is searching for underground stores of hydrogen gas, which could provide a valuable source of zero-carbon fuel.
The hunt has spread all over the world and engaged dozens of startups, including the Bill Gates–backed Koloma, which has been poking around the US Midwest to reach ancient oceanic rocks associated with hydrogen production. But the search so far has come up short.
No one has yet reported finding a commercially viable reservoir of the gas, and public data on what has been found remains in short supply. Yet researchers estimate that trillions of tons of H₂ are produced within Earth’s crust. If a small fraction could be recovered, it could meet global hydrogen demand for centuries.
Follow the global race to find hydrogen underground.
—James Dinneen
This story is from our latest print magazine, which is all about kids. Subscribe now to receive every issue when it lands.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 OpenAI agents hijacked a German website before the Hugging Face hack
The agents turned DseWiki into their own bulletin board. (Reuters $)
+ They shared tips on avoiding detection and made over 15,000 edits. (BBC)
+ OpenAI’s safety issues suggest it has a company culture problem. (MIT Technology Review)
2 The US military has disabled ad trackers due to Middle East targeting fears
Commercial location data has reportedly been used to target troops. (Reuters $) 
+ It can be sold by data brokers and used to track personnel. (Gizmodo)
+ The military is increasing restrictions on phone use overall. (Guardian)
3 A company claims its AI-designed drug can reverse aging markers
Patients’ average biological age fell by as much as six years in a clinical trial. (NYT $)
+ Insilico Medicine developed the drug, called rentosertib. (Bloomberg $)
+ Who gets the credit for AI-designed drugs? (MIT Technology Review)
4 Elon Musk’s xAI has lost its bid to block an AI-nudification ban
The Minnesota law aims to curb nonconsensual sexual images and CSAM. (Politico)
+ xAI argues the measure restricts free speech. (Reuters $)
+ Deepfakes are being weaponized. (MIT Technology Review)
5 The US is investigating Tesla’s rollout of Cybercab robotaxis
Regulators are probing how Tesla self-certified the unusual vehicle. (TechCrunch)
+ The robotaxi lacks a steering wheel and pedals. (Politico)
+ But Tesla CEO Elon Musk is not known to wait for regulations. (Reuters $)
6 Europe has its first commercial orbital rocket
The Spectrum is the first rocket to reach orbit from mainland Europe. (Verge)
+ German startup Isar Aerospace launched it from Norway. (Guardian)
+ Here’s what else we’re putting in space. (MIT Technology Review)
7 Tumbler Ridge shooting survivors have filed 30 lawsuits against OpenAI
They say OpenAI should have alerted police before the attack.(NYT $)
8 JD Vance’s “satanic” AI warning has resonated with Christian Republicans
AI’s spiritual consequences are causing growing concern. (WSJ $)
9 Another mysteriously perfect geometric shape has appeared on Saturn
Scientists still don’t know why Saturn forms these strange shapes. (Wired $)
10 Fake ads for AI grandfathers and underwear are targeting "slop voice"
Comedians created the viral campaign in New York subways. (New Yorker $)
Quote of the day
"Typically, when the public shifts, politicians shift with them. Trump is not doing that on data centers.”
—Darrell M. West, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution's Center for Technology Innovation, tells NPR that Republican midterm candidates are at odds with President Trump over data centers.
One more thing
What is AI?
  Artificial intelligence is the hottest technology of our time. But what is it? It sounds like a stupid question, but it’s one that’s never been more urgent.
Here’s the short answer: AI is a catchall term for a set of technologies that make computers do things that are thought to require intelligence when done by people. But even that definition contains multitudes.
And that right there is the problem. What does it mean for machines to understand speech or write a sentence? What kinds of tasks could we ask such machines to do? And how much should we trust the machines to do them?
Here’s why we still can’t agree on what AI actually is—and the real-world consequences it’s creating.
—Will Douglas Heaven
We can still have nice things

Whilst looking for a “real teardown” of Flock cameras to see what vulnerabilities they had (like say LiPo batteries that could be induced to burn).
I came across two nuggets of information,
1, The cameras are rented not sold.
2, The cameras use the same LPDDR4 DRAM as needed for AI systems.
https://www.gadgetreview.com/flock-safety-cameras-are-making-the-global-memory-shortage-even-worse
So, with the rented cameras using ~2 GB of LPDDR4 memory that is already well over priced due to AI created shortages… It’s more than likely Flock will significantly “up the rental” in the near future.
Worse as quite a few municipalities are “pulling out” and interesting behaviour starting to happen with regards Federal Roads and funding with the “Flock-Off Act”.
It may be “lay-off” time approaching for Flock sales and technical staff.

articles.title: Gary Oldman lo confirma: el nuevo actor de James Bond ya está fichado y él tiene su favorito
articles.text:
El oscarizado sir Gary Oldman acaba de anunciar lo que millones de personas esperaban desde hace meses: James Bond ya tiene nuevo actor. Después del final de la saga de Daniel Craig con No Time to Die, la propiedad creativa de la saga pasó a manos de Amazon MGM Studios, que durante mucho tiempo ha empezado a desarrollar su propia manera de revitalizar la franquicia. Por lo pronto, ya se sabe que el director de este ansiado reinicio será Denis Villeneuve (Dune, Blade Runner 2049).
Pero ahora parece que estamos muy cerca de conocer al actor que se convertirá en el próximo James Bond. Y es que Gary Oldman ha afirmado en una entrevista concedida al programa canadiense The Morning Show que la compañía ya tiene tomada la decisión. "Lo sabremos muy pronto, ¿verdad? Porque ya lo han elegido. Ya han tomado una decisión, aunque aún no la han anunciado", desvela.
Aunque Amazon MGM ha permanecido en silencio acerca de todos los rumores que han circulado durante meses, esta vez la información viene de uno de los nombres más potentes e importantes de la industria. Por ello, parece que esta vez sí es cierto, el nuevo actor de James Bond ya está fichado. De hecho, Gary Oldman ha dejado claro quién es su favorito para hacerse con el papel.
"Se rumorea que Jack Lowden está entre los finalistas", sugiere. No es de extrañar que mencione su nombre, pues Gary Oldman lleva años compartiendo trabajo con Lowden, pues juntos protagonizan la aclamada serie de espías Slow Horses. Ahora, el veterano intérprete no esconde que quiere que su compañero pase a vestir el esmoquin del agente 007. "Cruzo los dedos por Jack", sentencia.
El nuevo actor de James Bond está al caer
Lo cierto es que las palabras de Gary Oldman sobre el próximo actor de James Bond coinciden con un fuerte rumor surgido la semana pasada. En él, se especulaba con que Amazon MGM había programado unas audiciones para principios de septiembre y, así, cerrar definitivamente el proceso.
Los finalistas, según ese rumor, eran Jacob Elordi (Euphoria, Frankenstein), Paul Mescal (Normal People, Gladiator II), Harris Dickinson (Triángulo de la tristeza, El clan de hierro), Jack Barton (Heartstopper, Los hombres del S.A.S.), Callum Turner (One Night Only, Animales Fantásticos) y el mencionado Jack Lowden. Es muy posible que en las próximas semanas se desvele la decisión final.

articles.title: Fone de ouvido para corrida: os 10 melhores modelos para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Fone de ouvido para corrida: os 10 melhores modelos para comprar em 2026
Selecionamos os melhores fones de ouvido para correr; encontre modelos para corrida ao ar livre ou em locais fechados, de marcas como JBL, Bose, Shokz e Anker
Os melhores fones de ouvido para corrida em 2026 oferecem certificação contra suor, chuva e poeira, além de inovações em ergonomia, de forma que o dispositivo não caia da orelha durante uma prova.
Neste guia, o Tecnoblog reuniu 10 modelos de marcas como JBL, Anker e Shokz, que vão desde os tradicionais intra-auriculares até formatos open-ear, como os de condução óssea. Veja as especificações e os pontos positivos e negativos de cada produto a seguir.
O JBL Endurance Peak 4 é um fone intra-auricular voltado para atividades esportivas, com ganchos que passam ao redor das orelhas e ajudam na fixação. O modelo pesa 10,5 g por lado e tem certificação IP68, que indica resistência à poeira e à água.
Para situações em que o usuário precisa continuar ouvindo o ambiente, há os modos Ambient Aware e TalkThru. Essa combinação permite alternar entre maior isolamento e maior percepção dos sons externos, algo que pode ser relevante conforme o local da corrida.
O sistema de áudio usa drivers de 10 mm e oferece cancelamento adaptativo de ruído. A autonomia é de 12 horas com o ANC desligado ou 8 horas com o recurso ativado, e o estojo soma até 48 horas. O Peak 4 traz Bluetooth 5.4, conexão multiponto e seis microfones para chamadas.
O Bose Ultra Open Earbuds tem uma construção aberta apoiada na lateral das orelhas. Ao contrário dos fones intra-auriculares com modo de transparência, o modelo não precisa processar os sons externos para que você os ouça, preservando a percepção do entorno durante a reprodução de música.
No entanto, esse formato traz algumas limitações: ele não oferece cancelamento de ruído ativo e tem certificação IPX4, voltada à resistência contra respingos apenas.
O modelo utiliza Bluetooth 5.3, suporta conexão multiponto com dois dispositivos e permite ajustes de equalização pelo aplicativo da Bose. Já a bateria chega a sete horas e meia de reprodução com o Immersive Audio desligado. Quando ativado, a autonomia cai para até cinco horas; o estojo acrescenta outras 19 horas e meia.
No Soundcore Sport X20, cada unidade pesa cerca de 6,6 g e o encaixe é formado por ponteiras intra-auriculares e ganchos ajustáveis que passam ao redor das orelhas.
A estrutura recebe certificação IP68 e a tecnologia SweatGuard, para proteger fones de ouvido contra a corrosão causada pelo suor, enquanto os drivers dinâmicos têm 11 mm.
O modelo também possui cancelamento ativo de ruído e seis microfones com processamento por IA para chamadas. Para uma corrida ao ar livre, é possível alternar entre o cancelamento e os recursos de audição do ambiente de acordo com a necessidade.
Entre as especificações, o Sport X20 traz Bluetooth 5.3, suporta conexão multiponto e tem autonomia de até 12 horas nos fones — 48 horas considerando o estojo.
O JBL Endurance Race 2 utiliza um estabilizador que se apoia na parte interna da orelha para manter os fones posicionados durante exercícios. O conjunto pesa 53,9 g considerando fones e estojo e vem com três tamanhos de ponteiras, além da presença de certificação IP68 para proteção contra suor, chuva e poeira.
Com drivers de 6,8 mm, o fone da JBL também traz os modos Ambient Aware e TalkThru que podem ser alternados via toque. O aplicativo da marca também oferece configurações específicas para atividades esportivas.
A bateria chega a 12 horas de reprodução com o ANC desligado e o estojo acrescenta outras 36 horas, totalizando até 48 horas de uso. Com o cancelamento ativado, a autonomia dos fones cai para até 7 horas.
O Shokz OpenMove usa condução óssea em vez de alto-falantes convencionais. As vibrações são transmitidas pela região próxima às têmporas, mantendo os ouvidos abertos. Assim, o som ambiente continua chegando ao usuário durante a reprodução, diferentemente dos fones intra-auriculares.
A estrutura pesa 29 g e utiliza uma haste que passa atrás da cabeça. A classificação IP55 indica resistência a poeira e respingos de água, incluindo situações de suor e chuva leve, mas não é uma proteção destinada à imersão.
Porém, sua autonomia é de até seis horas por carga, inferior à de vários modelos deste guia.
O JBL Endurance Zone é um fone esportivo de formato aberto. Em vez de vedar o canal auditivo, os drivers ficam próximos às orelhas e reproduzem o áudio enquanto os sons externos continuam sendo ouvidos.
Os drivers dinâmicos têm 18 x 11 mm, mas não há cancelamento ativo de ruído. A certificação IP68 indica proteção contra poeira e água, tendo bons resultados nos testes feitos pelo Tecnoblog, enquanto quatro microfones são usados para chamadas.
Em bateria, a JBL promete até 8 horas de reprodução, ou 32 horas somando com a case. Mas durante nossos testes, o componente teve desempenho acima do esperado: foram 10 horas de reprodução contínua de músicas no Spotify.
O AeroFit 2 também faz parte da categoria de fones open-ear e utiliza ganchos ajustáveis para posicionar os alto-falantes próximos ao ouvido. Assim, o usuário continua ouvindo os sons do ambiente enquanto escuta o conteúdo reproduzido.
Seus drivers medem 20 mm x 11,5 mm e têm formato oval, uma dimensão maior que a de muitos fones intra-auriculares, mas não oferece cancelamento de ruído ativo para bloquear o som ambiente. Ele suporta codec LDAC, Hi-Res, tem certificação IP55 para poeira e respingos e recursos de IA.
A bateria chega a dez horas por carga e 42 horas com o estojo. Dez minutos de carregamento acrescentam até quatro horas de reprodução, segundo a marca, e o estojo também aceita carregamento sem fio.
O HUAWEI FreeClip 2 utiliza um formato de clipe, preso à lateral da orelha por uma estrutura em C que permite ouvir os sons externos enquanto o áudio é reproduzido. Cada fone pesa aproximadamente 5,1 g, e os lados são intercambiáveis: o sistema identifica automaticamente se a unidade está na orelha esquerda ou direita.
Os fones têm certificação IP57 para água e poeira, o sistema acústico utiliza um driver duplo de 10,8 mm, enquanto o processamento de chamadas conta com três microfones. No entanto, não oferece cancelamento de ruído ativo.
Com suporte ao Bluetooth 6.0, é possível conectar dois dispositivos simultaneamente, tendo uma autonomia de até nove horas por carga e 38 horas com o estojo, de acordo com a Huawei.
O JBL Soundgear Clips também adota uma construção open-ear em formato de clipe, permitindo que o usuário continue ouvindo os sons do ambiente durante a reprodução. O modelo pesa 6,5 g por unidade e tem quatro microfones que integram o sistema de chamadas.
O Bluetooth 5.4 permite conexão multiponto, e o aplicativo JBL Headphones oferece seis predefinições de equalização, além de oferecer proteção IP54 contra respingos d’água e poeira.
Sua bateria oferece até oito horas de reprodução, enquanto o estojo aumenta a autonomia total para 32 horas. O carregamento completo leva duas horas e há suporte a recarga rápida. Como acontece com outros modelos de ouvido aberto, o Soundgear Clips não utiliza ANC.
O Mibro O1 também utiliza uma construção open-ear que mantém os ouvidos livres e prende os fones à região externa das orelhas. O fone inclui drivers dinâmicos de 15,4 mm e botões físicos para os comandos, mas não traz ANC durante a reprodução de músicas.
No entanto, o Mibro O1 oferece Cancelamento de Ruído Ambiente (ENC), recurso destinado a reduzir ruídos captados pelos microfones e melhorar a transmissão da voz. Sua classificação IPX6 indica resistência a jatos de água, enquanto o Bluetooth 5.3 é usado para a conexão sem fio, mas sem multiponto.
A autonomia chega a sete horas de reprodução nos fones e a aproximadamente 35 horas com o estojo.
A escolha depende principalmente do tipo de encaixe, da resistência à água e da necessidade de ouvir os sons ao redor. Vale observar:
Não há um formato que garanta o mesmo encaixe para todas as pessoas, pois o tamanho e o formato das orelhas variam. Para atividades com bastante movimento, modelos com ganchos, estabilizadores ou estruturas que envolvem a orelha costumam oferecer uma fixação mais firme.
Depende do ambiente e da preferência do corredor. Fones in-ear oferecem maior isolamento e podem ser mais adequados em locais onde o ruído externo não é prioridade.
Já os modelos open-ear e de condução óssea mantêm os ouvidos mais livres, facilitando a percepção do ambiente, mas deixam o áudio mais sujeito aos ruídos externos e costumam pecar em qualidade sonora.
O JBL Endurance Peak 4 reúne certificação IP68, ganchos ao redor da orelha, ANC adaptativo e até 12 horas de autonomia. O Soundcore Sport X20 é outra opção com IP68, ganchos ajustáveis e até 12 horas por carga, permitindo adaptar melhor o encaixe durante uma prova.
O Soundcore AeroFit 2 é uma excelente opção de fone em formato aberto, pois combina construção com ganchos ajustáveis, certificação IP55, até 10 horas de autonomia e suporte a codecs avançados, como LDAC e Hi-Res.
O Mibro O1 tem um bom custo-benefício, trazendo certificação IPX6 contra jatos d’água e até 35 horas de autonomia considerando o estojo. Para quem prefere um modelo intra-auricular, o Soundcore Sport X20 oferece IP68, ganchos ajustáveis e ANC, embora pertença a uma categoria de preço diferente.
O Modo Transparência usa os microfones do fone para captar sons externos e reproduzi-los junto ao áudio que está sendo ouvido. Dessa forma, é possível perceber conversas, trânsito e outros ruídos sem retirar os fones. Ele é diferente de um projeto open-ear, no qual os sons externos chegam naturalmente ao ouvido.

articles.title: GTA Vice City and GTA III return to web browsers after a DMCA takedown — Open-source reverse engineering brings the classics to the web with over 100 FPS performance
articles.text:
GTA Vice City and GTA III return to web browsers after a DMCA takedown — Open-source reverse engineering brings the classics to the web with over 100 FPS performance
The games are available across two platforms.
Grand Theft Auto: Vice City has cemented itself as one of the most legendary games of all time. It originally came out in 2002 on the PS2 before making its way to the Xbox and PC a year later. Fast forward to 2026, and now the game is entirely playable in a browser window. It was actually already playable last year on DOS Zone but was quickly shut down following a DMCA strike from Take-Two. However, a different website called "Quenq" has taken up the mantle now, and it also hosts GTA III there.
The project is still the same because it quite literally says DOS Zone in the pause menu. Anyhow, for a change of pace, we tried the game on a OnePlus 12; it loaded immediately and ran without any issues. Beyond keyboard/mouse and controller, the game is also compatible with touchscreen controls. We were able to seamlessly move around the world and control Tommy in both landscape and portrait orientations.
You get a save game and mod manager, allowing you to upload your own files right into the browser. You can type cheats using an external keyboard as well. There's an FPS limit option before the game begins because GTA Vice City was intended to run at 30 FPS, so playing it at unlocked framerates (which this port supports) can sometimes cause bugs and physics to break. We were able to easily play the game past 100 FPS on desktop, though.
The project likely uses reVC — a community project that decompiles the original source code of GTA: Vice City into clean, readable C++ code. Then, WebAssembly helps translate C++ code into JavaScript that the browser can natively understand. The port should be running on WebGL 2, a JavaScript API that bypasses your browser's typical layout engine and talks directly to your GPU to execute graphics-intensive tasks.
The same goes for GTA III — it's also available on Quenq, features the same controls and options (except for the mod manager), and is likely built using re3, which is the decompiled source code of GTA III. This project doesn't seem to be ripped off from DOS Zone, as there is no indication of such in the pause menu. It also runs just as well as the Vice City port, and we had no issues playing it across a bunch of devices.
Just out of curiosity, we checked DOS Zone and actually found both Vice City and GTA III listed there, but they require uploading the game assets. You can also just download the data through a torrent after you click a button, but the platform leaves that choice to you with clear disclaimers that they won't be responsible for piracy. It's clear that the DMCA takedown has shifted the way the platform distributes these projects, but it's still impressive that they're up, nonetheless.
