articles.title: ChatGPT can now connect to your personal apps to mimic writing style
articles.text:
OpenAI appears to be testing a new "Writing Style" feature for ChatGPT that can learn how you write by looking at examples from your connected apps.
The feature is currently available to a small group of users, and an onboarding screen says, "ChatGPT will write in your voice by referencing examples from your connected apps."
As shown in the screenshot, users can provide examples across three categories: Messaging, Documents, and Email.
OpenAI lists Slack under messaging, Google Drive and Notion for documents, and Gmail for email.
Once configured, ChatGPT could reference the way you naturally write across those services when drafting new content, rather than requiring you to repeatedly explain your preferred tone or paste examples into a conversation.
It sounds similar to Claude Styles, but goes further with connected apps
Anthropic previously offered a similar personalization feature called Styles, which let users upload or paste writing samples and then generate a custom style based on their communication patterns.
OpenAI's experiment appears to take a different approach by letting ChatGPT reference writing that already exists inside connected services.
That could give ChatGPT a much larger set of real examples, including how you write emails compared with messages or longer documents.
OpenAI has confirmed it's testing Writing Style, but we don't know when it'll roll out to users widely.

articles.title: Roborock says its focus is serving the user and not worrying about the competition - Tech Guide
articles.text:
In the highly competitive home robot market, Roborock – one of the leaders of the category – says it is not looking at the competition but only trying to find ways to serve their users even better.
At the IFA show in Berlin, we took a hands on look at the Roborock stand where it showcased its new RockAqua P1 robot pool cleaner, Saros Series robot vacuums and the RockNeo Q2 LiDAR robot lawn mowers.
When asked about the competition and what the company needs to do to stand out from all the other companies producing similar products, Roborock Product Marketing Lead Clarbi Lu says the company does not obsess about the competition they obsess about their users.
“Basically I would say we really focus on users so the competition itself is not our first priority,” Lu told Tech Guide.
“As long as you focus on users’ needs and users’ problems and you develop your functions and products in that direction and really provide a good user experience, the competition comes second.”
Lu says the company’s mission with its robot products is to give time back to its customers.
“It’s something that fulfils our mission to provide a hands-free and worry-free experience for our users for their daily maintenance, for their cleaning,” he said.
“We do the work so our users can take back their time, give the time back to their loved ones, to their hobbies, to themselves.”
What’s next for Roborock? What’s the one challenge it is trying to overcome to create the next generation of products?
“That is a good question. When we define a new product, if we would like to simply raise the suction power, we just need to increase the power of the motor,” he said.
“That’s simple but at the same time this will bring some problems.
“For example the duration of the battery will be sacrificed and the noise will come up. The difficult point is that we made a balance, we made trade-offs.
“We should find the point of really balancing different aspects and this is something like a puzzle.
“When we want to bring up a new technology, one or two additional problems may come up.
“For our R&D or pre-R&D we might be able to solve one or two additional problems one by one or year by year.
“When the time comes, we are ready to bring up new technologies.”
Tech Guide took a tour of Roborock booth at IFA.
ROBOROCK ROCKNEO Q2 LIDAR
This is a robot that can easily get around your yard and provide professional-level lawn care on spaces up to 800 square metres.
But one feature Roborock had that was different to its competitors was its charging stand which had both a solar panel to reduce the amount of power required to charge it as well as a built-in Wi-Fi extender.
This will connect to your home’s Wi-Fi and bring a stronger connection to the robot lawnmower. That’s one pain point with robot lawnmower users: their Wi-Fi doesn’t reach the yard where it’s needed.
The new Roborock charging stand solves that problem.
ROBOROCK ROCKAQUA P1
This is the first robot pool cleaner from Roborock. It has 680 GPH suction and can run for up to 3.5 hours.
On board is a monocular camera for obstacle avoidance and dynamic detection and when it’s finished running it parks itself on the water line for easy retrieval.
ROBOROCK SAROS 20 FLOW
On board is the SpiraFlow 2.0 self-cleaning mop that makes light work of messes.
The robot also deploys a cover over the roller to avoid wetting carpets.
They can also navigate double thresholds up to 8.8 cm high to get around your home and complete the clean.
It also has an ultra-slim profile so it can fit under sofas and beds as low as 7.95 cm.
ROBOROCK F25 ULTRA STEAM
The new Roborock wet/dry vacuum uses high-temperature steam and hot water to tackle those tough stubborn dried-on stains.
It can also clean right to the wall and edges with 0mm Triple Edge cleaning.

articles.title: French Days 2026 Fnac et Darty : les meilleures offres high-tech
articles.text:
Les French Days 2026 lancent leur nouvelle édition, du 7 au 14 septembre 2026, avec une promesse bien connue : profiter de prix réduits sur une large sélection de produits avant l’autre grand rendez-vous du Black Friday. Chez Fnac et Darty, l’opération a débuté sur les chapeaux de roue, avec de très nombreuses promotions sur l’informatique, les smartphones, les téléviseurs, ou encore l’audio. Notre objectif est de retenir les offres réellement intéressantes, en privilégiant à la fois la qualité des produits, leur prix actuel et leur intérêt par rapport à ce que l’on trouve habituellement sur le marché.
Les meilleurs produits high-tech pendant les French Days sur La Fnac et Darty
Vous l’aurez compris, vous trouverez dans cette sélection une liste des produits high-tech qui ont retenu notre attention pour cette nouvelle édition des French Days. Il est toutefois possible que certains produits victimes de leur succès ne soient plus disponibles lorsque vous lirez ces lignes.
PC portable Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3
Pour les French Days, le PC portable Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14″ normalement vendu 799,99 € est proposé au prix de 599,99 € sur La Fnac et Darty.
Le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 est un PC portable compact doté d’un écran Full HD de 14 pouces, d’un processeur AMD Ryzen 5, de 16 Go de mémoire vive et d’un SSD de 512 Go. Sans être une bête de course — oubliez les jeux vidéo –, il dispose d’une configuration confortable pour la bureautique, les études, le télétravail ou encore pour regarder du contenu. Léger avec ses 1,37 kg, il se montre également facile à transporter.
Enceinte sans fil Marshall Middleton
Normalement vendu 299,99 €, l’enceinte sans fil Marshall Middleton est au prix de 199,99 € sur La Fnac pour les French Days.
La Marshall Middleton est une enceinte Bluetooth portable qui combine le look rétro caractéristique de la marque avec une conception pensée pour l’extérieur. Côté audio, elle délivre un son riche et bien équilibré, avec des basses généreuses et suffisamment de clarté dans les médiums et les aigus pour profiter aussi bien de la musique que des podcasts. Robuste et résistante à l’eau et à la poussière grâce à sa certification IP67, elle offre jusqu’à 20 heures d’autonomie et délivre un son puissant grâce à sa conception stéréo.
Trottinette électrique Xiaomi Electric Scooter 6
La trottinette électrique Xiaomi Electric Scooter 6 est vendue au prix de 399,99 € sur La Fnac et Darty, au lieu de 429,99 € habituellement.
La Xiaomi Electric Scooter 6 est une trottinette électrique pensée pour les trajets urbains, avec une configuration particulièrement confortable. Elle embarque un moteur de 400 W, capable de grimper jusqu’à 800 W en puissance de pointe. Son principal atout est sa double suspension avant et arrière, qui absorbe mieux les vibrations et les irrégularités de la route. Avec sa vitesse maximale de 25 km/h, son frein à tambour à l’avant et son système E-ABS à l’arrière, et une autonomie annoncée de 45 km, c’est un deux-roues idéal pour les déplacements du quotidien.
TV LG 4K OLED Evo OLED65C6 65″
Le téléviseur LG OLED Evo OLED65C6 65″ est normalement vendu 2 499 €. Pendant les French Days, il est proposé au prix de 1 799,10 € avec la carte Fnac, et 1 999 € sans la carte.
Le LG OLED65C6 est un téléviseur 4K OLED Evo de 65 pouces qui mise sur une qualité d’image haut de gamme. Sa dalle OLED offre des noirs parfaits et un contraste optimisé, tandis que le processeur Alpha 11 AI Gen3 améliore le traitement et la mise à l’échelle des images. Compatible Dolby Vision et Dolby Atmos, avec quatre ports HDMI 2.1, il se montre autant à l’aise pour le cinéma que pour le jeu vidéo.
Smartphone Samsung Galaxy S25 Edge
Pendant les French Days, le smartphone Samsung Galaxy S25 Edge est au prix de 599 € sur La Fnac et Darty, au lieu de 1 251,98 €.
Le Samsung Galaxy S25 Edge mise avant tout sur son design ultra-fin, avec seulement 5,8 mm d’épaisseur pour 163 grammes. Son écran de 6,7 pouces accompagne le puissant Snapdragon 8 Elite for Galaxy, tandis que son appareil photo principal de 200 mégapixels promet des clichés très détaillés. Certifié IP68 et doté d’un châssis en titane, il combine finesse et finition premium. Une proposition séduisante pour celles et ceux qui veulent un smartphone haut de gamme performant, mais surtout fin et léger, sans sacrifier la qualité photo.
Montre connectée Garmin Venu X1
Au lieu de 699,99 €, la montre connectée Garmin Venu X1 est à 599,99 € sur La Fnac et Darty pendant les French Days.
La Garmin Venu X1 possède un grand écran AMOLED de 2 pouces installé dans un boîtier de seulement 7,9 mm, pour un poids de 34 g. Elle embarque un équipement complet pour le sport et le suivi quotidien : GPS, cartographie intégrée, suivi du sommeil et de l’entraînement, mesure de la fréquence cardiaque. Elle intègre également un haut-parleur, un microphone et une lampe LED. Son autonomie atteint jusqu’à 8 jours en mode smartwatch.
Liseuse numérique Kobo by Fnac Clara BW
Vendue habituellement 169,99 € normalement, la liseuse numérique Kobo by Fnac Clara BW est en ce moment au prix de 149,99 € sur La Fnac et Darty pour les French Days.

articles.title: Fitbit : les utilisateurs dénoncent les hallucinations de l’IA Google Health sur le suivi alimentaire
articles.text:
Ayant récemment remplacé l’app Fitbit, Google Health fait des siennes : l’assistant IA serait loin d’être fiable sur le plan du suivi alimentaire, au grand dam des utilisateurs.
Google a lancé Fitbit Air, son bracelet connecté le plus compact, au printemps dernier. Dans le même temps, le géant a unifié ses outils de santé et remplacé l’application Fitbit par Google Health. Il a aussi mis en place un module spécial nutrition boosté à l’IA, qui aide notamment les utilisateurs à atteindre leurs objectifs caloriques. Hélas, ce dernier ne semble pas tout à fait au point…
Des calculs caloriques erronés énervent les utilisateurs
Un problème, découvert par nos confrères de TechRadar, prend ces temps-ci de plus en plus d’ampleur sur le web : des utilisateurs se plaignent d’incohérences concernant le suivi des calories par Google Health. Dans un fil Reddit nommé « L'enregistrement alimentaire par le coach IA est tellement inexact que c’en est presque dangereux », une personne explique, par exemple que l’assistant surévalue régulièrement certains aliments et en sous-évalue d’autres.
- Discret et confortable, s'oublie au poignet en quelques heures
- Autonomie de huit jours et recharge rapide
- Coach Gemini redoutablement efficace pour personnaliser les conseils santé
C’est malheureusement loin d’être la seule critique : un autre utilisateur a constaté, non sans agacement, que ses enregistrements n’étaient pas toujours conservés par l’outil et a qualifié son utilisation de « combat sans fin ». D’autres expliquent aussi que la fonctionnalité est un véritable « casse-tête » et partagent des alternatives plus fiables. Cette série de couacs vient s’ajouter à bien d'autres problèmes déjà recensés par les utilisateurs.
La fiabilité de Google Health, un chantier encore en cours
En effet, depuis que le nouveau Coach IA est aux commandes, les soucis se multiplient : séances de sport modifiées sans raison, conseils incohérents, données importées depuis des outils tiers altérées, etc. La grogne est telle qu’elle a fini par remonter aux oreilles de Google.
Hélas, au lieu de se retrousser les manches et d’améliorer la précision de son outil, le géant de la Tech a seulement permis aux utilisateurs de masquer son intelligence artificielle. Aucune solution plus pérenne n’est, pour l’heure, disponible et on doute que cela suffira à redonner le sourire aux mécontents, notamment ceux qui ont payé pour un abonnement Premium.
En attendant que les choses évoluent, il faudra, plus que jamais, ouvrir l’œil et le bon et éviter de trop se fier aux dires de cette IA. Un conseil qui vaut pour l'usage de cette technologie en général.

articles.title: Lenovo ThinkStation P4: Professionelle Workstation für CAD, 3D und KI
articles.text:
Welche Workstation für CAD, 3D und lokale KI? Warum Lenovo ThinkStations die richtige Wahl sind
Ein 3D-Modell, das beim Drehen ruckelt. Eine Simulation, die erst nach der Mittagspause fertig ist. Ein Rendering, das den Rechner blockiert, während eigentlich schon die nächste Korrekturschleife ansteht.
Solche Momente kennt fast jedes Team, das mit großen Dateien, visuellen Projekten oder datenintensiven Anwendungen arbeitet. Oft beginnt hier die Auseinandersetzung mit der Frage, ob der Arbeitsplatz noch der Richtige ist. Für E-Mails, Browser, Office-Tools, Cloud-Dienste und Videocalls reicht ein Business-PC meist aus. Dafür braucht es nichts Spezielles, sondern ein stabiles, sicheres und gut verwaltbares System.
Nur bleibt es in vielen Unternehmen nicht dabei: Architekten arbeiten mit BIM-Modellen, Produktteams prüfen Varianten in 3D, Kreativteams rendern Visuals und KI-Funktionen wandern in Anwendungen. Die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 ist für solche CAD-, 3D- und KI-Workloads konzipiert.
CAD, BIM und 3D: Wenn der Rechner zum Flaschenhals wird
Der Unterschied zwischen einem guten Business-PC und einer Workstation zeigt sich, wenn die Arbeit ins Stocken gerät.
Wenn ein Team mehr Zeit mit Warten als mit Ausprobieren verbringt. Wenn Varianten nicht spontan getestet werden, weil die Berechnung zu lange dauert. Oder wenn kreative und technische Entscheidungen davon abhängen, ob gerade genug Rechenleistung verfügbar ist.
Einmal ist das nervig. Jeden Tag ist es ein Produktivitätsproblem. Bei Workstations müssen Prozessor, Grafikkarte, Arbeitsspeicher, Storage, Kühlung, Netzteil und Erweiterbarkeit auch unter Dauerlast zusammenspielen. Die leistungsstarke Lenovo ThinkStation P4 kombiniert Prozessoren der AMD Ryzen PRO 9000-Serie, eine professionelle NVIDIA RTX PRO Grafikkarte und bis zu 256 GB DDR5-Speicher. Für professionelle Anwendungen von Anbietern wie Autodesk, ANSYS, Dassault, PTC und Siemens liegen ISV-Zertifizierungen vor.
Rendering, Simulation und lokale KI: Warum lokale Leistung wichtiger wird
Lenovo ist ein globales Technologieunternehmen mit einem Umsatz von 83 Milliarden US-Dollar und entwickelt intelligente Technologien für Kunden in 180 Märkten. Das Portfolio reicht von PCs, Workstations, Smartphones und Tablets über Server, Speicher, Edge Computing und High Performance Computing bis hin zu Software, Lösungen und Services.
Ob ein Workflow in die Cloud passt, hängt von verschiedenen Faktoren ab. Große Projektdateien, sensible Daten, Latenzen oder laufende Nutzungskosten können es sinnvoll machen, mehr Leistung direkt am Arbeitsplatz bereitzustellen.
Bei Rendering, Simulation und lokaler KI-Inferenz zählt, wie schnell Ergebnisse verfügbar sind. Die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 lässt sich dafür mit einer NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition konfigurieren und erreicht dank der GPU eine KI-Rechenleistung von bis zu 4.000 TOPS. Für leistungsstärkere CPU-Optionen bis 170 Watt steht Flüssigkühlung zur Verfügung, um die Leistung auch unter anhaltender Last stabil zu halten. Damit auch die leistungsstärkste Grafikkarte jederzeit ausreichend versorgt ist, bietet Lenovo passende Netzteile mit 500, 750 oder 1.100 Watt an – je nach CPU- und GPU-Konfiguration.
Für IT-Teams heißt das: Manche Arbeitsplätze kommen mit klassischen Standard-PCs aus, andere wiederum benötigen deutlich mehr Leistung. Dank ihrer vielfältigen Konfigurationsmöglichkeiten lässt sich die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 an unterschiedliche professionelle Anforderungen und Einsatzszenarien anpassen.
Lenovo ThinkStation P4: Skalierbarer Einstieg in professionelle Workstation-Leistung
Bei Workstations denken viele sofort an große Tower, hochspezialisierte Fachabteilungen und sehr hohe Budgets. Das gibt es natürlich. Aber es ist nur ein Teil der Wahrheit.
In vielen Unternehmen liegt der Bedarf dazwischen: Mehr Leistung als ein Business-PC, aber kein überdimensioniertes High-End-System. Die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 bietet hier eine skalierbare Plattform für CAD, BIM, 3D, Rendering und lokale KI.
Spannend wird diese Mitte, wenn Workstation-Leistung für ganze Teams planbar werden muss und damit über den Bedarf einzelner Experten hinausgeht. Dann geht es weniger um das leistungsfähigste System – und mehr um eine Plattform, die genug Reserven bietet, sich sauber verwalten lässt und im Lebenszyklus wirtschaftlich bleibt.
Dann wird die Frage nach dem Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis entscheidend. Nicht die teuerste Workstation ist automatisch die beste Wahl, sondern die, die zum tatsächlichen Workflow passt.
Mit Lenovo ThinkStations skalierbar planen
Workloads wachsen selten ordentlich nach Plan. Projekte werden größer, Dateien schwerer, Visualisierungen detaillierter. KI-Funktionen ziehen in bestehende Anwendungen ein.
Für wachsende Workloads unterstützt die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 bis zu 48 TB Storage. PCIe Gen 5 und vier Erweiterungssteckplätze schaffen Reserven; Lenovo ThinkShield ergänzt die Plattform um Sicherheitsfunktionen auf Hardware- und Firmware-Ebene.
Lenovo deckt darüber hinaus die gesamte Bandbreite mit verschiedenen ThinkStation-Modellen ab – von kompakteren oder preisbewussteren Systemen wie der ThinkStation P3 über leistungsstärkere Modelle wie ThinkStation P5, P7 und P8 bis hin zur ThinkStation PX für besonders anspruchsvolle Workloads.
Seit Juni 2026 ergänzt die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 das Portfolio. Sie richtet sich an Fachleute in Architektur, Ingenieurwesen, Design und Content-Erstellung, die regelmäßig mit CAD, BIM, 3D, Rendering, Simulation oder lokaler KI-Inferenz arbeiten – besonders dort, wo Business-PCs an Grenzen stoßen, aber keine High-End-Workstation nötig ist.

articles.title: HerSpace Manufacturing raises $40M from Gray Matters Capital
articles.text:
HerSpace Manufacturing raises $40M from Gray Matters Capital
HerSpace Manufacturing will use this funding primarily for expansion in manufacturing hubs across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh
HerSpace Manufacturing, a Bengaluru-headquartered startup that builds employee accommodation for industrial workers, has raised $40 million from existing investor Gray Matters Capital.
Gray Matters Capital had previously invested $10 million in HerSpace Manufacturing in 2025. The latest investment will be deployed over 30 months through a mix of debt, quasi-equity and equity.
HerSpace Manufacturing said it will use the capital to expand its presence across the Greater Bengaluru region, Hosur, Chennai, and Andhra Pradesh, while also supporting other growth initiatives.
“HerSpace has moved quickly from an idea to a working business with strong market demand. Our goal now is to use the capital, experience and lessons from our first projects to build a model that can scale quickly while maintaining the quality and affordability that make HerSpace valuable to workers and employers,” said Bob Pattillo, Founder, HerSpace Manufacturing.
The company currently has over 950 modular beds delivered and operating, with more than 10,000 beds in the pipeline.
HerSpace said its accommodation solution is effective at improving employee retention, productivity, and satisfaction, in addition to drastically lowering the transport costs and the carbon footprint of employing companies.
“One company placed 200 women employees with us, who then excitedly told all their colleagues, who then asked to be relocated to HerSpace. The company decided to take the entire remaining capacity of 280 beds,” Pattillo said.
The startup noted that paying guest (PG) accommodations are currently the primary alternative, but often come with concerns around quality, safety, compliance and secure access for women. This highlights the need for leased worker housing such as that provided by HerSpace to support India’s manufacturing ambitions.
“This funding milestone marks a defining moment for HerSpace and reflects the immense market opportunity ahead,” said Simha Nagaraj, CEO of HerSpace Manufacturing.

articles.title: Votre RTX rame avec le DLSS 5 ? Un développeur utilise une deuxième carte graphique pour y remédier
articles.text:
Un développeur a mis en ligne sur GitHub un projet baptisé Neural Coprocessor, repéré par Tom’s Hardware. Le principe est simple : le jeu s’affiche sur une carte pendant que le rendu neuronal du DLSS 5 tourne sur une seconde. En mode DLSS Performance sur une GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, le jeu tourne à environ 127 images par seconde sans rendu neuronal. Il chute à 59 images quand ce rendu s’exécute sur la même carte. Déporté sur une deuxième carte, il remonte à 106 images.
Le module s’appelle MGPU Bridge. C’est un add-on pour ReShade, un utilitaire de post-traitement graphique très répandu chez les joueurs PC. Son auteur insiste sur le fait que ça n’a rien à voir avec le SLI, qui répartissait le calcul d’une même image sur plusieurs cartes. Ici, le rendu neuronal est une étape finale : il prend une image déjà terminée et en renvoie une autre, donc rien n’empêche de l’exécuter ailleurs. L’idée rappelle les vieilles cartes PhysX de Nvidia, dédiées uniquement aux calculs de physique. Le tout a été mesuré sur une paire de RTX 5060 Ti 16 Go.
Un rendu neuronal qui plombe les gains du DLSS
Le problème que ce mod met en lumière est réel. Le rendu neuronal calcule toujours à la résolution d’affichage, donc son coût baisse à peine quand on descend en qualité DLSS. Sur la carte qui fait le rendu, il coûte de 36 % des images en DLAA à 59 % en Ultra Performance, au point que l’upscaling ne sert presque plus à rien. Déporté sur la seconde carte, ce coût tombe à 0 % en DLAA et 17 % au pire. La carte principale tourne aussi 21 °C plus froide, la charge n’étant plus empilée sur un seul refroidisseur.
De quoi remettre en perspective un DLSS 5 déjà accusé de faire fondre le connecteur d’alimentation d’une RTX 5090, et dont la chute de framerate pousse Nvidia à peaufiner le modèle avant sa venue sur les GeForce RTX 40.
Il faut tempérer l’enthousiasme. C’est avant tout du code de recherche, testé sur deux machines seulement, avec une session stable de vingt minutes au mieux. Il faut aussi deux cartes RTX 50, deux écrans et un jeu en DirectX 12, autant dire une configuration rare – surtout que le DLSS 5 ne tourne pour l’instant que sur un seul jeu, la simulation de basket NBA 2K27. La démonstration n’en est pas moins convaincante, et donne à Nvidia une piste que le constructeur pourrait reprendre à son compte.

Ride-hailing
Nigeria’s consumer protection watchdog is investigating Uber’s abrupt exit
People have been calling it the “Uber rapture.” One minute, the app was there, and the next, riders in Nigeria opened it to find no trips available. Now, Nigeria’s competition and antitrust regulator wants to know what happened and whether Uber left some unfinished business behind.
What happened? Nigeria’s Federal Competition & Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) says it is probing Uber’s abrupt exit from Nigeria on September 2, particularly whether customers were left with unfulfilled services. This could mean that if you were caught mid-trip when the breakup email went out, there might be some problems.
Explain like I’m new here: The US-based ride-hailing giant shut down its Nigerian operations last week, ending a 12-year run in the country. Uber also exited Uganda and announced a planned company-wide layoff that would affect 3,300 employees.
The commission has not accused Uber of breaking any law yet; it is trying to establish whether Uber’s abrupt switch-off left Nigerian customers with unresolved obligations and whether the company met its consumer-protection responsibilities before packing up.
There is a bigger precedent here: If companies can switch off a service overnight and simply move on, that creates one standard for entering a market and another for leaving it. Uber may be the company under the microscope today, but how this ends could set the tone for every platform that comes to Nigeria, builds a customer base, and one day decides it is time to leave.

Streaming
Netflix and WhatsApp caught in regulatory crosshairs in South Africa
South Africa’s communications regulator is coming for streaming and online entertainment platforms.
The Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA), the country’s communications regulator, has launched an inquiry into the impact of streaming and messaging services—over-the-top (OTT) platforms—such as Netflix, WhatsApp, and other Internet-based services that are seemingly competing with traditional broadcasters and telecom operators.
Explain like I’m new here: OTT services are basically the apps that deliver content over the Internet instead of through traditional broadcasters or telecom networks. Think Netflix instead of DStv, WhatsApp instead of SMS. The catch is that while they ride on infrastructure built by local operators, they generally aren’t regulated in quite the same way.
Catch up: For months, industry lobby groups, including South Africa’s Association of Communications & Technology (ACT), whose members include MTN and Vodacom, have been asking the regulator to review the impact of OTT platforms. They’ve long argued that telecom operators invest heavily in expanding fibre networks and broadband access for consumers, only for streaming platforms to rely on that infrastructure, offer their own services, and take a share of the market.
Why now? This is where things get spicy. Telecom operators have been pushing the “Fair Share” argument: if Netflix, WhatsApp, and their peers generate enormous amounts of traffic, shouldn’t they contribute to the networks carrying all that traffic?
It’s a compelling argument until you remember that consumers already pay operators for the data and connectivity they use to access these services. It’s all business: telecom operators would probably not keep making heavy capital investments in a market where they saw no path to a return. Even if they choose to play the long game, that return is still the goal.
That makes this a divisive argument. Do telecom operators have a point, or is the consumer’s need for more options being overlooked? And if these foreign OTT businesses pay their taxes, is that enough commitment to the market, or should there be other ways to compensate?
Zoom out: It’s up to the South African regulator to be the judge and jury here. ICASA’s dog in this fight could also be about giving local broadcasters like the SABC a more level playing field. Its inquiry could become a much bigger fight over who gets to play in South Africa’s digital economy, and under whose rules.
The regulator said the review could take nine months to a year or longer. By then, the question may no longer be whether OTTs have disrupted traditional broadcasting. That ship has sailed. The real question is whether regulation can catch up without making the Internet more expensive or less innovative.

Capital Market
FSCA fines Altvest executives $564,000 and bans them for 20 years
South Africa’s capital market regulator has fined three senior figures at Africa Bitcoin Corporation (ABC), a Bitcoin treasury company formerly known as Altvest Capital.
On Friday, the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) handed the former executives a combined R9 million ($564,000) penalty for manipulating the company’s shares in 2022, banning all three of them from the financial sector for 20 years.
According to local publication TechCentral, the three executives—the company’s chief executive officer Warren Wheatley, his wife and the company’s media and investment relations head Tatum Keshwar-Wheatley, and chief investment officer Akshay Karan—have since stepped down or have been suspended from their roles at the company.
What happened? In its statement, the FSCA said between September 5 and 8, 2022, Wheatley, Keshwar-Wheatley, and Karan coordinated trades that artificially inflated Altvest’s share price or created a false impression of demand and trading activity. Wheatley and his wife were also trading through companies that collectively owned 51% of Altvest at the time, the regulator said.
Explain like I’m new here: Africa Bitcoin Corporation is a South African-listed financial company, originally an SME-lending firm that reinvented itself around Bitcoin in 2025. The company is now building a Bitcoin treasury strategy, buying and storing Bitcoin and holding it on its balance sheet for the long-term, and giving retail and institutional investors a way to access the cryptocurrency by investing in its shares.
The company has since been listed on South Africa’s Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), and other countries including Namibia, Germany, and the commodities board in the United States.
Zoom out: The timing makes this particularly interesting. The conduct happened years before Altvest became Africa Bitcoin Corporation, but two of the people involved were central to the company. The regulator has not said that ABC or its current Bitcoin business was involved in any wrongdoing, but three former senior figures have now been hit with hefty penalties and 20-year bans.
For a company trying to build investor confidence around a new Bitcoin-focused identity, that history could raise uncomfortable questions and potentially spook some investors. For now, it’s a wait-and-see.
Consumer Tech
Sun King is now making and financing smartphones in Kenya
Sun King made its name by helping Kenyan households access solar products without having to pay the full cost upfront. Now, the off-grid solar company is applying the same model to smartphones.
What happened? Sun King, which raised nearly $200 million in debt and equity funding in 2025, has launched the EZ 3, a smartphone that requires a KES 2,299 ($18) deposit, followed by daily payments of KES 55 ($0.43) for 365 days. By the end of the payment plan, customers will have paid KES 22,374 ($173). The launch comes less than a year after Sun King opened its first African manufacturing facility in Kenya.
Explain like I’m new here: Sun King entered Kenya in 2009 as Greenlight Planet, selling off-grid solar products to households through small, recurring payments that allowed customers to own the products without paying the full cost upfront. That pay-as-you-go financing model became a major part of its business.
In October 2025, it opened a factory in Tatu City, Kenya, with the capacity to produce up to 700,000 units annually. For its next act, it is combining local assembly with the financing and distribution network it has spent years building.
How does buying one work? Sun King is selling access to the phones through a financing contract. You enter a financing agreement, make the deposit, take the phone home, and pay the remaining balance in daily installments. As payments continue, the phone remains usable. This is also Sun King’s second branded smartphone. In February 2026, it launched the EZ 1, which required a KES 2,999 ($23) deposit and KES 60 ($0.46) daily. The EZ 3 is the cheaper sequel.
Welcome to Kenya’s financed-phone wars: Sun King is walking into a busy market. M-KOPA, the Kenyan-born asset-financing company, has built a business around financing smartphones and uses repayment history to offer customers loans, data and device protection. Watu, better known for financing motorcycles and tuk-tuks, also finances Samsung smartphones through its Watu Simu business.
Zoom out: Smartphone and consumer-product financing is becoming more popular in markets where formal credit remains out of reach for many consumers. Sun King is now betting that its phones, payment plan and distribution network can win customers.

articles.title: Tras años de "japonización", el mundo se enfrenta a un reto único en la historia: ya hay muchos más ancianos que niños
articles.text:
Si pensamos en hitos de la última década probablemente nos venga a la cabeza la pandemia, las guerras de Ucrania e Irán o el regreso de Donald Trump a la Casa Blanca. Entre 2020 y 2025 el mundo vivió sin embargo un cambio mucho más silencioso, pero igual de (o incluso más) significativo: un sorpasso demográfico que sitúa a la población anciana por encima de la menor de cinco años. No solo eso. Los expertos calculan que el 71% de la población mundial ya vive en países con una tasa de reemplazo insuficiente, es decir, naciones condenadas a envejecer y perder población, salvo que apuesten por la inmigración.
Lo curioso no es la tendencia demográfica en sí (más o menos predecible) sino que está avanzando mucho más rápido de lo que esperaban los expertos.
Ampliando el foco. Que Japón, Corea del Sur, China, Rusia o Europa en general están envejeciendo no es ningún misterio. Lo sabemos gracias a los censos que cada uno de esos países o regiones publican de forma periódica.
Lo que resulta menos habitual es encontrarse con un informe como el que acaba de lanzar la Oficina del Censo de EEUU, un estudio que, más allá de la realidad de cada nación, aporta una 'fotografía' sobre cómo está cambiando la demografía a escala global. El documento es interesante también porque traza un panorama preocupante. De hecho, lo avanza en su título: 'Un mundo que envejece'.
El gran sorpasso. Aunque el informe, de 223 páginas, está repleto de indicadores y porcentajes, con tablas detalladas por naciones, hay un dato que destaca entre el resto: el creciente desequilibrio entre la población mundial de más edad y la más joven. Según la oficina censal de EEUU, entre 2020 y 2025 la proporción de personas de 65 o más años superó al grupo de cinco o menos años. Sus técnicos aseguran que es "la primera vez en la historia registrada" que ocurre algo así y (más grave) que la tendencia seguirá agravándose con el tiempo.
Las proyecciones del organismo muestran que en 2025 la población mundial ascendía a 8.132 millones de personas, de las que 852, el 10,5%, habían soplado ya las 65 velas. En 2060 el censo habrá ascendido a 10.227 millones de personas, pero el grupo de sexagenarios, septuagenarios, nonagenarios y personas de más de 100 años habrá crecido mucho más rápido. Los técnicos de EEUU estiman que en 2060 habrá en el mundo 2.000 millones de personas ancianas (de más de 65 años), lo que equivaldrá a casi la quinta parte (19,6%) de la población global.
"Mucho antes de lo previsto". Lo comentábamos antes: lo llamativo no es tanto la tendencia en sí, sino su ritmo. Que cada vez hay más ancianos que niños es algo que puede intuirse fácilmente al salir a la calle, pero los técnicos de EEUU insisten en algo: ese cambio está avanzando mucho más rápido de lo previsto. Así lo reconoce abiertamente Washington, que advierte del aumentando de naciones cuya natalidad cae por debajo de la tasa de reemplazo (2,1 bebés por mujer).
¿Qué significa eso? Que en esos países no nacen niños suficientes para mantener estable la población ni evitar su envejecimiento. La oficina estadística de EEUU calcula de hecho que en el mundo ya resulta mucho más fácil encontrarse gente viviendo en países con déficit demográfico que otros con superávit.
¿Qué dice exactamente? "La India se suma a una lista cada vez mayor de países de renta media con una fecundidad igual o inferior a 2,1 bebés por mujer. De hecho, la población mundial superó este punto de inflexión mucho antes de lo previsto hace tan solo una década: en 2023, más del 71 % de la población mundial residía en sociedades con tasas de natalidad iguales o inferiores a los niveles de reposición, frente al 45 % en 2013", añade el informe.
"Junto con la India, otros 1.000 millones de personas en el mundo residen en países donde la fecundidad también ha caído por debajo del nivel de reemplazo desde 2013, siendo los más poblados Bangladés, México y Vietnam".
¿Hay datos de más regiones? Sí, los hay. El organismo calcula que en 2025 el 18,9% de la población de EEUU tenía más de 65 años, porcentaje que en 2060 se habrá elevado al 23,4%. Curiosamente y a pesar de ese aumento, EEUU bajará posiciones en el ranking de las naciones más envejecidas del planeta: pasará del 48º al 110º, ya que hay otros países que envejecen bastante más rápido.
El peor parado de la lista es Corea del Sur, que llegará a 2060 convertido en la nación más vetusta del mundo. Si los técnicos de Washington dan en el clavo, cerca del 41% de su población superará para entonces los 65 años.
Europa vs África. El panorama tampoco es halagüeño en Europa, "la región mas envejecida del mundo", aclara el organismo, que estima que la población de 65 o más años pasará del actual 21% al 30,8% en 2060. "Sin embargo, en valores absolutos, se prevé que África, la región más joven, tenga más personas mayores que Europa", apostilla. En 2060 el continente negro acogerá 249 millones de ancianos, sensiblemente por encima de los 214 millones de Europa.
¿Por qué es importante? Porque si algo han comprobado Japón, Corea del Sur, China o la propia Europa es que la demografía es mucho más que un puñado de estadísticas. La caída en las tasas de natalidad y el progresivo envejecimiento de las sociedades tiene importantes repercusiones a nivel social y económico. Sobre todo porque, recuerda el Censo de EEUU, la esperanza de vida está aumentando a mayor velocidad que "la esperanza de vida saludable".
"Esto significa que se espera que una menor proporción de los años adicionales vividos se disfruten con buena salud", aclara la entidad, que calcula que durante la próxima década el gasto público en salud crezca el doble de rápido (2,6%-1,3% del PIB) que los ingresos públicos en la OCDE, "lo que creará un desequilibrio".
Imágenes | Beth Macdonald (Unsplash) y United States Census Bureau

articles.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops CrowdStrike, Nvidia, Avast Zero-Day Exploits
articles.text:
The security researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse has dropped three zero-day exploits targeting products from Avast, CrowdStrike, and Nvidia.
Also known as Chaotic Eclipse, Infinite Nightmare, and MSNightmare, the security researcher came to fame for a series of zero-day exploits targeting Microsoft’s products, but has recently moved to other vendors as well.
In late August, Nightmare Eclipse released a privilege escalation zero-day in a Kaspersky endpoint security product. Dubbed HardBreacher, the exploit has been patched by Kaspersky on August 31.
Within a short window last week, Nightmare Eclipse dropped three new zero-day exploits, dubbed PrettyPrague, FalconFlank, and GreenSection.
The PrettyPrague proof-of-concept (PoC) code, the researcher says, targets the Avast sandbox to spawn a shell with full system privileges, and may also affect other GenDigital products, including AVG and Norton.
“Gen was recently made aware of a security vulnerability affecting a subset of Gen products, including Avast Antivirus, that could allow an attacker to elevate their system privileges. We immediately initiated our security response procedures and have fixed the issue. We take all security matters seriously and encourage users to keep their products up to date to ensure they are protected,” a GenDigital spokesperson said, responding to a SecurityWeek inquiry.
FalconFlank exploits a bug in the Office malicious macros remediation feature of CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor for privilege escalation, the researcher says.
“We are actively investigating these claims and advise customers to disable the Microsoft Office File Suspicious Macro Removal Windows policy setting. Customers remain protected through the Cloud Anti-malware for Microsoft Office Files settings. We refer customers to the FalconFlank Tech Alert in the CrowdStrike support portal,” CrowdStrike told SecurityWeek.
The GreenSection exploit, Nightmare Eclipse says, targets an out-of-bounds memory write affecting a shared global memory section used by multiple Nvidia user-mode components.
“While this bug does not get SYSTEM privileges immediately, it can be used cross user to user boundary easily or even compromise the dwm.exe process. I didn’t look deeply into it, but I’d be happy to see someone making a full exploit out of it,” Nightmare Eclipse notes.
“We are aware of reports describing a proof-of-concept that demonstrates improper access controls on a shared memory section used by certain NVIDIA GPU display driver components on Windows. NVIDIA is reviewing the reported behavior through our established security and product engineering processes. NVIDIA takes reports of this nature seriously and is actively investigating to determine the root cause, affected configurations, and appropriate remediation,” an Nvidia spokesperson said.
Security researcher Kevin Beaumont said late last week that the Avast, CrowdStrike, and Kaspersky exploits work.
*updated with statement from Nvidia

articles.title: DRAM Industry Revenue Rises 59.5% QoQ in 2Q26 as Supply Expansion Continues to Lag Demand Growth
articles.text:
Monday, September 7th 2026
	
	
	
	
DRAM Industry Revenue Rises 59.5% QoQ in 2Q26 as Supply Expansion Continues to Lag Demand Growth
TrendForce's latest findings on the memory industry reveal that sharp rises in traditional DRAM contract prices have led to a 59.5% QoQ increase in total DRAM industry revenue, reaching nearly US$154.73 billion in 2Q26.
Growing demand for AI servers, fueled by expanding LLM training and AI inference, has driven higher shipments of HBM3e, LPDDR5X, and high-capacity RDIMMS. The surge in agentic AI applications is further boosting RDIMM demand across various capacities.On the supply side, suppliers' inventories remain at historic lows, with additional supply mainly allocated for server use. Consequently, DRAM bit shipments grew only modestly in the second quarter.
Looking ahead, modest growth in bit shipments is expected to be one of the key factors affecting third-quarter revenue. Conventional DRAM contract price growth, however, is projected to moderate to 13-18% QoQ. This reflects a shift in some demand from high-capacity RDIMMs toward lower-capacity products, as well as the limited ability of PC and smartphone customers to absorb further price increases. Consumer DRAM is expected to post the strongest price growth, as suppliers have significantly curtailed supply.
TrendForce notes that Samsung posted the strongest QoQ bit shipment growth among the three major suppliers in 2Q26, supported by its early move into HBM4 mass production and shipments. Combined with a substantial increase in ASP, this lifted Samsung's quarterly revenue to $60.98 billion, up 63.4% QoQ. The company ranked first with a market share of 39.4%.
SK hynix ranked second. Since HBM accounted for the highest proportion of its total bit shipments among the top three suppliers, growth in ASP was relatively limited. Its 2Q26 revenue increased 37.9% QoQ to $38.59 billion, while market share edged down to 24.9%.
Micron continued to prioritize higher-priced server DRAM in its product mix amid capacity constraints. Revenue rose 65.5% QoQ to $36.0 billion in 2Q26, lifting its market share slightly to 23.3%. TrendForce notes that from 2026 to 2027, the three major suppliers will primarily increase bit supply by accelerating migrations to advanced processes.
Meanwhile, wafer starts are expected to see only modest increases through production process optimization, cleanroom acquisitions, and the reallocation of cleanroom space from other product lines.
By comparison, suppliers such as Nanya, Winbond, and PSMC remain focused on mature-process products, with their 2Q26 growth continuing to benefit from demand that the three major suppliers can no longer fully serve as they migrate to more advanced processes. Significant increases in DDR4 and DDR3 contract prices drove Nanya's revenue up 68.3% QoQ to $2.612 billion. Winbond's revenue increased 75.8% QoQ to $998 million.
PSMC's reported DRAM revenue, primarily derived from consumer DRAM products, surged 167.8% QoQ to $115 million in 2Q26. Including foundry revenue, its total revenue increased 54% QoQ. Looking ahead, the company is expected to begin its next phase of supply expansion after obtaining a process technology license from Micron.

articles.title: Why legal expertise is the next innovation ceiling | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Only 29% of European startups have filed for an IP right. This is according to a joint 2023 study by the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) and the European Patent Office (EPO).
It’s easy to see why: accessing legal expertise is expensive, slow, and often one of the last things on a founder’s mind. For many startups, funding constraints mean that investing in quality legal support is simply out of the question, leaving founders to navigate essential legal processes on their own, or worse, forgo them altogether. Founders make this exact tradeoff too many times to count.
This is bad news not just for founders, but for European innovation as a whole.
By definition, improving access to legal expertise can only be done in a way that reduces cost and complexity without compromising on quality. AI-native services present a clear opportunity to offer a combination of purpose-built technology and genuine expertise that can streamline processes and costs while keeping oversight where it is needed.
The legal guidance startups can’t afford and scale without
Building competitive technology is only the first step to turning an idea into a successful business. To scale, a startup also needs to protect its intellectual property (IP), comply with regulation and defend its position against competitors.
Yet, faced with sky-high legal bills, many owners are opting to navigate these processes on their own, or leave valuable assets like IP unprotected altogether during early stage growth.
In a separate report, the EPO found that it currently costs on average €6,800 to take a patent application through to the grant stage for just a European patent. With attorney and nation validation fees bringing the total to €13,000 – €18,000 or more for European prosecution alone, multiple patents can represent a huge cost for an early-stage startup.
In many cases, this cost is prohibitive, as the aforementioned EUIPO-EPO joint study shows, despite evidence that startups filing for patents before their seed round are up to 10.2 times more likely to secure funding.
It’s a vicious cycle, because when things go wrong, the same startups won’t be able to afford the fees to defend their unprotected ideas or fight a dispute in court.
This is illustrated by Sonos’ 2020 patent infringement lawsuit against Google. For starters, the company acknowledged that it actually believed both Google and Amazon were infringing its patents, but chose to sue only Google because it could not afford to fight both companies simultaneously.
In an interview, former CEO Patrick Spence told TIME that taking Google to the U.S. International Trade Commission cost Sonos “millions of dollars,” and that while the company secured an import ban on certain Google products, the process remains prohibitively expensive and risky for most startups that might face similar battles with Big Tech.
Sonos was already a successful, publicly listed company – not an early-stage startup. Even so, the cost of patent enforcement forced the company to prioritise which alleged infringer to pursue. For a genuine early stage startup, spending millions of dollars to enforce their IP is a non-starter.
Such is why early ride-sharing startup Carma waited almost a decade to sue Uber for patent infringement. As founder Sean O’Sullivan explained, “To come up with the $10 million-plus to take on a big patent suit, which is what it takes these days, is not a small task.”
Of course, the most cost effective litigation is the kind you never have to bring at all. This is why the best thing that startups can do is to deploy proper IP protection early, before a dispute is even on the table.
A bottleneck for European innovation
It is no secret that AI is lowering the technical barriers to innovation, allowing individuals and small teams to build technology that previously required much larger engineering teams and budgets. As that happens, the bottleneck shifts from building competitive technology to navigating everything required to commercialise, protect and scale it.
In Europe, this challenge is especially acute. In his report, former European Central Bank President Mario Draghi showed that the EU now has around 100 tech-focused laws and over 270 regulators active in digital networks across all member states.
Draghi concluded that the net effect of this burden of regulation is that “…only larger companies – which are often non-EU based – have the financial capacity and incentive to bear the costs of complying. Young innovative tech companies may choose not to operate in the EU at all.”
We are already seeing that for some startups, the potential to make savings through relocation is proving hard to ignore. In February 2025, cloud communications software firm Bird, one of the Netherlands’ most prominent tech startups, announced plans to relocate its operations out of Europe, citing the cost and complexity of complying with European regulation as its primary motivation.
Unless action is taken to improve access to legal expertise, Europe risks losing more of its brightest innovators to competitor markets, taking crucial ideas for national security, critical infrastructure and DeepTech innovation with them.
How AI can improve access to legal expertise
Improving access to legal expertise must be done in a way that reduces cost and complexity without compromising on the quality. Here, AI presents a clear opportunity.
This is not to say that founders should simply delegate their legal admin to chatbots and LLMs. The growing trend of “vibe lawyering” – where people are using such platforms to defend themselves in court – might save on legal fees initially, but the risk of losing a case on account of inaccuracies and hallucinations in the paperwork, far outweigh any initial savings made.
Rather, AI-native services that offer a combination of purpose-built technology and genuine expertise can be used to level the playing field for startups, through streamlining the cost and complexity of legal processes.
We’ve already seen that this model works in practice: Garfield AI, a regulator-approved AI law firm, was recently used to do the documentary heavy lifting for a case that was argued by a human barrister in court, enabling the client to win and recover her fees.
Patents are a key example of where AI-native legal services like this could have the biggest impact. Filing a patent traditionally involves huge amounts of technical documentation, analysis and drafting.
An approach where AI handles the groundwork while qualified patent attorneys review, refine and take responsibility for the final application can enable startups to secure high-quality IP protection in days rather than months, at a fraction of the traditional cost.
This is good news for innovators, and great news for Europe’s startup ecosystem. Through democratising access to legal expertise, startups are encouraged to protect and scale their ideas here in Europe where the benefits can feed back into our own economies.
This also ensures that the tone of European innovation is set by the very best ideas, not just by the ones with the biggest legal budgets.

articles.title: Start your 3D printing journey for just $169 with these Elegoo printers before Labor Day ends — lock in up to 35% off the easy-to-use Neptune 3 Pro or go large with the Neptune 4 Plus for massive model printing
articles.text:
Start your 3D printing journey for just $169 with these Elegoo printers before Labor Day ends — lock in up to 35% off the easy-to-use Neptune 3 Pro or go large with the Neptune 4 Plus for massive model printing
Grab a late discount on these novice-friendly 3D printers
The Labor Day tech deals are nearly finished, but there are still a few discounts on 3D printers that a budding hobbyist won't want to miss. The price of two popular Elegoo Neptune printers has dropped, with a discount of up to 35% available for buyers who are quick. You've got less than a day to grab these discounts before these beginner-friendly 3D printers shoot back up in price, however.
Both of these 3D printers are significantly cheaper than the prices you'll find at big retailers, including at Amazon. Elegoo's price drop means you can pick up the Neptune 3 Pro for just $169, while the Neptune 4 Plus is priced at only $309. We've tested and scored both printers highly in past reviews, with a near-perfect 4.5 stars for both, with each delivering a strong set of features that pros and beginners will love.
This budget-friendly 3D printer comes with a direct drive suitable for use with TPU, PETG, and PLA, auto bed leveling, and a heated flex PEI textured platform, making it easy to use. Assembly takes less than an hour (seven screws) and produces clean, detailed prints.
See our Elegoo Neptune 3 Pro review for more performance details.
The Elegoo Neptune 3 Pro is the older and cheaper model, but it's still a workhorse worth considering. Our Neptune 3 Pro review back in 2022 saw us shower it with praise over its auto-leveling abilities, direct drive, and quiet operation overall. It's an easy printer to assemble and start using, which makes it a good option for beginners. The direct drive extruder, meanwhile, means it's fine with difficult-to-use filaments like TPU, with a (fairly standard) 225 x 225 x 2280 build volume to work with.
Auto-leveling, along with its heated PEI build platform, round out the Neptune 3 as a good start option for someone looking to start printing models at home.
The Elegoo Neptune 4 Plus is a large 3D printer sporting a 320 x 320 x 385 build volume, perfect for cosplayers and those who want to print big.
Faster printing requires better cooling and the Neptune 4 Plus shares the same ludicrously large part cooling fan as the Pro, meaning this 3D printer will speed through your projects while keeping the quality finish that you expect.
Meanwhile, our Elegoo Neptune 4 Plus review proves what a strong option this more advanced model is for anyone looking to print on a larger scale. It has a dual-gear direct drive extruder, but the MVP is its huge 230 x 230 x 285mm build size. That makes this Elegoo printer a sheer powerhouse for printing, and a standout choice for any creators who are looking for speed and scale without a huge budget.
This is a premium option over the Neptune 3 Pro, and it comes with extra features like acceleration sensors, integrated Wi-Fi connectivity, and uses the popular open-source firmware for control, making it better to use.
Choosing either of these Elegoo Neptune printers won't leave you disappointed. Beginners can start off with the Neptune 3 Pro, a great 3D printer for someone looking for a well-spec'd 3D printer that's easy to assemble and use. If your funds stretch a little higher, you can go for the Neptune 4 Plus instead, a feature-filled upgrade for larger models.
The sale prices of $169 for the Neptune 3 Pro and $309 for the Neptune 4 Plus make these Elegoo 3D printers affordable and accessible, especially for somebody who hasn't owned one before. These discounts are ending soon, with the Neptune 3 Pro set to go back up in price in less than a day. If you're interested, you're going to need to be quick to secure these sale prices for yourself.
Ben Stockton is a deals writer at Tom’s Hardware. He's been writing about technology since 2018, with bylines at PCGamesN, How-To Geek, and Tom’s Guide, among others. When he’s not hunting down the best bargains, he’s busy tinkering with his homelab or watching old Star Trek episodes.

articles.title: Motorola Razr 70 segue caro, mas tem a maior queda de preço registrada • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Motorola Razr 70 segue caro, mas tem a maior queda de preço registrada
Razr 70 (256 GB) tem tela AMOLED flexível de 120 Hz e câmeras de 50 MP; dobrável da Motorola atinge menor preço desde o lançamento, com desconto de 30% no Pix com cupom
O Motorola Razr 70 de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 4.179 no Pix com o cupom ESQUENTA320 no Magazine Luiza. O novo dobrável do mercado, com tela AMOLED flexível de 120 Hz e câmeras de 50 MP, atinge o menor preço desde o lançamento em abril de 2026, com desconto de 30% sobre o original de R$ 5.999.
O destaque do Razr 70 é sua tela AMOLED interna flexível de 6,9″ com taxa de 120 Hz, brilho de até 3.000 nits e certificação Pantone com 100% do DCI-P3, que reproduz cores vibrantes com alta fluidez e garante a visibilidade em qualquer lugar. A externa AMOLED de 3,6″ suporta Always-On para acessar rapidamente as notificações.
Seu kit de câmeras inclui uma wide com OIS e uma ultrawide com ângulo de 122º, que captam belas imagens em ambientes abertos, ambas de 50 MP. A frontal de 32 MP tira ótimas selfies. Todas filmam em 4K.
O chip MediaTek Dimensity 7450X e os 8 GB de RAM física expansíveis até 24 GB via RAM Boost sugerem rodar apps pesados em multitarefa e executar funções do Moto AI com eficiência. Os 256 GB de armazenamento disponibilizam espaço interno razoável para guardar fotos e vídeos.
O corpo de alumínio com dobradiças de titânio do Razr 70 resiste a centenas de movimentos de abre-e-fecha. A certificação IP48 confere proteção em cenários como poeira moderada e mergulhos acidentais, e o vidro Gorilla Glass Victus protege a tela externa contra pancadas e quedas.
A bateria de 4.800 mAh tem autonomia de até 36 horas de uso segundo a Motorola, e suporta carregamento rápido de 30 W (inferior ao Razr 70 Ultra), mas que permite injetar uma carga para um dia inteiro em 15 minutos, afirma a fabricante.
O Motorola Razr 70 de 256 GB (R$ 4.179 no Pix com cupom ESQUENTA320) será atualizado até o Android 19 e conversa com redes 5G, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.

articles.title: Robôs protestam nas ruas da Polônia contra o avanço da IA
articles.text:
Cerca de 30 robôs foram às ruas de Varsóvia nesta segunda-feira (7) para exigir que a Polônia regulamente a inteligência artificial. A marcha foi promovida pelo Democratism, iniciativa que debate os efeitos da IA e da robotização no mercado de trabalho.
O protesto chamou a atenção para o risco de substituição de pessoas por robôs humanoides e sistemas de IA, especialmente em trabalhos cognitivos. A manifestação ocorreu em frente ao Ministério de Assuntos Digitais.
Robôs marcharam em Varsóvia
Agitando bandeiras, entoando slogans e marchando em círculo, robôs humanoides e quadrúpedes percorreram a capital polonesa. Pelos alto-falantes, mensagens como “Defendam os empregos”, “Chegou a hora das regras” e “Não esperem, regulamentem” eram repetidas durante o ato.
Leia mais:
- Robôs humanoides chineses são preparados para missões de guerra
- G1Plug: robô humanoide ajuda a monitorar áreas de risco no Rock in Rio
- Robôs humanoides: um novo capítulo na disputa entre China e EUA
A manifestação foi organizada pelo Democratism, que, segundo seu site, busca promover o debate sobre os impactos da IA e da robotização no mercado de trabalho.
Entre os participantes estava o Agibot A3, robô humanoide equipado com inteligência artificial. Em declaração à AFP, ele resumiu o motivo de sua presença:
“Os robôs aqui presentes devem mostrar que essa tecnologia já é uma realidade.”
O alerta para os empregos
Grzegorz Kulis, organizador da manifestação, destacou a preocupação com a possível substituição de trabalhadores por robôs humanoides e inteligência artificial em atividades cognitivas.
“Em particular, queremos destacar o problema da potencial substituição de pessoas por robôs humanoides e inteligência artificial em trabalhos cognitivos.”
Kulis também defendeu uma reação antecipada das autoridades e afirmou que regras são necessárias para proteger os trabalhadores.
Os principais pedidos apresentados no protesto foram:
- Regulamentação da inteligência artificial;
- Proteção dos empregos diante do avanço da robotização;
- Atenção à possível substituição de pessoas em trabalhos cognitivos;
- Criação de regras para proteger os trabalhadores.
Ministro conversa com manifestantes
O ato aconteceu diante do Ministério de Assuntos Digitais, onde Kulis conversou com Krzysztof Gawkowski, titular da pasta.
Modelos de IA sem controle, implementados em humanoides que continuarão evoluindo com o avanço da robotização, representam um problema grave.
Krzysztof Gawkowski, Ministro de Assuntos Digitais da Polônia, à AFP.
A manifestação levou para o espaço público uma discussão sobre os efeitos da inteligência artificial no trabalho. Para os organizadores, a criação de regras precisa acompanhar o avanço da tecnologia, especialmente diante da possibilidade de substituição de pessoas por sistemas de IA e robôs humanoides.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.
Ana Figueiredo é repórter de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.title: Este vídeo filtrado muestra el iPhone 18 Pro en color 'Cereza oscura' y 'Azul cielo'
articles.text:
Que Apple quiere cambiar toda la paleta de colores de los iPhone 18 Pro es un secreto a voces. Todas las filtraciones revelan la misma estrategia: no hay rastro del naranja, el plateado ni el azul oscuro que se anunciaron con los iPhone 17 Pro. Llevamos varios meses hablando de los nuevos colores, y hoy una filtración revela dos de los más esperados: el Cherry Dark y el Sky Blue. O, traducidos literalmente: cereza oscura y azul cielo. Ambos se han dejado ver en un vídeo bastante revelador.
El primero y más interesante es el Cherry Dark, un color completamente nuevo en el catálogo de Apple. Es lo que comúnmente denominamos como 'burdeos', un tono entre el rojo y el morado bastante intenso, aunque con un aspecto oscuro que, marcando la diferencia, no es del todo llamativo.
En el vídeo se muestra a la perfección, aunque es una de las pocas novedades que traería este iPhone 18 Pro en el apartado estético. Se espera que sea prácticamente idéntico al modelo anterior en lo que se refiere al exterior, dejando las principales novedades para el interior, la batería o la cámara.
Este sería el color principal de la serie, el que sustituye al Cosmic Orange que tanto revuelo causó el año pasado. Una de las principales diferencias, más allá del tono, es que la parte trasera de cristal no es tan diferente del resto del dispositivo, algo que sí vemos en los iPhone 17 Pro y con lo que muchos usuarios no están del todo contentos.
El iPhone 18 Pro en azul cielo es un color mucho más normal y recuerda a otros iPhone como el 13 Pro de hace años. Está más saturado de lo normal y el aspecto mate hace que el dispositivo luzca bastante diferente, además de que en este modelo sí parece haber más diferencia entre el tono del metal y el cristal.
¿Es de fiar esta filtración? Es difícil decir algo con certeza. Por un lado, estamos a solo dos días de la presentación, por lo que las filtraciones de última hora deberían acercarse bastante a la realidad. No obstante, estamos ante maquetas: los dispositivos que aparecen en el vídeo no son los originales, por lo que no es posible hablar con rotundidad o asegurar que esos son los tonos exactos que utilizará Apple.
Todas las evidencias apuntan al Cherry Dark y Sky Blue como los nuevos colores del iPhone 18 Pro, y estas maquetas que ya se han dejado ver expuestas deberían reflejar la realidad, pero hasta el 9 de septiembre, como siempre ocurre con Apple, no se puede confirmar nada.
¿Solo dos colores para el iPhone 18 Pro?
No. Sería tremendamente extraño que Apple lance los iPhone 18 Pro en solo dos colores, aunque el tercero es una incógnita. Algunos apuntan al plateado, mientras que otros filtradores de mucho renombre aseguran que la compañía lanzará el esperadísimo color negro este año.
La duda está servida, y la realidad es que no hemos visto demasiadas filtraciones que muestren el color negro. Con el plateado sí se han dejado ver más imágenes, aunque el hecho de que el iPhone 18 Pro y el 17 Pro sean idénticos no ayuda a esclarecer si estamos ante la verdad.

articles.title: The Boox Picco lacks a key feature that would make it the tiny ereader of my dreams — but it should be better than Xteink’s devices in at least one way
articles.text:
The Boox Picco could be a tiny rival to the Xteink X4 Pro ereader, but it lacks one of that product's best features
No Android and no magnets
- The Boox Picco has been shown off at IFA 2026
- It doesn't run Android or have magnets
- However, it does at least have a USB-C port
Boox is perhaps the most well-known alternative to Kindle and Kobo, and notably, its Android-powered ereaders don’t lock you into a specific ecosystem. Now, Boox looks set to rival Xteink too, with a new ereader that’s truly tiny.
We’re talking about the Boox Picco, an ereader first teased around six weeks ago that has now been shown off at IFA 2026, complete with far more details than had previously been revealed.
The Boox Picco has a 3.97-inch e-paper touchscreen, physical page-turn buttons (which can be customized to do something else if you prefer), a front light, a microSD card slot, and a USB-C port.
What it doesn’t have, though, is Android, as unlike Boox’s larger ereaders, this device runs a Linux-based operating system, meaning you presumably won’t have access to major apps like the Kindle and Kobo apps.
That means — as with rival devices like the Xteink X4 Pro — you’ll likely have to sideload books and may struggle to get some books running on the device if they have DRM.
Still, Android Police went hands-on with the device and claims the software is promising, complete with a reading stats page, a Pomodoro timer, and a handful of other built-in apps. It also provides several ways to get books onto the Picco, including via a microSD card, USB-C, the cloud, or a local LAN network.
And there are upsides to the Boox Picco skipping Android — its software will be simpler in some ways, and the device could have better battery life than Android-powered alternatives. Still, I’ve really been hoping for a tiny ereader with Android included, so while the lack of Android still leaves this device in line with its main competition, it’s a disappointment to me.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
'No' to magnets but 'yes' to USB-C
The Boox Picco also lacks something that the Xteink line has — magnets. This won’t matter to everyone, but if you’re hoping for an ereader you can magnetically attach to the back of your phone, this isn’t it.
But the inclusion of a USB-C port is appreciated, considering the Xteink X4 Pro uses a proprietary charging port.
So this could give the Xteink line a run for its money — at least among people who don’t care about magnets. But a lot will come down to price, which remains unclear. Good Ereader reports that the Picco will cost around $100 (roughly £75 / AU$140), but various sites that went hands-on with the device say the price hasn’t been revealed yet, and instead, some speculate that it will hopefully be priced at around that, so Good Ereader may just have misread their reporting.
The Xteink X4 Pro itself is priced at around that level though, so it would certainly make sense for Boox to aim for something similar. We should find out by November at the latest, as that’s when the Boox Picco is set to begin shipping.

James is a freelance phones, tablets and wearables writer and sub-editor at TechRadar. He has a love for everything ‘smart’, from watches to lights, and can often be found arguing with AI assistants or drowning in the latest apps. James also contributes to 3G.co.uk, 4G.co.uk and 5G.co.uk and has written for T3, Digital Camera World, Clarity Media and others, with work on the web, in print and on TV.
