articles.title: The real reason your phone is getting more expensive
articles.text:
When Apple debuts the next generation of iPhones this week, they’re likely to come with an unwanted change: a higher price tag. A price hike from the supply-chain powerhouse would be the clearest sign yet that soaring memory costs have become unavoidable — with no end to the memory crunch in sight.
The real reason your phone is getting more expensive
Soaring RAM costs are driving up prices across the tech industry. It may take years to settle down.
The real reason your phone is getting more expensive
Soaring RAM costs are driving up prices across the tech industry. It may take years to settle down.
Call it “chipflation” or “RAMageddon.” The shortage is reversing a decades-long decline in memory costs that helped make consumer electronics more powerful without making them dramatically more expensive. The terms “memory prices” and “memory shortage” appeared in 473 company transcripts last quarter, according to data provided by AlphaSense. The entire industry is seemingly working on the problem. And yet, we’re years away from seeing it fixed.
The common wisdom is that AI is at fault: The technology isn’t just contributing to higher energy prices and layoffs; it’s also helping drive up the cost of everything from smartphones to game consoles.
But the shortage was brewing well before ChatGPT took off — and was then amplified by AI’s unending hunger for RAM. The current market is the product of a complicated and very profitable reshuffling of the memory industry within a system that was already failing to keep up.
“We need to build more wafer capacity,” Manish Bhatia, president and COO of Micron — one of the three largest memory manufacturers — told The Verge. “[It’s] a very different challenge for the industry than it had been for many years before, where technology alone was able to keep up with the demand.”
For years, memory manufacturers could increase production by fitting more chips onto each wafer. But those gains were shrinking and taking longer to achieve. In 2021, even as pandemic-era electronics demand surged, Micron concluded that the problem was more fundamental: Technological advances alone would no longer create enough capacity to keep pace with long-term demand. Manufacturers would have to process more wafers — and build enormous new facilities to do it.
Then the memory business collapsed. Pandemic-era purchases of computers, tablets, and phones had pulled demand forward; consumer spending weakened, and manufacturers were left with excess inventory. They lost money and slowed their expansion plans.
By the time the market began recovering, generative AI had unleashed a wave of demand far larger and more memory-intensive than manufacturers had ever anticipated.
The memory business is also extraordinarily concentrated. Three manufacturers account for about 90 percent of the market, according to Counterpoint, leaving the world dependent on a handful of companies to divide limited capacity between AI infrastructure and consumer devices. Counterpoint estimates that Samsung controlled 39 percent of the memory market in the second quarter of 2026, followed by SK Hynix at 26 percent and Micron at 25 percent.
The memory inside your phone or computer broadly falls into two buckets. DRAM, or dynamic random-access memory, temporarily holds the information a device needs while opening apps, loading webpages, or running software. NAND flash memory provides longer-term storage for things like photos and files.
“It’s not as simple as saying data centers are consuming RAM. The RAM is not the same.”
Inside AI data centers, specialized processors rely heavily on a form of DRAM called high-bandwidth memory, or HBM.
“It’s not as simple as saying data centers are consuming RAM,” David Naranjo, associate director at Counterpoint, told The Verge. “The RAM is not the same.”
By stacking memory chips together and using advanced connections and packaging, HBM can move enormous quantities of data to and from those processors much faster and more efficiently.
It’s more difficult to produce, but also more lucrative to sell. Deep-pocketed AI chipmakers like Nvidia and AMD and tech giants like Meta and Microsoft have an insatiable need for it to power their AI systems — and are more than happy to pay.
HBM also consumes significantly more manufacturing capacity than conventional DRAM. Memory chips are made many at a time on large, circular silicon wafers. Because a finished HBM product stacks multiple, larger chips together, it requires considerably more silicon. Micron estimates that producing a given amount of HBM requires roughly three times as many wafers as producing the same amount of conventional DRAM.
The incentives increasingly favor AI. Rather than guessing how many phones or laptops will sell a year from now, memory makers can lock in multiyear commitments from some of the world’s richest companies.
“We have been engaging in discussions with customers, prioritizing those who can guarantee committed future captive demand,” Jaejune Kim, Samsung’s executive vice president of memory, said on the company’s last earnings call.
AI is also increasing demand for conventional DRAM. Phone and PC makers want to run smaller AI models directly on their devices, requiring more sophisticated conventional memory — and more of it. Future models may need substantially more memory than their predecessors to support those capabilities.
“The three big memory guys, they’re just basically allocating the capacity that they have to these companies.”
“As AI spreads across various services such as search, coding, and productivity tools, the scope of demand is widening from a memory perspective,” said Song Hyun-jong, president of SK Hynix, another of the big three memory manufacturers, on the company’s most recent earnings call. “We are witnessing a structural shift in demand where both AI memory and conventional memory are growing together.”
Samsung and Micron have both said they remain committed to conventional DRAM. Micron’s Bhatia told The Verge that it still accounts for most of the company’s wafer capacity. But limited supply, surging demand, and AI customers willing to make long-term commitments have made it extraordinarily lucrative to cede space to HBM.
SK Hynix posted a record 76 percent operating margin last quarter, up from 41 percent a year earlier, while Micron’s adjusted gross margin hit a record 85 percent. Samsung’s semiconductor profits, meanwhile, jumped roughly 250-fold from a year earlier.
“It’s more profitable,” Naranjo said. “The three big memory guys, they’re just basically allocating the capacity that they have to these companies.”
Counterpoint estimates that DRAM prices for smartphones increased roughly 56 percent in the first quarter of 2026 compared to a quarter earlier, and grew around 83 percent in the second quarter. For 16GB of DRAM for a smartphone, Counterpoint estimates that it cost roughly $42 in the second quarter of 2025 and about $181 a year later — an increase of more than 300 percent.
Those aren’t necessarily Apple’s prices — few companies have more leverage with suppliers — but the figures show how dramatically the component costs of building a high-end phone have changed.
The obvious solution is to make more memory. The problem is that it takes years to accomplish — even if you’re working fast.
Micron is currently demonstrating just how much work “more” entails.
In July, the company poured the first concrete for its planned manufacturing complex near Syracuse in upstate New York. Once completed, the site will contain 2.4 million square feet of cleanroom space, making it the largest semiconductor manufacturing site in US history by that measure — and Micron’s largest facility anywhere in the world.
Those cleanrooms where the chips are made will occupy only a fraction of the entire build, which is roughly the size of 350 football fields.
“By the time we’re done, we’ll have built probably 15 to 20 million actual square feet of building space to support the 2.4 million square feet of cleanroom,” Bhatia told The Verge. In one of Micron’s fab designs, the cleanroom occupies just one floor of a five-story building.
Micron doesn’t expect meaningful output until 2030
The remaining space will house a vast network of water-treatment, power, air-handling, and utility-distribution systems needed to keep it running.
Even though Micron reached the concrete pour ahead of schedule, it still took more than two years. The company began permitting after its CHIPS Act grant for New York was confirmed in March 2024, broke ground in January 2026, and poured concrete about six months later.
The physical construction unfolds in three broad stages. Preparing the ground can take six to nine months, Bhatia said. Building the concrete structure and facade can require another 18 months. But the most complicated stage comes after the building is standing: installing the vast network of mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and piping systems required to operate a semiconductor fab.
Those systems must turn an enormous industrial building into an environment where a single microscopic particle doesn’t land in the wrong place and ruin a chip.
Bhatia offered a sense of the precision required:
“Imagine trying to build all of New York state and not have any ants anywhere in the entire state,” he said. “That’s what we’re trying to do on every one of these wafers, and we do it over and over again.”
Completing the building still doesn’t produce memory. Micron expects to activate and test essential systems like power, water, and ventilation at the end of 2028, then spend 2029 moving in manufacturing equipment and beginning pilot production. The company doesn’t expect meaningful output until 2030. Even on an accelerated timeline, the journey from permitting to production will have taken roughly six years.
The company’s new Idaho fab is further along and is expected to begin wafer output in mid-2027.
Micron is spending enormous amounts to move the process along more quickly, roughly doubling its capital expenditure from a year earlier to exceed $25 billion this year.
Even with that investment, Micron can’t identify a clear point at which supply will catch up because demand continues to grow almost as quickly as manufacturers can expand.
“We’ve said that right now it’ll be beyond 2027, and we don’t see when it closes just because demand continues to grow so fast,” Bhatia said.
Counterpoint doesn’t expect capacity to catch up with demand until late 2027 or early 2028 in the best-case scenario. The market data firm IDC similarly expects the shortage to last through 2027 and well into early 2028 before there is meaningful relief.
PC and smartphone makers can’t absorb component costs that have multiplied several times over indefinitely. They can raise prices. They can make fewer devices. They can put less memory in them. Or they can focus on more expensive devices with enough profit margin to absorb the added cost.
Citing soaring memory costs, Microsoft recently raised Xbox prices by another $100 to $150, leaving some models as much as $300 more expensive than at launch. Microsoft also raised the price of some Surface Pro laptops and tablets by $500 over their original starting price. Meta, meanwhile, added $100 to the cost of its Quest 3 headset.
Apple is perhaps the most revealing test case because it should be among the companies best equipped to withstand the shortage. Its scale gives it extraordinary leverage with suppliers, and its customers have historically proved willing to pay premium prices. Yet Apple has already raised prices across its lineup of Macs and iPads.
Now attention is turning to the iPhone.
Rather than releasing its full lineup at once this fall, Apple is expected to introduce the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max alongside its first foldable iPhone, while holding the standard iPhone 18 and refreshed Air until spring 2027, according to Bloomberg.
Tim Cook described memory pricing as a “100-year flood”
That leaves Apple’s fall lineup concentrated heavily at the most expensive end of the market — exactly where it has the most room to protect its margins. Counterpoint’s supply-chain tracking shows Apple preparing roughly 10 percent more iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units for September through December than it allocated to the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max during the same period last year.
On Apple’s last earnings call, the company forecast slower growth due partly to worsening supply constraints, including for memory chips, and said higher memory costs had directly reduced its gross margin. Then-CEO Tim Cook described memory pricing as a “100-year flood,” citing “exponential increases” that had caused Apple to raise prices.
The iPhone 18 Pro could start at $1,299, according to The Wall Street Journal’s calculation based on estimates from TechInsights that factor in component costs and attempt to minimize margin reductions. That would be $200 more than the iPhone 17 Pro. Samsung and Google have each raised the starting prices of some new phones by $100 this year, though several also come with more storage.
Apple may be better positioned than most companies to pull off higher prices. Its installed base, tightly integrated ecosystem, and loyal customers make its phones behave more like luxury goods than interchangeable electronics. The company has already gained market share by keeping its prices steady while lower-end competitors raised theirs. In places like China, the world’s largest smartphone market, it almost became common sense to opt for a premium iPhone when lower-cost alternatives were selling for nearly as much.
For other manufacturers, the options are worse.
Counterpoint and IDC are already seeing smartphone companies reduce expected shipments while shifting toward more expensive models. If they can’t sell as many phones, they can at least try to extract more revenue from each one.
That means more OLED displays, AI features, larger memory configurations, and other upgrades that can justify higher prices. As a result, revenue for PCs and smartphones could actually remain flat or even rise as unit sales decline.
In other words, AI isn’t just making electronics cost more. The memory shortage is changing which electronics companies bother making in the first place.
Eventually, more supply should arrive.
Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are all investing heavily in additional manufacturing. But because new facilities take years to build, that spending won’t bring immediate relief.
SK Hynix is investing 600 trillion won in its Yongin Semiconductor Cluster, a massive complex south of Seoul first announced in 2019, and has accelerated its target for completion from 2045 to 2033. The company says it will double its capacity within five years but still expects demand to outpace supply through 2030.
Samsung and SK Hynix also plan to invest a combined 800 trillion won, or about $588 billion, in four new memory-chip factories in southwestern South Korea, according to The Wall Street Journal. Micron’s New York and Idaho projects are part of the more than $250 billion it says it will spend on US manufacturing and research through 2035.
A potentially important fourth player is also emerging in China. CXMT is building additional fabs, though its technology isn’t yet considered as advanced as that of Samsung, SK Hynix, or Micron. Apple is currently testing CXMT chips but would need approval from the Trump administration to do business with the company.
The other possibility is that supply won’t have to catch up because demand will collapse first. If the AI investment bubble bursts, memory manufacturers could suddenly find themselves facing very different economics.
For now, that remains hypothetical. The long-term contracts AI companies have signed with memory suppliers make the immediate future easier to predict.
“2027 is pretty locked and loaded,” Naranjo said.
Counterpoint and IDC expect price increases to slow from the breathtaking pace of the past year to single or low double digits. But slower increases aren’t the same as falling prices.
“Not to say prices will come down to 2025 levels, but the price increases will stabilize at a new normal,” Nabila Popal, a senior director at IDC, told The Verge. That new normal is “at least triple what they used to be.”
New fabs still take years to come online, while AI data centers and increasingly sophisticated consumer devices continue to require more memory. And manufacturers have little economic incentive to prioritize cheaper consumer electronics over customers willing to pay handsomely and commit years in advance.
Naranjo’s forecast was blunt.
“It’s not a happy ending anytime soon.”

articles.title: You can now play PS3 games straight from the disc, without owning a PS3
articles.text:
Discs Matter: The team behind RPCS3 has announced another significant milestone for the project. The PlayStation 3 emulator is now a step closer to its original goal: perfectly preserving the entire PS3 library for future scholars and gamers alike.
The RPCS3 team recently unveiled a major upgrade for the emulator: PS3 games can now run directly from their original Blu-ray discs, giving retro gaming enthusiasts a new way to use their physical collections. The developers are billing it as a "plug & play" solution, though users will still need to meet a few mandatory hardware requirements to get it working.
Support for direct disc play was made possible by "digant73" and "Megamouse," the RPCS3 team said. The two developers recently contributed crucial changes to the emulator's codebase, extending on-disc play support to Linux, FreeBSD, and macOS.
The feature was previously available on Windows alone but is now a "universal" option across all supported operating systems. Install times for on-disc packages have been optimized as well.
 – RPCS3 (@rpcs3) September 6, 2026
RPCS3's developers say direct disc support should theoretically extend to physical games released as far back as 20 years ago, with no need to rely on external servers. Users will still need to provide a valid decryption key for their specific disc release and boot from a compatible Blu-ray drive; RPCS3 uses the provided key to decrypt the game's content on the fly.
RPCS3's quickstart guide includes a handy list of working BD drives, which should be capable of reading a PS3 disc's file structure, dumping its contents, and booting the game from within the emulator's UI. Last time I tried, I had no issues extracting and booting an original copy of Demon's Souls through my "UHD Friendly" Asus Blu-ray burner (BW-16D1HT). Now, I should be able to boot the game straight from the disc as well.
RPCS3's developers say a compatible BD drive is a "hard" limitation the emulator won't be able to overcome anytime soon. PS3 games don't use the standard Blu-ray format, so drives need specific MediaTek chipsets to read the discs properly. Many drives use these chipsets, but not all of them do – hence the "official" compatibility list.
The RPCS3 team is positioning direct disc play as a way to get the most out of personal physical game libraries. The timing sends a pointed message to Sony, which recently confirmed it will stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games starting in 2028, shifting the platform toward an all-digital future.
Still, direct on-disc play is another major advancement for an emulator tasked with the once "impossible" goal of emulating the PlayStation 3's Cell multi-core microarchitecture. RPCS3's compatibility rate recently reached a "playable" state for 75% of the entire PS3 library.

articles.title: Samsung Foundry Allocates Half of 4 nm Capacity for HBM4 Base Dies
articles.text:
Monday, September 7th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Samsung Foundry Allocates Half of 4 nm Capacity for HBM4 Base Dies
According to Korean media, Samsung Foundry, a division that operates silicon manufacturing as a subsidiary of Samsung Electronics, is reportedly allocating significant capacity for HBM4 base die manufacturing. For HBM4, Samsung is producing the base die on a 4 nm node, which reportedly receives half of the entire manufacturing capacity of the 4 nm node, internally referred to as SF4. Customers of HBM4 and the upcoming HBM4E memory standards are now requesting base dies to be filled with custom logic. For instance, customers could implement custom logic like memory controllers and PHYs directly on the HBM base die, significantly reducing the area occupied by these components on the main compute chiplet.
Samsung operates its SF4 manufacturing at Pyeongtaek Campus 2 (P2) and Campus 3 (P3) on lines S5 and S6. An increase in manufacturing is not only coming for ASIC designs by external customers but also for HBM4 base die manufacturing, which is becoming especially important for ASIC customers aiming to maximize the performance of their designs.With its HBM manufacturing business, Samsung is capturing a significant volume from buyers. In Q2 2026, Samsung secured 38% of the HBM market share by revenue, a notable increase from just a year ago when the company held 15%. Meanwhile, SK hynix's share has decreased from 64% in Q2 2025 to 50% in Q2 2026, as many customers have diversified and started sourcing their HBM from Samsung. With more offerings like custom base dies and capacity expansions, Samsung could capture even greater revenue share in the coming quarters if the foundry business continues to perform well.

articles.title: Dyson has a whole new fan style, and it's straight out of Arrakis
articles.text:
Dyson's new fans look like a Dune sandworm in appliance form — but they're so powerful you'll forget all about that when you switch them on
A world away from the sleek loop fans Dyson is known for
- Dyson has launched three new fan-purifiers, all with star-shaped nozzles
- The nozzle is designed to be both powerful and very quiet
- I saw them in action, and they're super-effective... but the styling will be divisive
Dyson's loop fans are instantly recognizable. In the home appliance world, their sleek, bladeless design has gained somewhat iconic status. But now we are about to enter a new Dyson fan era — and the design could not be more different to those sleek loops. With their chunky, curving bodies topped with a gaping, star-shaped opening, the new Dyson HushJet fan-purifiers remind me of nothing more than the giant sandworms in the new Dune films.
I perhaps should have seen it coming. Dyson debuted the new look with the HushJet Purifier Compact in September 2025, and it's also used for the HushJet Mini Cool personal fan. But when I saw the new, full-sized range on show in Berlin last week (at Dyson's IFA 2026-adjacent event) I was momentarily stunned.
Both of the previous HushJet fans were compact gadgets, and there was something about seeing the design scaled up — to quite gigantic proportions, in the case of the largest options — that made it feel significantly more unsettling.
The star nozzle draws inspiration from aviation engineering. I spoke to a Dyson engineer about it last year, and she explained the shape was especially good at minimizing the turbulence in the airflow, to create a quiet yet powerful jet of air.
I got to try the new fans out, and I was blown away — pun intended — by how powerful they were. When it came to blasting air, they felt significantly more effective than the loop-style Dyson fans I've used. So while I wasn't immediately sold on the styling, I had no complaints about the effectiveness of the airflow. I'd very happily have one of these in my bedroom over the summer, regardless of the fact it wouldn't blend in at all.
Double-duty
Like most of Dyson's fan models, the HushJets are pulling double- or even triple-duty. They operate as air purifiers, too, and one can also be used as a heater. At the top of the range is the Dyson HushJet Big+Quiet Cool Pure+ Formaldehyde air purifier (and kudos to the Dyson engineer I spoke to, who managed to remember that name without having to check his notes).
The purification capabilities are the most advanced of any of the new models, with the ability to capture a huge range of pollutants, including formaldehyde, and shift a massive amount of air, very quickly. It's around the same diameter as the Dyson Purifier Big+Quiet — ie really very chunky. It's designed for use in large spaces like offices, but it can also be used to clean multiple rooms in a home.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
There are also a couple of medium-sized options, built for at-home use. These are the HushJet Pure Cool+ Formaldehyde, and the HushJet Hot Cool Pure+ air purifier, which loses the formaldehyde-capturing capabilities but can be used as a heater over the colder months.
I have no doubt the new-look design will end up being divisive — I think the quirky styling might fit more naturally in an office or commercial setup than it would in a living room, where it'd surely stick out like a sore thumb in many cases. When I asked the Dyson rep if the plan was for the HushJet range to eventually replace the loops, he suggested perhaps not, given how instantly recognizable the loops are as Dyson appliances. I'll be watching with interest.
Pricing and availability
Pricing is as follows: the medium-sized HushJet Pure Cool+ Formaldehyde will cost $599 / £549.99 / AU$999, and the medium-sized HushJet Hot Cool Pure+ air purifier will be $599 / £549.99 / AU TBC. The large HushJet Big+Quiet Cool Pure+ Formaldehyde will come in at $1,099 / £899.99 / AU TBC.
In the US, all three will go on sale in fall 2026. In the UK, the large and medium Formaldehyde options will launch in October and the heater option will arrive in December. In Australia, it's October 2026 for the Cool Pure+ Formaldehyde and "early 2027" for the other two.

articles.title: RPCS3 emulator can now run PS3 games on PC directly from a disc drive in landmark development — unlocks 20 years of physical titles on Windows, Linux, and macOS
articles.text:
RPCS3 emulator can now run PS3 games on PC directly from a disc drive in landmark development — unlocks 20 years of physical titles on Windows, Linux, and macOS
Test-run games without dumping them to your precious SSD. Less friction more fun.
The developers of the Sony PlayStation 3 emulator RPCS3 have told their social media followers that it is now possible to play games straight from discs. As announced on Twitter/X, the emulator’s latest refinement works only with certain internal and external Blu-ray drives. Happily for retro gamers, there’s a lengthy compatibility list of drives featuring many models and brands, and the same drives are also compatible with dumping your media to fixed storage.
Above you can see the RPCS3 devs are pretty happy with the slick new “plug and play” refinements that are available to users of the latest version of the emulator. “You can now play your PS3 games on PC... DIRECTLY FROM THE DISC DRIVE!” boast the open source emulator programmers. “PLUG AND PLAY! Owning your games as physical media allows you to play games released as far back as 20 years ago without relying on any servers!” The RPCS3 team thanks digant73 and Megamouse, specifically, for contributions making this feat possible.
Indeed, this is another step forward in making a slick emulator that works in a surprisingly frictionless fashion. Though the Tweet mentions PC, specifically, extended disc drive play support is also available on Linux, FreeBSD, and macOS. You just need to check that drive compatibility list. Moreover, all users can enjoy “optimized install times for package installations from the disc drive.” It has also been confirmed that PS4 and PS5 console users with Linux installs can launch PS3 games directly from disc using RPCS3.
Here’s a quick tip for folks who have an obscure Blu-ray drive that isn’t in the list. If you want to confirm compatibility with the drive, just put a PS3 disc in it. If you can browse its files, it's compatible; if nothing shows up, then it's not.
With pricing for the best SSDs now sky-high, being able to test-run new (old) games before dumping them to fixed storage could be a boon. It might also be good for auditioning a batch of discs you have recently bought, to see which ones are keepers.

articles.title: Bentley’s Torcal EV tries to balance authenticity with fake V8 sounds
articles.text:
Thanks to their ability to provide a smooth ride and quiet powertrain with ease, electric vehicles are a true shoo-in for the high-end luxury automotive segment. Rolls-Royce has the Spectre, Cadillac’s Celestiq is taking bespoke to a whole new level, and Mercedes has given the EQS the full Maybach treatment. From Volkswagen Auto Group, Bentley is just about to debut its 2027 Torcal, a spacious SUV that shares a platform with the electrified Porsche Cayenne.
Bentley’s Torcal EV tries to balance authenticity with fake V8 sounds
The British automaker is on the hunt for a new demographic with its first electric vehicle.
I recently got a quick ride in a heavily camouflaged preproduction Torcal as a way to experience it before its official debut toward the end of this month. Between this brute’s spacious interior, supple ride quality, and focus on craftsmanship in the digital age, all signs point to it not just being a viable competitor in the segment, but also characteristically Bentley.
When I say heavily camouflaged, this not only covers (pun intended) the Torcal’s exterior, but the interior as well. Thick black cloth was draped over most of it, to the point of the engineers punching holes in the cloth for proper seatbelt usage. The exterior was rather deceiving, too; apparently they affixed false body paneling under the wrap so as not to fully spoil its overall shape and profile. Upon first glance, it seemed like Bentley took a page from Lucid’s Gravity by making it wider at the front than at the back—in the name of teardrop-resembling aerodynamics—but Martin Page, the Torcal’s product line director-slash-chauffeur for my ride, assured me that what I was seeing (or rather, trying to see) wouldn’t be production.
However, this enabled me to zero in closer on what I could feel and hear. Whether up front or in back, the Torcal is amply spacious, even though it’s noticeably smaller in size and shape than Bentley’s current Bentayga. Page explained the great lengths that engineers reached to ensure it had an isolating and tremendously smooth ride. Running off-the-shelf two-chamber air suspension — common in the rest of the brand’s lineup — would seemingly suffice with an EV’s inherently good chassis balance, but engineers took it a step further by carefully altering the flow of oil through its adaptive dampers. This means that the jump in ride and handling between Comfort and Sport modes is much more discernible. No matter the mode, it rode incredibly smoothly. Heavy focus was paid to the Torcal’s alignment, too, with steering that returns to and maintains center as confidently as possible.
Diving deeper into signature Bentley characteristics, developing the best simulated engine note was high on the list of priorities. Inspiration came from the brand’s V8-powered Turbo R of the 1980s, except the track itself was recorded by a musician’s drum beat and mixed accordingly, rather than simply churned out from a synthesizer.
“What we wanted to do throughout the car is maintain craftsmanship, not only in the materials but also in the way we execute the digital aspects,” Page shared.
“What we wanted to do throughout the car is maintain craftsmanship, not only in the materials but also in the way we execute the digital aspects.”
— Martin Page, Torcal’s product line director
The reasoning behind this lies in hearing subtle imperfections, much like one would from an analogue internal combustion powertrain. Going one step further, the Torcal’s throttle tuning seemed to mimic a torquey V8 with progressive power delivery. In light of this, Page added that with this sound turned on, it gives occupants auditory cues to tie to the vehicle’s torque delivery, which is known to help reduce motion sickness. The sound has not yet been finalized and is still being finely tweaked at the time of this writing.
I got a peek at the digital instrument cluster and center infotainment screen — Page had to observe the speed limit, after all. The image these display in the background is of a fine crystal decanter hand-cut by Cumbria Crystal with light shone through it. In Page’s words, this shows the natural refractions and reflections that you get from every one of the cuts. It’s another indication of the brand’s focus on craftsmanship in the digital age, albeit a subtle one.
It’s also worth pointing out that Bentley takes net environmental impact seriously. “In this car we take sustainability to another level, we have clear targets for circular material and green aluminum,” Page shared. “The door cards are made with a natural fiber — not injection-molded plastic — that’s fully recyclable and fully sustainable.”
Then, Bentley is working with fellow UK company Fox Brothers to offer a Merino wool interior option, not just as a lesser-taken route for comfort (Volvo’s done well with wool, too) but also as a sturdy, renewable material that will hold up to automotive use. Finally, the assembly plant in Crewe, England, has tough requirements for green energy use (namely solar) and other renewable practices.
Output, battery, and charging specs are not carved into stone just yet. Power will be north of 800 hp and 700 lb ft of torque, and curb weight is estimated to be nearly 6,000 lbs. Page was quiet about battery size (though, expect it to mirror the Porsche’s 108 net kWh unit), and the targeted range is over 370 miles. With a peak charging rate of 400 kW, the brand is aiming for a 10–80 percent top-up in under 20 minutes, with 100 miles tacking on in as little as seven.
“We’re trying to be authentic in the whole experience,” Page summed up as we headed back to the parking lot where I met him.
The approach with the Torcal is to make a great Bentley first, and in the process of doing so, a great EV. It combines some already hashed-out tech from Volkswagen, but the brand is hoping its focus on craftsmanship and fine-tuning will attract discerning, well-heeled potential customers who want an electric luxury vehicle. Pricing hasn’t been announced yet, but it will be interesting to see how the Torcal is received after its full official unveiling.
Images by Bentley

articles.title: Kioxia's Flash-for-DRAM Initiative Eyes AI Workloads - EE Times
articles.text:
Kioxia has moved one step closer to its ambitious goal of replacing DRAM with flash for some memory content serving AI workloads. It presented a Compute Express Link (CXL) module at a briefing in Tokyo; the module is built around XL-Flash, a specialized NAND chip with sharply improved processing speeds.
This CXL module—aimed at replacing part of DRAM content alongside AI compute—uses NAND flash optimized for high-speed processing. Kioxia claims that replacing some DRAM with CXL modules can double memory capacity at the same cost while improving performance by 30%.
CXL—an interface standard that ties together different memory types and devices inside a system into a single large memory space—allows capacity to be allocated dynamically as needed. As a result, a NAND-based CXL module is cost-competitive against DRAM. While DRAM reads data extremely fast, it is difficult to expand in capacity and is more expensive.
On the other hand, cheaper NAND-based CXL enables an ultra-large memory pool at a lower cost than a DRAM-only configuration. Here, substituting NAND for DRAM in certain AI workloads hinges on evolving system architectures that can tolerate higher latency in exchange for greater density and lower cost per bit.
Flash window of opportunity
NAND flash offers substantially more storage capacity at a given price point, but its access speeds are measured in microseconds rather than DRAM’s nanoseconds. However, emerging applications in data center tiering and edge AI now provide new openings for systems designed to manage mixed-latency storage hierarchies.
These systems can route less time-sensitive operations to flash-based memory while reserving DRAM for performance-critical tasks. Consider machine learning model inference in data center environments, where latency may not matter much unless it’s more than an order of magnitude worse than high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
Next, in edge AI, which commonly employs pre-trained models, Kioxia said its CXL module aligns with NAND’s advantage of large capacity. It’s also immune to NAND’s weaknesses of slow writes and limited endurance, and its low-power consumption suits energy-sensitive edge environments.
At this memory-technology crossroads, a CXL module can boost NAND flash memory processing speeds as part of the initiative to replace some DRAM demand in AI servers. Consequently, if NAND can absorb some DRAM capacity in data center servers and emerging applications such as edge AI, the addressable market for flash widens at the expense of DRAM chips.
Nevertheless, Kioxia’s flash-for-DRAM initiative is a supplementary strategy rather than a core design initiative. It heeds specialized NAND applications that can offset the absence of DRAM. But the question is: why Kioxia?
Kioxia’s memory imperative
Unlike other top-tier memory producers—Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix—Kioxia lacks a DRAM portfolio. That leaves the Japanese memory chipmaker exposed in a market where its key rivals can leverage both DRAM and flash memory technologies. In other words, Kioxia’s singular focus on NAND flash has become a liability.
Moreover, within the NAND flash space, China’s Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. (YMTC) is narrowing the multi-year technology gap in a matter of months. That especially threatens Kioxia’s position in price-sensitive memory segments. Then there is Micron, which has regained momentum in the NAND flash market after a difficult stretch spanning many years.
Such competitive pressures have left Kioxia searching for strategic differentiation. Here, it must extract value from its existing NAND capabilities through novel initiatives: enter the NAND-based CXL module to replace some DRAM demand. But that’s only half of the story.
In NAND-based CXL module design, while technical tradeoffs are well understood, implementation requires software stacks and system designs that exploit the cost-density advantages while managing latency penalties. That, in turn, calls for ecosystem support from server manufacturers, hyperscalers, and software vendors.
Without design wins and ecosystem support, it will remain a forward-looking statement regarding memory architecture rather than a memory industry breakthrough. Therefore, industry watchers are keenly awaiting design win announcements from Kioxia; they will validate the technical premise of NAND substitution in memory-intensive AI workloads.
Until then, Kioxia carving out a middle path to position flash as a tier between DRAM and storage will remain a work in progress. While the technical details of this unlaunched module are making waves in the memory world, flash as a DRAM proxy must open a differentiated revenue stream to become a persistent HBM twin.

NAND Flash’s Reversal of Fortune Amid the AI Boom
From GPUs to Memory Pools: Why AI Needs Compute Express Link (CXL)

articles.title: Erdrutsche am Berg: 166 Gletscher-Sensoren sollen in der Schweiz helfen
articles.text:
Nach der Sturzflut im Himalaya: Welche Warnsysteme gibt es in Europa vor dieser Naturgefahr?
Die verheerende Sturzflut im Himalaya vom 26. August 2026 führte eindrücklich vor Augen, welche zerstörerische Kraft von sogenannten gekoppelten Naturgefahren ausgeht. Das sind gefährliche Kettenreaktion, bei der ein Ereignis das nächste auslöst.
Sturzflut von mehr als 1.000 Höhenmetern im Himalaya
An der Nordflanke des Langtang-Lirung-Bergmassivs brach an dem Tag eine gewaltige Masse aus Fels und Eis ab. Vorläufige Schätzungen reichen von rund 100 Millionen bis zu 200 Millionen Kubikmetern. Die Massen stürzten zunächst mehr als 1.000 Höhenmeter ab, erodierten die Flanken des Tals und wurden zu einem rasenden Strom aus Eis, Wasser, Schlamm und Geröll. Mit einer Geschwindigkeit von bis zu 180 Kilometern pro Stunde überspülte der Schlammstrom in weniger als 10 Minuten den 22 Kilometer entfernten Grenzposten Gyirong und breitete sich von dort weiter aus.

 Points forts
- Autonomie longue durée.
- Nouveau format qui rafraîchit la gamme Fold.
- Écrans très lumineux.
- Charge à 45 W.
Points faibles
- Absence de Flex Mode.
- Pas de téléobjectif.
Le Galaxy Z Fold 8 apporte un souffle nouveau à une gamme Samsung Fold qui commençait sérieusement à s'encroûter. Son format passeport, presque carré, lui confère une ergonomie nouvelle, lui permet de jouer les liseuses, d'être rangé plus facilement dans une poche et presque de se laisser confondre avec un smartphone monobloc traditionnel. Il a bien peu de défauts à son actif : sa batterie au silicium-carbone lui octroie une très bonne endurance, il se charge assez rapidement, il se montre puissant et ses écrans, qui mériteraient sans doute une calibration plus pointue, sont très lumineux et font la chasse aux reflets. Il ne lui manque qu'un volet photo plus généreux, avec un téléobjectif, pour répondre pleinement aux attentes que fait naître son positionnement tarifaire.

 Plus fin, plus puissant mais également plus cher, le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra profite de deux écrans très lumineux, d’une pliure discrète, d’un volet photo polyvalent, de performances remarquables et d’un multitâche maîtrisé. Son autonomie solide, sa charge améliorée et son suivi logiciel longue durée renforcent encore l’ensemble. Quelques limites subsistent, notamment l’absence de S Pen, une étanchéité perfectible et quelques logiciels préinstallés. Une évolution très aboutie, davantage fondée sur le perfectionnement que sur la révolution, réservée au nouveau format de son petit frère.

articles.title: Séisme chez Volkswagen : 100 000 suppressions de postes et la moitié des modèles rayés de la carte
articles.text:
La crise traversant l’industrie automobile met à rude épreuve les constructeurs. Même ceux qui étaient historiquement les plus solides sont aujourd’hui menacés. C’est le cas de Volkswagen, qui entend mener une vague de licenciements sans précédent, avec 100 000 emplois en moins d’ici 2030. Le but est de limiter la casse face à une baisse anticipée des ventes en Chine et aux États-Unis.
Certains qualifieront certainement cette mesure de véritable casse sociale. Oliver Blume, le PDG du groupe Volkswagen, ne pouvait rester la bouche cousue face à de tels choix. Dans une interview accordée à Auto Express, il explique ainsi que sa marque assume « pleinement [sa] responsabilité envers l’ensemble de [ses] collaborateurs, [ses] partenaires et l’emploi industriel dans le monde entier ».
La moitié du catalogue sacrifiée pour sauver les meubles
Avant d’ajouter qu’ « au cours des prochaines années, nous investirons plusieurs centaines de milliards d’euros pour rendre nos marques emblématiques encore plus attractives, plus fortes et plus compétitives ». Vu le contexte actuel, l’objectif est pour le moins ambitieux, avec une marge opérationnelle de 9 % et un bénéfice annuel de 31 milliards d’euros d’ici 2030. Un tel fil rouge ne peut mener qu’à des décisions difficiles dans l’immédiat.
Outre la suppression de 50 000 postes supplémentaires en plus des 50 000 initialement prévus depuis 2024, c’est une importante réduction des gammes qui aura lieu. Volkswagen compte en ce sens rayer de son catalogue la moitié de ses modèles. Rien que ça ! Et en bonus, les gammes seront simplifiées de 75 %, ce qui signifie qu’il y aura moins de versions disponibles pour chaque modèle. L’objectif est bien entendu une rationalisation menant aux économies.
Quels sont les modèles et les marques sur la sellette ?
Cela se voit d’ores et déjà avec la disparition de modèles à faibles volumes comme la Volkswagen Jetta, la Porsche Taycan Sport Turismo et les Audi A1 et Q2. Les ventes des deux premiers véhicules faiblissaient à vue d’œil alors que celles des deux derniers ne dégageaient plus une marge suffisante. Le but est de revenir aux véhicules les plus porteurs, ce qui « profitera davantage au client ». On veut bien l’entendre, même si les raisons sont ailleurs…
Outre des modèles, ce sont carrément des marques entières qui pourraient disparaître. Même si aucune décision n’a encore été prise, Seat a des chances de ne pas passer la prochaine décennie. Cupra, qui dégage déjà de meilleurs bénéfices avec des produits plus attractifs, prendrait alors le relais. Le groupe reverra en parallèle ses objectifs de production à la baisse, avec 9 millions de véhicules d’ici 2030, contre près de 12 millions aujourd’hui.

articles.title: Dyson unveils new range of robot vacuums, air purifiers, floor cleaners and hair care products - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Dyson has unveiled a range of products incorporating advanced intelligence to deliver a new level of performance including a new robot vacuums, air purifiers, floor cleaners and hair dryers and straighteners.
DYSON R3 ROBOT NUROVI SPOT AND SCRUB UV – TBC
The Dyson R3 NUROVI Spot and Scrub UV can detect stains by using UV light, AI vision, and green laser illumination.
You can identify around 200 types of household substances and objects and will clean repeatedly until those stains are gone.
It has 30,000 PA and 65% more suction pressure for powerful cleaning across both hard floors and carpets.
It is set for release in early 2027.
DYSON R2 NUROVIA WASH AND DRY – $1,449
The Dyson R2 debuts the new Dyson Reuleaux triangle pads, which maintain constant width and contact to get right into the corners.
This way the vacuum maximises edge and corner contact for improved coverage.
The cleaning is enhanced with 75-degree Celsius water heated at the dock, which helps with the removal of stubborn stains.
DYSON R1 NUROVI DRY – $949
This has the same twin capture technology as the R2, with 21,000 Pa suction, and shares the same side sweeper system with a webbed connector that controls the pressure and direction of the brushes.
DYSON W1 PENCIL WASH – TBC
Dyson’s floor care range now includes the W1 Pencil Wash, which has been upgraded to add a more absorbent roller and hygienic wash system.
It also has self-cleaning technology on the charging dock and maintains the same light and slim design for easy use to achieve maximum cleaning convenience.
It will be available in early 2027.
DYSON HUSHJET BIG AND QUIET PURE+ FORMALDEHYDE AIR PURIFIER – TBC
The largest model in the range and the most powerful purifier Dyson has produced, the HushJet Big and Quiet Cool Pure+ Formaldehyde air purifier can clean rooms quickly and project purified air up to 20m.
The HushJet nozzle drew its inspiration from aviation and applies aerospace principles to control airflow in the home.
Due for release in early 2027.
DYSON HUSHJET COOL PURE+ FORMALDEHYDE AIR PURIFIER – $999
This delivers powerful Purification but has a more compact format yet can still handle large spaces quickly without the need to step up to a full-scale system.
The Dyson HushJet Pure Cool+ Formaldehyde air purifier offers up to 3x more powerful purification than its predecessors.
It can project air far into the room for improved purification while cooling at the same time.
Will be available in October.
DYSON HUSHJET HOT COOL PURE+ AIR PURIFIER – TBC
This is a powerful three-in-one purifier that brings purification, along with heating and personal cooling, in one product.
It is designed to offer comfort year-round and can be used in spaces where thermal comfort and air quality need to work closely together.
Due for release in early 2027.
DYSON CORRALE COOLSHINE STRAIGHTENER – $499
The Dyson Corral Cool Shine straightener has reimagined hot plate styling and changes the way hair is straightened, shaped, and finished.
It has precision heat control, flexing plates, and active cooling to deliver glossy, sleek, and straight results with less heat damage.
DYSON AIRSMOOTH HOT BRUSH – $399
This is Dyson’s first dedicated hot air brush that has been designed to simplify everyday styling routines while still delivering stunning results.
The product incorporates Dyson’s pioneering airflow technology with Pivot Flex and anti-snag bristle technology, which allows users to style with ease and help create a natural blowout across all hair types.

articles.title: Hackers exploit new MikroTik RouterOS flaws to hijack routers
articles.text:
Hackers are exploiting a chain of two recently disclosed vulnerabilities in MikroTik routers to take control of devices with SSH services exposed to the internet.
One of the security issues, tracked as CVE-2026-67276, is an SSH authentication bypass flaw in MikroTik RouterOS caused by incomplete validation of RSA public keys.
An attacker who knows a username and the public modulus of that user’s key can exploit it by crafting a different key and logging in without the legitimate private key.
The second security issue is identified as CVE-2026-86060. It is an SSH privilege escalation flaw in MikroTik RouterOS due to improper handling of specially crafted usernames.
Hackers can leverage it using a specially crafted username to manipulate the SSH session so that the attacker obtains full administrative privileges.
Both vulnerabilities were discovered by Poland's CERT agency with the help of GPT-5.5-cyber and GPT-5.6-sol and received a critical severity rating.
The Polish agency dubbed the exploit chain “MikroTrick,” and warned that it is now actively exploited in the wild.
“In recent days we have been observing attacks against RouterOS devices accessible from the internet,” Poland's CERT warns.
“We have obtained confirmation that the attackers are exploiting this combination of vulnerabilities to take full control of devices whose SSH service is accessible from public networks.”
The Polish CERT also highlighted a third flaw, CVE-2026-67277, which affects the RouterOS bandwidth-test service and allows unauthenticated attackers to leak kernel memory or to remotely crash/restart the router.
MikroTik fixed the vulnerabilities in RouterOS 7.25beta3, 7.24.2, 7.23.4, and 6.49.21, released on September 3, and Poland's CERT validated the fixes.
In its advisory, the vendor notes that not all configurations are affected, but did not disclose any details to give users time to apply the security updates.
The updates add a compromise-detection mechanism to the routers that looks for known signs of unauthorized configuration changes at startup, disables malicious entries, and logs a critical warning.
However, the CERT notes that the absence of a marker indicating compromise should not be taken as a guarantee that a router has not been compromised.
The CERT shared the following indicators of compromise (IoCs):
- Log entries: ‘login failure for user -2 from <ip> via ssh’ and ‘user <name> added by ssh:-2@<ip>’
- Presence of a highly privileged ops account
- 82.192.72.4 — linked to confirmed successful attacks
- 103.102.31.18 — observed attempting to exploit MikroTrick
If compromise is suspected, the Polish agency recommends isolating the router, preserving logs and configuration, then factory-resetting the device and rebuilding it from a trusted configuration while rotating passwords, keys, and other secrets.
For those unable to apply the updates immediately, one recommendation is to restrict or disable externally accessible SSH, WWW/WWW-SSL, and bandwidth-test services, and avoid the built-in SSH clients and outbound TLS connections over untrusted networks.
As of September 5, there were 122,500 MikroTik devices with an exposed SSH interface, according to data provided by The ShadowServer Foundation. The exact number of devices vulnerable the MikroTik exploit was not determined, though.

articles.title: Les French Days démarrent fort : voici les premières promos qui nous font hésiter à sortir la carte
articles.text:
La rentrée a beau être derrière nous, il reste parfois quelques lignes sur la liste des fournitures. Surtout celles à plusieurs centaines d’euros, qu’on avait prudemment laissées pour « le mois prochain ». Les French Days peuvent justement donner un coup de pouce pour boucler ces achats. Du 7 au 14 septembre 2026, Numerama fait le tri ici des meilleures affaires repérées en ligne chez tous les marchands participants (Fnac, Darty, Boulanger, Amazon, Cdiscount et bien d’autres…).
Gardez ce live sous le coude, dans vos favoris par exemple ! On l’alimente tout au long des French Days. Certaines offres risquent de filer entre deux visites, mais on continue de fouiller pour vous en dénicher d’autres.
Les meilleures promos des French Days
Le vélo électrique Hercules Urbanico GR I-11
Un gravel électrique avec une transmission Shimano GRX à 11 vitesses et des freins à disque hydrauliques à 1 199 €, voilà une offre qui mérite qu’on s’y attarde. Cet Hercules Urbanico GR I-11 chez Upway affiche moins de 5 km au compteur, avec quelques marques extérieures signalées par le mécanicien.
C’est aussi bien un vélo pour aller travailler puis quitter le bitume pour une balade, avec des pneus Schwalbe de 50 mm de large et un porte-bagages. Le moteur arrière Bafang de 30 Nm convient davantage aux parcours plats ou vallonnés qu’aux fortes côtes. Il pèse 24 kg et sa batterie de 410 Wh n’est pas amovible, il faut donc pouvoir brancher le vélo là où vous le rangez. Enfin, cet exemplaire est en taille L, conseillé par Upway pour un gabarit de 1,75 à 1,90 m.
Smartphone Google Pixel 10a
Le Pixel 10a avait un problème à sa sortie en mars : Google demandait 549 € pour un téléphone presque identique au Pixel 9a, qu’on trouvait alors autour de 350 €. Difficile de vous conseiller de payer 200 € de plus. À 389 € sur Amazon en version 128 Go, l’écart avec ce tarif du 9a se réduit à une quarantaine d’euros, et les petites améliorations du nouveau modèle deviennent plus défendables.
On retrouve un smartphone avec un très bon rapport qualité-prix avec un verre de protection plus résistant, un écran plus lumineux et un bloc photo entièrement plat, qui évite au téléphone de basculer quand on le pose sur une table. C’est un très bon photophone avec un excellent traitement logiciel des photo.
Aspirateur robot Narwal Flow
Si Narwal ne vous dit pas encore grand-chose, c’est aussi parce que la marque n’est arrivée en France qu’à l’été 2024, alors qu’elle comptait déjà parmi les grands noms du secteur en Chine. Le Flow, lancé chez nous en septembre 2025, appartient à cette première phase de développement et il tombe en promo à 664 € au lieu de 799 €.
Depuis, le Flow 2 et, plus récemment, le Freo 20, auquel nous avons attribué 8/10 dans notre test, ont rejoint le catalogue. Une marque qu’on suit donc de près, notamment pour son efficacité en lavage. C’est justement ce qui fait encore l’intérêt du premier Flow : sa serpillière à chenille est rincée à l’eau chaude à 45 °C et raclée en continu, pendant que le robot avance. Elle frotte le sol tout en évacuant les saletés, au lieu de les transporter jusqu’au prochain passage à la station. Ce système réussit assez bien sur les taches tenaces, là où les patins humides atteignent vite leurs limites. Si vous avez surtout du carrelage à nettoyer, c’est un modèle vraiment efficace avec une application intuitive.
TV Samsung OLED TQ55S92H
Le Samsung S92H fait partie de la nouvelle gamme OLED 2026. Lancé en mai à 1 999 € en 55 pouces (140 cm), ce successeur du S90F devient déjà bien plus accessible : la Fnac le propose à 1 599 € sans carte, ou 1 439,10 € pour les adhérents.
Samsung a changé un élément important sur la gamme cette année : ce 55 pouces utilise une dalle WOLED de LG Display, alors que son prédécesseur était équipé en QD-OLED. Son nouvel argument reste toutefois le filtre Glare Free pour se démarquer de son concurrent historique sur le segment. Ce filtre atténue fortement les reflets des fenêtres et des lampes. C’est utile pour regarder un film sans devoir systématiquement fermer les rideaux. Les joueurs retrouvent aussi quatre HDMI 2.1 et jusqu’à 165 Hz sur PC compatible. En revanche, Samsung persiste à se passer du Dolby Vision : les films concernés restent lisibles en HDR10, mais sans les ajustements d’image propres à ce format.
Forfaits 5G Cdiscount (50 € offerts en bon d’achat)
50 € en bon d’achat pour changer de forfait, c’est l’offre de Cdiscount Mobile pendant les French Days. Deux formules retiennent notre attention : 100 Go à 9,99 €/mois, avec 25 Go en Europe et dans les DOM, ou 200 Go à 12,99 €/mois.
Les deux sont sans engagement, sur le réseau 5G de Bouygues Telecom, avec une carte SIM à 1 €. Si vous avez du Wi-Fi à la maison et au travail, les 100 Go devraient déjà laisser une bonne marge. Le vrai argument pour dépenser 3 € de plus, ce sont surtout les 35 Go utilisables en 4G dans 164 destinations, dont les États-Unis, le Japon et le Maroc. De quoi éviter d’acheter une SIM de voyage pour ces séjours, souvent très couteuse. Attention, les appels classiques ne deviennent pas pour autant illimités dans tous ces pays.
Batterie externe Ugreen MagFlow Pro
Du refroidissement liquide dans une batterie externe, c’est la nouveauté qu’Ugreen vient de présenter à l’IFA cette année. La MagFlow Pro intègre une micropompe qui fait circuler un liquide pour évacuer la chaleur produite pendant la recharge sans fil. L’intérêt est bien là : quand ça chauffe trop, la recharge ralentit. Ce système doit donc aider à maintenir une puissance élevée plus longtemps, plutôt que d’afficher 25 W sur la boîte pour les perdre après quelques minutes. Tout juste sortie, elle passe à 105,99 € au lieu de 129,99 € sur le site Ugreen avec le code DL65062.
Cette dernière se fixe au dos d’un téléphone compatible et délivre jusqu’à 25 W sans fil en Qi2, ou 45 W avec son câble USB-C intégré. Un petit écran indique même la puissance réellement délivrée, en plus du niveau de batterie. Cela reste cher pour 10 000 mAh : on paie surtout le confort de la recharge magnétique et ce nouveau refroidissement.
Moniteur PC MSI MAG OLED (27″)
À 334,99 € au lieu de 399,99 € avec le code COCORICO15, ce MSI MAG 274QP QD-OLED X24 donne une bonne raison de remplacer un ancien écran LCD. Le passage à l’OLED prend tout son intérêt dans un jeu comme Resident Evil Requiem, noté 9/10 dans nos colonnes : les noirs profonds, sans le voile gris d’un écran LCD, rendent l’exploration des couloirs sombres encore moins rassurante. Sur ses 26,5 pouces, la définition QHD offre une image fine tout en demandant moins de puissance à votre carte graphique que la 4K. Les 240 Hz intéresseront surtout les amateurs de jeux compétitifs.
La luminosité annoncée se limite à 200 nits en SDR et 400 nits en pointe HDR. Mieux vaut donc l’installer à l’écart d’une fenêtre, et ne pas attendre les effets lumineux des OLED plus haut de gamme.
Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro
À 129 € après remboursement, contre 249 € au lancement, les Galaxy Buds 4 Pro deviennent particulièrement intéressants pour accompagner un smartphone Samsung. Pour arriver à ce prix il suffit de passer sur Amazon, vous payez 179 € à la commande, puis récupérez 50 € après l’achat en remplissant le formulaire de remboursement Samsung avant le 29 novembre. Pensez à vérifier que les écouteurs sont bien vendus par Amazon (les vendeurs tiers de la marketplace sont exclus de l’opération).
Que dire sur ce modèle si ce n’est que Samsung conserve une recette qui fonctionne assez bien à un prix plus accessible que son concurrent Apple. Chaque écouteur dispose de deux haut-parleurs, l’un pour les graves et l’autre pour les aigus, avec un haut-parleur de basses agrandi sur cette génération. La réduction de bruit s’ajuste également à votre environnement et à la façon dont les écouteurs sont placés dans vos oreilles. Côté autonomie, Samsung annonce toujours six heures avec la réduction de bruit activée, et 26 heures en comptant les recharges du boîtier.
Console de jeu rétro NEOGEO AES+
Avec les 64 Ko de RAM principale de la NEOGEO d’origine, dont elle reprend l’architecture, cette AES+ ne devrait pas vider les stocks de mémoire à elle seule. Attendue le 12 novembre prochain, elle profite déjà d’une nouvelle promotion : 183,99 € au lieu de 199,99 € sur Cdiscount avec le code COCORICO15.
L’intérêt de cette AES+, c’est de pouvoir ressortir ses anciennes cartouches NEOGEO AES et y jouer sur un téléviseur actuel grâce à la sortie HDMI. SNK et Plaion ont reproduit le matériel d’origine avec de nouvelles puces dédiées, et fournissent même un stick arcade filaire au format de celui de l’époque. De quoi intéresser les amateurs d’arcade qui veulent retrouver la machine et ses commandes, jusque dans leurs dimensions. Attention toutefois, aucun jeu n’est inclus dans cette édition : il faudra posséder des cartouches compatibles ou acheter les rééditions prévues pour l’accompagner.
Trotinette électrique Navee GT3 Pro
Pour les French Days, la Navee GT3 Pro tombe à 369 € contre 579 € à son lancement. À ce prix, elle devient intéressante si vous cherchez une trottinette pour aller travailler sans trop sacrifier le confort. Elle dispose notamment de suspensions à l’avant et à l’arrière, associées à de grands pneus de 10 pouces tubeless (pour éviter les crevaisons). Et si vous ne connaissez pas encore Navee, la marque fait désormais partie de Dreame Group, le groupe derrière les aspirateurs robots Dreame.
Le moteur de 400 W, capable d’atteindre ponctuellement 1 000 W, lui donne aussi de quoi aborder les montées. On apprécie la présence de clignotants et la compatibilité avec Localiser d’Apple, même si le point à regarder avant de l’acheter reste son poids : 22 kg, qu’il faudra bien porter si vous avez des escaliers. Attention également aux 60 km d’autonomie affichés : ils sont calculés à 15 km/h. À 25 km/h, Navee annonce plutôt 45 km dans ses conditions de test, et votre parcours ou votre gabarit peuvent encore réduire cette distance.
Deux sets LEGO Pokémon (Pikachu et Evoli)
Chez Cdiscount, une combinaison mérite le détour : Pikachu et sa Poké Ball à 133,88 €, auxquels vous pouvez ajouter Évoli, affiché à 44,99 €, avec 50 % de remise sur ce deuxième set grâce au code FRENCHD50. Soit environ 156,38 € les deux, contre 259,98 € aux tarifs officiels.
L’opération concerne d’autres LEGO, mais cette association permet de réunir deux des premiers modèles Pokémon sans payer Pikachu seul au prix fort.
Nous avons d’ailleurs monté ce Pikachu de 2 050 pièces. Il s’agit d’une vraie construction à exposer, avec sa Poké Ball et un socle électrique qui cache un clin d’œil aux connaisseurs : le numéro 25, sa place dans le Pokédex. On peut ajuster ses oreilles et ses membres pour varier la pose, et même modifier le bout de sa queue pour représenter un mâle ou une femelle. Prévoyez toutefois de la place : l’ensemble mesure 35 cm de haut et 39 cm de profondeur. Le duo s’adresse donc surtout aux fans qui veulent consacrer un coin d’étagère à Pokémon.
TV LG OLED65C6
Le LG C6 de 65 pouces tombe à 1 799 € avec la carte Fnac, ou 1 999 € sans pour les French Days. Sortie en 2026, cette nouvelle génération succède au C5, qui était déjà une très bonne référence pour les films comme pour les jeux.
LG affine surtout son modèle avec un traitement d’image plus évolué, chargé de mieux restituer les détails et d’améliorer les vidéos de moins bonne qualité. Il est aussi un peu plus lumineux. Pour le reste, on conserve ce qui fait l’intérêt de cette gamme : les noirs parfaits de l’OLED et une grande image de 165 cm pour profiter de ses films. Pour jouer sur PC, il passe aussi de 144 à 165 Hz, à condition d’avoir une machine capable de suivre.
PlayStation Portal
Pour jouer à GTA 6 en novembre sans priver tout le monde de télé, le PlayStation Portal est une bonne idée. Sa version Midnight Black passe à 234,99 € au lieu de 249,99 € chez Cdiscount avec le code COCORICO15 pour les French Days. Cet accessoire diffuse les jeux de votre PS5 sur son écran de 8 pouces, avec les commandes et les sensations de la DualSense : parfait pour poursuivre une partie dans le canapé pendant que la télé sert à autre chose. Depuis sa mise à jour, il permet aussi de jouer à une sélection de jeux en cloud sans allumer la PS5, avec un abonnement PS Plus Premium, un bon Wi-Fi reste cependant indispensable.
Quelles sont les dates des French Days ?
En 2026, les French Days de rentrée se déroulent du 7 septembre au 14 septembre inclus. Comme pour le Black Friday, de nouvelles promotions peuvent tomber chaque jour même si la plupart des commerçants proposent d’entrée de jeu leurs meilleures promotions.

articles.title: Revolut et Visa font payer une IA à votre place en France, une grande première
articles.text:
Revolut et Visa ont annoncé lundi avoir réalisé en France le tout premier paiement sécurisé initié par une intelligence artificielle en conditions réelles. Une expérimentation qui pourrait, à terme, transformer nos habitudes d'achat.
Après avoir quelque peu bousculé les usages bancaires avec son appli tout-en-un, Revolut veut donner à ses clients la possibilité de laisser un agent d'intelligence artificielle régler leurs achats à leur place. Ce lundi 7 septembre 2026, une carte Revolut française a en effet servi de cobaye pour une transaction bien réelle, menée dans le cadre du programme Agentic Ready de Visa, et orchestrée par un assistant numérique et sécurisée, le tout grâce à la technologie Visa Payment Passkey. Une manière concrète de tester ce que pourrait devenir le commerce du quotidien, sans sacrifier la sécurité ni le contrôle du client, promettent les différentes parties prenantes.
Revolut et Visa testent en France le tout premier paiement initié par une IA
L'expérience menée par Visa et la fintech britannique s'est déroulée avec de vraies données bancaires, sur un vrai système marchand européen, celui de Cleverbridge. Une carte Revolut destinée aux particuliers a été confiée à My Agent, l'agent de test développé par Visa, chargé d'initier le paiement. L'authentification, elle, a été assurée par Visa Payment Passkey, la technologie qui remplace le sésame classique par une validation biométrique, qui marque au passage la toute première transaction agentique activée par cette technologie en France.
Les deux groupes ont un vrai intérêt à s'y intéresser maintenant. Selon le Baromètre du numérique 2026, un Français sur deux utilise déjà un outil d'IA générative, un chiffre qui grimpe même à 85 % chez les jeunes adultes. Les assistants numériques s'invitent déjà dans la recherche, dans la comparaison de produits ; il ne manquait que l'étape du paiement.
Revolut ne veut pas tout transformer non plus. La transaction s'est appuyée sur le système Visa Intelligent Commerce, qui mobilise les mêmes outils que d'habitude, pour la sécurité des cartes, pour le contrôle d'identité, et la surveillance de la fraude en temps réel. L'idée est de montrer qu'un agent IA peut initier un paiement au nom du client, mais toujours avec son consentement explicite et sous le contrôle de l'émetteur, sans ouvrir de brèche dans les protections déjà en place. Est-ce suffisant pour rassurer les sceptiques ou simples méfiants de l'IA dite agentique ?
Vers un commerce piloté par l'IA, mais sous contrôle
Pour Revolut, qui on le rappelle revendique 80 millions de clients dans le monde dont 8 millions en France, cette expérimentation vise à dessiner le paiement de demain. Béatrice Cossa-Dumurgier, la patronne de Revolut pour l'Europe de l'Ouest, explique que l'intelligence artificielle est déjà en train de changer la façon dont on fait ses achats. « Les paiements doivent évoluer avec ces nouveaux usages », résume-t-elle, tout en insiste de nouveau sur la sécurité, la transparence et le contrôle client.
Chez Visa, on tient un discours similaire. La dirigeante européenne du réseau de paiement, Florence Mélique, voit dans ce test la preuve que les consommateurs peuvent déléguer certaines tâches à une IA, à condition que les garde-fous suivent, ajoutant que « la confiance sera la véritable monnaie d'échange ».
À noter que le test s'est volontairement concentré sur des scénarios de paiement courants, le genre de transaction que l'on effectue sans trop réfléchir. Une manière prudente d'avancer, alors que le secteur cherche encore ses repères sur ce nouveau terrain, en laissant toujours le client maître de ses décisions. Reste à savoir si les Français, déjà largement acquis à l'IA générative, seront prêts à lui confier les cordons de leur bourse. Ça, c'est moins sûr.

articles.title: Swiss startup Jaipur Robotics raises €4.3 million to expand its AI operating system across more waste-to-energy plants | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Jaipur Robotics, the Swiss AI company transforming waste plant operations with computer vision and automation, today announced a €4.3 million Seed funding round to pursue market leadership, expand into new regions, and further verticalise and broaden the product depth.
The round was led by EquityPitcher Ventures and High-Tech Gründerfonds (HTGF). In March 2025, the company announced the successful closing of a €725k pre-Seed funding round led by TiVentures SA, and a few months later, it secured an additional €161k from Venture Kick.
“We envision a future where data from waste fully drives safety and automation. This round enables us to revolutionise entire plant operations,” Ermes Zamboni, co-founder and CEO of Jaipur Robotics.
Founded in 2024 by Ermes Zamboni and Nikhil Prakash, Jaipur Robotics develops computer vision and AI solutions for industrial sites, including Waste-to-Energy (WtE), cement, and biomass plants, making them safer, smarter, and more efficient.
According to the company, WtE plants convert non-recyclable waste into energy, but they face several operational challenges, including the presence of hazardous objects (e.g., gas cylinders, concrete blocks) that can cause costly shutdowns, difficulties in ensuring optimal combustion due to the variability of waste materials, and a shortage of specialised operators to oversee and manage the waste bunkers.
Through its products, the company offers oversized and dangerous item detection in bunkers and truck unloading bays, calorific value mapping (Lower Heating Value – LHV) of waste. Its technology leverages deep learning algorithms and computer vision to enable crane operators to effectively mix waste before it is introduced into the combustion chambers. Operators receive clear, real-time visual guidance through an intuitive heat map that accurately highlights areas of higher and lower calorific values within the bunker.
The company also offers crane-tracking solutions that provide precise, real-time monitoring and prediction of the position and operational status of one or more overhead cranes within the bunker of a Waste-to-Energy plant.
Highlighting its impact, the company reported the following results, calculated per plant per year:
- More than 80% fewer unplanned shutdowns via real-time hazard detection.
- Over €1 million in added value from improved waste mixing as calorific-value mapping optimises combustion and compliance.
- Smarter crane operations with predictive guidance automating crane control and maximising productivity.
With the largest European WtE dataset, comprising over 50 million labelled images, Jaipur Robotics’ system analyses more than 5 million tonnes of waste per year and detects hazardous materials with 99% accuracy.
Anna Stetter, Investment Manager at HTGF, said, “What convinced us to co-lead this round is the combination of a dataset, a founding team with rare depth across mechanical engineering, deep learning, and industrial deployment, and outstanding, measurable results at customer sites.”
Headquartered at Technopole Ticino in Manno, near Lugano, Switzerland, the company has a 40-person team and two R&D centres in Switzerland and Asia. It is actively growing its team across AI, engineering, and commercial roles.

articles.title: Women’s wellness brand Nua raises $50M in Series C round led by Peak XV, Filter Capital
articles.text:
Women’s wellness brand Nua raises $50M in Series C round led by Peak XV, Filter Capital
Nua will use the funding towards its next phase of growth as it aims to reach Rs 500 crore in annualised revenue in the next two years from Rs 100 crore now.
Women’s wellness brand Nua has raised $50 million in a Series C round of funding led by Peak XV & Filter Capital along with participation from existing investors Mirabilis Investment Trust and Footpath Ventures.
The funding round includes primary raise and secondaries offering partial exits to Kae Capital, Lightbox VC, and existing angel investors, a statement said.
Nua plans to deploy the capital towards its next phase of growth with a focus on brand building, expanding reach and distribution, and strengthening R&D.
Mumbai-headquartered Nua Founded was in 2017. It says it serves over 3 million women and girls every month across categories including zero irritation period care, maternity care, and everyday intimate care.
Nua's founder & CEO Ravi Ramachandran said, “Since our inception, we have sought to address neglected needs in women's wellness through better-for-her products and a brand that genuinely speaks to today's young women and girls.”
He said the funding will help scale Nua's annualised revenue run rate from Rs 100 crore to ₹500 crore in 24 months, while remaining profitable. “As we look ahead, we will continue to anticipate the evolving needs of women and build products that make a meaningful difference to their everyday lives.”
Nua recently launched the digital offerings Nua Period Tracker app and SecretKeeper chat to engage with consumers beyond its product portfolio.
Sakshi Chopra, Managing Director, Peak XV, said, “Women's wellness in India is a large and evolving opportunity, and Nua has demonstrated a strong ability to build a brand that resonates deeply with consumers.”
“The company has emerged as the fastest-growing brand in the category and the second-largest player online, demonstrating its ability to compete and win alongside much larger incumbents,” she added.
Filter Capital's co-founder and managing partner Sumit Sinha said, “Nua is redefining feminine hygiene and wellness with its superior product proposition and a brand that has built a remarkable connection with consumers.”
