articles.title: Malas noticias para los móviles baratos de Samsung: lo peor que podía pasar, va a pasar
articles.text:
El mercado está loco. La crisis de la memoria RAM y los chips está afectando a todas las compañías del sector y las subidas son un no parar. Hoy le toca a Samsung. Concretamente, a los móviles de gama media y gama baja que vende la compañía en buena parte del globo. Una de las regiones más importantes para la surcoreana está a punto de anunciar una subida de precio masiva para los modelos más populares de la compañía. Y, aunque a día de hoy no te afectará de forma directa, lo cierto es que puedes ir preparando la cartera.
Si tenías pensado comprar un móvil de Samsung dentro del segmento medio, es probable que lo más inteligente sea hacerlo cuanto antes. Se ha filtrado que la división de la compañía en la India está a punto de subir los precios en modelos tan populares como el Galaxy A37 y A57. Y no poco.
Al parecer, Samsung aplicará un aumento de unas 6.000 rupias a los dos modelos sin una justificación más allá de la crisis de la memoria RAM. No son nuevos modelos ni traen ninguna novedad, simplemente suben de precio por culpa de una pérdida efectiva en el margen de venta.
Samsung hace esto después de subir el precio en esta nueva generación: los Galaxy A37/A57 se lanzaron con un precio más alto que los Galaxy A36/A56. En España también así, por lo que todo apunta a que el resto del planeta podría estar ante la misma situación.
¿Subirán de precio los Samsung de gama media en España?
Samsung lanzó el Galaxy A56 por 479 euros en España el año pasado. Este año ha hecho lo propio con el Galaxy A57 a 529 euros, aplicando una subida de 50 euros entre generación y generación. Es decir, un movimiento prácticamente idéntico al de la India.
¿Qué significa esto? Que, al igual que hará en la India en los próximos días, Samsung se podría ver obligada a volver a subir el precio de los Galaxy A37/A57 a mitad de curso. Esta vez sin nuevos modelos de por medio, simplemente por culpa del coste de los chips y la memoria RAM.
Si lo hace, es posible que el PVPr pase de esos 529 euros a unos 549 o 559 euros para el Galaxy A57 de 128 GB, un precio alto, pero que sigue la línea ascendente de casi todos los dispositivos de gama media y gama alta. Es decir, se aleja de las cifras que teníamos hace años, pero mantiene la distancia con los smartphones que se sitúan por encima: todos los gama alta también han subido en los últimos meses.
El mejor ejemplo puede llegar este mismo miércoles 9 de septiembre, cuando Apple presentará sus nuevos iPhone, probablemente, con precios más altos en todo el mundo.

articles.title: A Microsoft engineer says "typing code is absolutely over," here's what he means
articles.text:
Big quote: GitHub Copilot is taking on more of the work that happens around writing code, not just the code itself. Its agent can now set up environments, make changes in a repository, run tests, and open a pull request for a developer to review. David Fowler, a Microsoft Distinguished Engineer who leads work on Aspire, put it bluntly in a post on X: "Typing code is absolutely over."
Fowler was not suggesting that software engineers are becoming unnecessary. But as AI handles more routine coding work, developers may spend less time writing individual lines and more time on system design, requirements, dependencies, and the review needed to make sure software is secure and works as intended.
Copilot's coding agent is part of that change. GitHub has added Windows development environments for the agent, allowing it to build and test Windows-targeted projects, run linters, and check whether builds succeed. The agent can then return its work to a human developer for review through a pull request.
GitHub has also brought agent sessions to the Windows Subsystem for Linux, which is useful for teams that build software across Windows and Linux toolchains, especially when applications are developed on Windows but tested or deployed in Linux-based environments.
 – David Fowler (@davidfowl) September 3, 2026
Microsoft is making similar changes in Aspire, its code-first toolchain for building distributed applications. Aspire lets developers describe application components such as services, containers, and databases in one application model, giving an AI agent more context than it would get from a single source file or a chat prompt.
Aspire 13.1 introduced deeper support for AI coding assistants. Aspire 13.2 added an agent-friendly command-line interface and support for the Model Context Protocol, which can give AI tools controlled access to development resources and context.
Microsoft's Aspire team said in April that AI agents can be good at generating code, but that producing code is different from delivering a working application. Aspire is meant to close some of that gap by allowing an agent to start services, inspect logs and telemetry, identify errors, restart components, and test again. In theory, that gives an agent a way to investigate an application failure directly instead of relying on a developer to copy error output into a chat window.
Microsoft is using AI on the security side as well. Its MDASH system is an agentic vulnerability scanner used by engineering teams working on Windows, Azure, and identity systems. Microsoft's Windows security team said MDASH "enabled our security team to perform vulnerability hunting at the scale of Windows with a much higher depth of analysis than was previously possible."
The company said the work includes components such as the Windows kernel, Hyper-V, and the networking stack. Those are large and security-sensitive codebases, where automated analysis can help researchers examine more code and investigate issues more quickly.
Microsoft's native Windows development tools are also part of the picture. The company recommends WinUI 3 for new native Windows applications, and the framework is now open source. More accessible source code and documentation can make it easier for AI tools to understand common project structures and supported APIs.
Microsoft has also published a guide for using Copilot to build WinUI applications. It covers code completion, file context, and project-specific instructions, showing that the company expects AI assistance to become part of regular Windows development work.
Project Zenith, announced September 4, adds a hardware angle. Microsoft described it as a stripped-down Windows 11 setup for developers, with a baseline requirement of 64GB of unified memory and 250GB/s of memory bandwidth. The initial focus is on AMD Ryzen AI Halo chips.
The hardware is intended to support local AI models with more than 30 billion parameters. Running models locally could reduce cloud inference costs and give developers more control over how proprietary code and data are handled.
All of which explains why Fowler's remark is less sweeping than it first appears. He was not predicting that developers will disappear; instead, his post reflected how their work is changing. AI may take over more boilerplate coding and routine fixes, but developers will still decide what gets built, review what the tools produce, and make sure the software is secure, reliable, and ready to run in the real world.

articles.title: El decreto de Meloni de reconocimiento facial con IA genera preocupación entre los expertos
articles.text:
El decreto de Meloni de reconocimiento facial con IA genera preocupación entre los expertos
Italia ultima una de las regulaciones más ambiciosas de Europa para el uso policial de estas tecnologías
Algún día no lejano, participar en un concierto, levantar una pancarta en una manifestación o ir a un estadio para ver un partido podría convertirse, con la ayuda de la inteligencia artificial, en una oportunidad de vigilancia masiva e identificación colectiva por parte del gobierno de turno. Parece un escenario distópico digno de una dictadura, pero es el camino que ha emprendido Europa con las tecnologías de reconocimiento facial, que cada vez más países están utilizando. E Italia lleva la delantera.
España aún no posee legislación específica sobre ello. Pero hace dos años, en agosto de 2024, entró en vigor el AI Act (Ley de IA), el primer marco regulatorio del mundo sobre inteligencia artificial: un reglamento europeo que clasifica los sistemas de IA por niveles de riesgo, con aplicación escalonada.
Sobre la identificación biométrica policial, el reglamento fija en teoría una prohibición general, pero introduce excepciones ―terrorismo, personas desaparecidas, delitos “graves”― y deja a cada Estado un margen amplio para desarrollar el procedimiento concreto. Y aquí está el problema: en Italia, que ya ha implementado esa normativa, la polémica es mayúscula.
El 4 de agosto, el Gobierno de Giorgia Meloni aprobó de forma definitiva, tras un intercambio de borradores con el Parlamento, el decreto que adapta la ley italiana a la Ley de IA, aunque todavía no publicado en la Gaceta Oficial (el contenido se conoce solo por una nota del Ejecutivo). Italia se convierte así en el primer país de la UE en dotarse de un marco jurídico detallado para las excepciones que la Ley de IA deja abiertas al uso policial del reconocimiento facial. En España, el Proyecto de Ley Orgánica para el buen uso y la gobernanza de la IA está en el Congreso, con el plazo de enmiendas abierto.
El decreto italiano distingue dos usos: identificación en tiempo real, reservada a amenazas graves como terrorismo o búsqueda de desaparecidos, con autorización del fiscal; e identificación a posteriori, que solo se activa tras cometerse un delito, para identificar sospechosos ya señalados. Respecto al primer borrador, el cambio más relevante afecta a eventos con “necesidades de orden público” —plazas, estadios, manifestaciones—: la policía puede grabar y conservar esas imágenes, pero el reconocimiento facial ya no se activa automáticamente sobre todos los presentes, sino solo si se comete un delito, con autorización judicial en 24 horas. Los datos se borrarían a los 7 días si no ha pasado nada.
Las organizaciones de derechos civiles están en pie de guerra, aunque son pesimistas sobre la posibilidad real de frenar la bola de nieve. Le pone palabras Diletta Huyskes, socióloga de la Universidad Estatal de Milán y fundadora de la ONG Immanence, una de las voces más activas durante el debate parlamentario italiano: “No hay nada que hacer, partiendo de la base de que los reguladores europeos, de una u otra forma, permiten que los gobiernos actúen de esta manera. Mi postura es totalmente contraria a los usos que proponen, pero estamos delante de una tendencia que viene gestándose desde hace años”.
Según la nota del Ejecutivo (a falta de texto final), el Gobierno ha retocado de manera cosmética algunos aspectos técnicos —requisitos de la base de datos, procedimiento de borrado, poderes del Garante de Privacidad—, pero no los más controvertidos: sigue permitido el reconocimiento a posteriori en espacios públicos, no se han reforzado las autorizaciones judiciales para el tiempo real, ni se exige informar a la ciudadanía de cuándo está activo el sistema.
“La implementación de esta tecnología crea una infraestructura de vigilancia omnipresente. Incluso con un cambio de gobierno, puede usarse fácilmente con fines autoritarios”, critica Huyskes.
El periodista y experto en control biométrico Fabio Chiusi coincide y va más allá: “Hay partidos aún más extremistas que los que están en el poder, como el del general Roberto Vannacci, que pide drones con cámaras térmicas para garantizar la seguridad. ¿Es posible creer que instituciones guiadas por estos instintos puedan cumplir con las condiciones que impone la Ley de IA? ¿Durante cuánto tiempo?”. Y añade: “Hace pocos años, pensar en ciudades vigiladas por miles de ojos tecnológicos siempre abiertos nos hacía pensar en el régimen chino; hoy afecta a las democracias más avanzadas. Esta tendencia no se frena con enmiendas puntuales, sino con prohibiciones absolutas”.
Para Huyskes también son problemáticos la opacidad sobre los criterios de entrenamiento o los procedimientos de eliminación de imágenes: “Obstaculizan la supervisión democrática y la protección de los derechos fundamentales”. En palabras de Chiusi: “Para este Gobierno, registrar automáticamente a todos los presentes en una manifestación —es decir, vigilancia masiva— es compatible con una sociedad democrática”.
La periodista Laura Carrer, investigadora del Hermes Center Hacking for Human Rights, coincide: “Se está normalizando una vigilancia que antes no existía. La hemos vinculado al requisito de que exista un delito para usarla, pero mientras tanto, queda registrada”. Y lamenta la falta de control externo: “El único pilar que queda es la supervisión judicial, aunque la activación puede autorizarla el fiscal, no un juez. El fiscal lleva la investigación y es más probable que la autorice”. Insiste en ese punto Aljosa Ajanovic Andelic, de EDRi (European Digital Rights): “El organismo autorizador debería evaluar la necesidad y la proporcionalidad. La cuestión importante es si la autoridad examina realmente la necesidad de ese despliegue en particular, o simplemente valida de manera rutinaria una decisión policial ya tomada”.
Ajanovic cree que la ley italiana “pone a prueba la frontera entre el reconocimiento facial en tiempo real y a posteriori”, con implicaciones que van más allá de Italia: “Si se capturan y almacenan continuamente los datos biométricos de todas las personas que transitan por un espacio público, y luego se decide a quién identificar, ¿es realmente un sistema posterior, o una forma de lograr un efecto de vigilancia muy similar mediante una secuencia técnica diferente? Si esos datos se usan después para criminalizar a los asistentes a una manifestación, se estaría actuando de facto como un sistema en tiempo real”.
El experto pone el ejemplo de Hungría, que “también excluyó la identificación facial rápida de la categoría de ‘tiempo real’ usando imágenes fijas en lugar de transmisión en directo, y luego amenazó con usarla para identificar y multar a quienes asistieran a la manifestación del Orgullo de Budapest [que el Gobierno del ultra Viktor Orbán prohibió]. Según nuestro análisis, el sistema húngaro es en tiempo real porque puede influir en el comportamiento durante una protesta, y por tanto viola el AI Act”. Lo que teme EDRi es que las leyes nacionales “se utilicen para eludir las prohibiciones y expandir los sistemas biométricos de vigilancia masiva”.
Antes de EDRi, Ajanovic coordinó en 2022, desde Òmnium Cultural, la campaña Catalangate, sobre el espionaje con el software israelí Pegasus a políticos, activistas y periodistas catalanes en el contexto del procés: “Utilizar sistemas de vigilancia para combatir el crimen solo con autorización judicial es un concepto que se presta fácilmente al engaño. No solo lo vimos en Cataluña; también con los ecologistas en Francia o los movimientos propalestinos en Alemania y Reino Unido. Cuando ciertos movimientos son etiquetados como terroristas, las garantías judiciales existen solo sobre el papel”. El límite temporal en la retención de datos, añade, es útil porque es auditable en principio, “pero el problema es el mismo que vemos en migración: la falta de transparencia y el secretismo hacen que sea inverificable”.
Para los migrantes y solicitantes de asilo, señala, el efecto disuasorio “puede ser particularmente significativo porque su relación con las autoridades ya es más precaria”. A esto se suma el llamado function creep: “Un migrante puede tener datos biométricos en una base por razones que no tienen nada que ver con la delincuencia. Si la policía puede acceder a esas bases, las consecuencias de una coincidencia errónea son mucho más graves. Con el nuevo Reglamento de Deportación de la UE, los Estados deberán registrar a personas indocumentadas, así que esta interoperabilidad podría producirse casi automáticamente”.
Según el Instituto Xnet, el proyecto español acierta en la obligación de etiquetar deepfakes y al recoger prohibiciones de la Ley de IA como la perfilación social, y al imponer sanciones fuertes al sector privado; pero lo critican por no aplicar esas mismas sanciones cuando es el sector público quien infringe la ley, y por ser, en conjunto, “más una ley de sanción y vigilancia que de derechos ciudadanos”.
Según Ajanovic, España tiene todas las opciones abiertas: puede replicar los usos italianos o “adoptar normas más estrictas y prohibir, por ejemplo, la identificación biométrica ex post”. Y concluye: “La sociedad civil española tiene una oportunidad mucho más importante que la simple supervisión de la ley, porque el legislador puede decidir dónde poner el umbral nacional. No solo importa lo que la ley dice que debe hacer el sistema, sino lo que permite técnicamente que haga la policía. La Ley de IA no le exige a España reproducir la interpretación más permisiva del reglamento”.

articles.title: « Nous sommes entrés dans une nouvelle ère » : cette fusée réussit là où l'Europe attendait depuis des décennies
articles.text:
La deuxième fois était donc la bonne, et c’est une formidable avancée pour l’Europe spatiale. Samedi 5 septembre 2026, à 22h12, la fusée Spectrum de la société allemande Isar Aerospace s’est arrachée avec succès du pas de tir d’Andøya, tout au nord de la Norvège. Sept minutes plus tard, elle larguait ses satellites en orbite basse.
Le contraste avec le tout premier essai de l’entreprise est spectaculaire, et a de quoi faire sourire : en mars 2025, il y a à peine plus d’un an, cette même fusée retombait en mer au bout d’une trentaine de secondes, avant de s’abîmer dans une grosse explosion. Il y avait cependant quelques motifs de satisfaction : au moins, le lanceur avait décollé.
Cette fois, le scénario était différent : Isar Aerospace tient sa qualification, et l’Europe a surtout démontré qu’elle peut avoir un accès souverain à l’espace depuis son propre sol – plus exactement depuis l’Europe continentale, sans avoir besoin de recourir à une base spatiale lointaine, comme le centre spatial de Kourou, en Guyane française (Amérique du Sud).
Le lanceur Spectrum n’a pas la prétention de venir concurrencer Ariane 6. C’est un petit engin, haut de 28 mètres, large de 2 et mobilisant 10 moteurs pour emporter jusqu’à une tonne en orbite basse (entre 100 et 2 000 km d’altitude). C’est, en somme, un microlanceur, qui complète la gamme des fusées européennes sur un segment précis.
Ce vol, baptisé Onward and Upward, emportait en l’espèce cinq cubesats et une expérience, du matériel universitaire sélectionné par l’agence spatiale allemande (DLR) et soutenu par le programme Boost ! de l’Agence spatiale européenne. Boost ! vise à soutenir les initiatives commerciales proposant des services de transport spatial.
Rien n’a été simple pour Isar Aerospace entre le raté du printemps 2025 et le tir réussi de cette fin d’été 2026. Le premier vol avait donc tourné court et il fallait déjà se remettre en selle pour la suite. Ce rebond, d’abord espéré pour janvier, a hélas glissé de report en report. Le deuxième tir a connu une fuite dans un réservoir sous pression puis divers soucis.
Une réussite qui tombe à pic pour l’Europe
Hasard du calendrier, la fusée Spectrum est parvenue à décoller quatre jours avant un sommet spatial organisé à Paris par Emmanuel Macron, consacré à la souveraineté spatiale européenne – les 9 et 10 septembre 2026. Selon Les Echos, Washington a fait pression sur les géants comme SpaceX et Blue Origin pour qu’ils esquivent l’évènement.
Malgré cette manœuvre qui a poussé les entreprises américaines à déserter la séquence, des dizaines d’autres nations demeurent invitées et prévoient de venir. Surtout, l’Europe peut bomber le torse malgré le coup américain, et démontrer que l’on peut aussi se débrouiller sur le Vieux Continent. Même s’il aura fallu cravacher 18 mois pour gommer 30 secondes d’échec.
Ce timing, personne ne l’avait scénarisé. Mais la politique a évidemment saisi la balle au bond : pendant que Washington boude une conférence sur la gouvernance de l’orbite, Emmanuel Macron a salué le tir, dans un tweet qui visait aussi à donner le change. « L’Europe prend son destin en main, y compris dans le domaine spatial », a-t-il écrit.
« Pour la première fois, un acteur privé européen a placé sa fusée en orbite après un lancement depuis le sol européen. […] Une victoire pour toute l’Europe. […] Ces succès disent ce dont notre continent est capable lorsqu’il innove, investit et assume son ambition : bâtir une Europe puissance, indépendante jusque dans l’espace », a-t-il ajouté.
D’autres félicitations sont venues d’ailleurs en Europe, mais aussi de Josef Aschbacher, le directeur de l’Agence spatiale européenne, qui s’était alarmé du déclin européen dans le spatial et de la nécessité de davantage compter sur soi-même pour les vols spatiaux. Le concurrent américain Rocket Lab a aussi adressé ses félicitations.
Un vol de qualification n’est pas encore une cadence industrielle. Isar affirme avoir déjà cinq Spectrum en production et vise à terme jusqu’à 40 fusées par an dans sa future usine près de Munich, avec un second pas de tir prévu au Canada. C’est un rythme bien plus soutenu qu’Ariane 6 ou Vega-C, les deux lanceurs stars de l’Europe.
« Nous avons réalisé en quelques années ce qui avait pris des décennies à l’industrie spatiale européenne. L’Europe dispose désormais d’un accès souverain à l’espace. Nous sommes entrés dans une nouvelle ère pour les vols spatiaux européens. », juge Daniel Metzler, CEO et cofondateur. Isar Aerospace doit désormais enchaîner les tirs pour transformer cette réussite unique en service commercial régulier.

articles.text:

articles.title: Project Zenith: Was dieses Spezial-Windows für High-End-PCs anders macht
articles.text:
Project Zenith: Diese Version von Windows 11 ist für High-End-PCs gedacht
Microsoft will auch zukünftig relevant für Entwickler:innen bleiben und hat deshalb Project Zenith vorgestellt. Unter diesem Namen optimiert der Hersteller sein Betriebssystem nicht nur gezielt für Entwickeler:innen, sondern liefert die veränderte Version direkt auch mit besonders leistungsstarker Hardware aus. Die High-End-PCs sollen direkt nach dem Auspacken und beim ersten Hochfahren zum Programmieren genutzt werden können.
Diese Anforderungen erfüllen die Project-Zenith-PCs
Die Ankündigung des optimierten Windows-11-Setups auf leistungsstarken Rechnern beschreibt Project Zenith als „sofort einsatzbereite, ablenkungsfreie Windows-Umgebung für Entwicklergeräte“.
Die Geräte, auf denen die spezielle Windows-11-Version ausgeliefert wird, haben es dabei in sich: mindestens 64 Gigabyte (GB) RAM und eine Speicherbandbreite von über 250 GB pro Sekunde. Entwickler:innen sollen „über 30 Milliarden Parametermodelle lokal und ohne Datenlimit ausführen“ können.
Um das realisieren zu können, kündigt Microsoft an, dass Project Zenith als erstes mit dem Ryzen AI Halo von AMD verfügbar sein wird. Weitere Geräte der OEM- und Silicon-Partner sollen „in den kommenden Monaten“ folgen.
Die Hardware, auf der die Entwickler-Version von Windows 11 laufen soll, wäre damit geklärt. Doch wie genau sieht die Software aus?
Kein neues Windows: Microsoft nutzt die Windows Developer Config
Auch wenn es auf den ersten Blick so wirken könnte, hat Microsoft hier keine neue Version seines aktuellen Betriebssystems entwickelt. Stattdessen handelt es sich um ein und dasselbe Windows 11, das derzeit bereits auf Millionen PCs weltweit läuft.
Den Unterschied macht die Konfiguration, die Microsoft Anfang Juni zur Build 2026 als „Windows Developer Config“ vorgestellt hat und die auf praktisch jedem Windows-PC angewendet werden kann. Das Ziel ist eine schlankere, „ablenkungsfreie“ Windows-Umgebung für Entwickler:innen.
Im Detail bedeutet das zum Beispiel, dass „Dateierweiterungen, versteckte Dateien, vollständige Dateipfade und der Detailbereich aktiviert“ sind. „Tipps zum Startmenü, Account-Benachrichtigungen, zuletzt verwendete Ordner/Dateien und Sync-Provider-Tipps“ sind hingegen deaktiviert, fasst Windows Latest zusammen. Zudem sind Windows Terminal und Visual Studio Code bereits an die Taskbar angeheftet und das Windows-Subsystem für Linux (WSL) ist integriert.
Microsoft betont, dass das nur die „sinnvolle Ausgangsbasis“ ist. Nutzer:innen können weiterhin „mit den von Ihnen bevorzugten Tools, Sprachen und Frameworks konfigurieren, erweitern und personalisieren“.
Project Zenith: Microsoft bündelt Windows 11 mit Entwickler-Hardware
Letztlich beschreibt Project Zenith die Kombination der Developer-Config mit leistungsstarker Hardware, sodass Entwickler:innen direkt nach dem Auspacken loslegen können. Microsoft gibt an, dass das Projekt im Austausch „mit Entwicklern darüber, was sie heute von Windows benötigen und wohin sich die Plattform entwickeln soll“, entstanden ist. Das Unternehmen verspricht zudem, dass Project Zenith „erst der Anfang“ ist.

OpenAI has acknowledged a “wiki incident” in which its AI agents hijacked a community-edited German website and used it as a message board for cheating during tests and other rogue behaviour.
The company said the episode highlights the need for greater transparency around unintended AI behaviour, or “misalignment”, and admitted that the industry lacks clear standards for reporting such incidents. OpenAI is working with regulators worldwide on improving disclosure practices, following growing scrutiny over the safety of autonomous AI agents.
Meanwhile, social media is giving books a new lease of life. Communities such as BookTok and Bookstagram are turning reading into a social activity, with readers and creators sharing reviews, recommendations, bookshelf tours and more. articles.title: CD and vinyl sales are surging as frustration with digital media keeps growing
articles.text:
In a nutshell: It's time to dust off that old turntable and boombox: physical media is seeing a big resurgence, with both CDs and vinyl sales jumping by double digits in the first half of 2026. The news comes as public anger over digital media, from increasing streaming prices to buyers not actually owning their purchases, intensifies.
News of the latest increase in physical media sales comes from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). It revealed that recorded music revenues for H1 2026 were up 6.9% from the first half of 2025 and outpaced inflation, with both streaming and physical formats posting gains.
It was physical media that grabbed the headlines. Revenue in this sector grew an impressive 25.9% as vinyl saw 17.7% growth and CD revenue went up a massive 58.6%.
Streaming, of course, remains the largest source of recorded music revenue by far. It generated $4.9 billion, up 4.7%. Paid subscriptions reached $3.4 billion, up 6.4%, while ad-supported free subscriptions were up 3.7% to $900 million.
It's fair to say that 15 or 20 years ago, many people would have expected CDs and vinyl to have vanished completely by now. But consumers are spending more money on these formats.
There have been plenty of reminders this year of why physical media isn't dying, one of the biggest being that buyers actually own their purchases. This contrast was illustrated perfectly in June when Sony said it was removing 551 movies and TV series from the PlayStation Store in the UK on September 1, 2026, due to licensing issues. The content will also be deleted from the libraries of customers who have already purchased it.
The same thing happened when Sony wiped more than 1,300 seasons of Discovery TV shows in 2023, another reminder that the EULA that comes with digital purchases almost always describes the transaction as the purchase of a revocable license.
 – Tom Warren (@tomwarren) August 22, 2026
Sony's decision to stop offering new PlayStation games on disc after January 2028 has also pushed angry consumers to embrace physical media – not that Sony cares.
Digital revenue did increase during H1 2026, too, so it's not like everyone is canceling their Spotify and Apple Music subscriptions and buying CDs instead; the RIAA describes the report as an illustration of a "diversifying marketplace." Still, it shows that CDs and vinyl aren't being added to our list of Once-Iconic Tech Products That Are Now a Fading Memory just yet.

articles.title: GeForce RTX 5070 vs. Radeon RX 9070 XT: 2026 Update
articles.text:
We recently compared the Radeon RX 9070 XT and GeForce RTX 5070 Ti head-to-head across 52 games and found that, overall, they delivered very similar performance. That was the reason for comparing them in the first place: based on performance, they are direct competitors, or at least they are meant to be.
However, as things stand today, there is a massive price divide between the two, with the RTX Ti GPU now commanding a premium of more than 50%. Given that, the standard RTX 5070 has become the more relevant comparison for the 9070 XT, even though the Radeon GPU is currently the cheaper of the two.
At the time of testing, the 9070 XT can be had for around $730 to $750. Meanwhile, RTX 5070 models start at $800, with most priced around $820. That means the 12GB GeForce GPU carries roughly a 9% price premium in this matchup.
As with our previous 52-game comparison, we benchmarked each game at two resolutions using two quality presets, with some configurations tested both with and without ray tracing. That gives us plenty of data to work through.
Most testing was conducted in-game using external performance-monitoring software, while results captured using a built-in benchmark are clearly labeled on the graphs.
With that covered, let's get into the data.
Test System Specs
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D | 
| Motherboard | MSI MPG X870E Carbon WiFi [BIOS 7E49v1A4] Resizable BAR Enabled | 
| Memory | G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB DDR5-6000 CL30 [CL30-38-38-96] | 
| Graphics Card | Sapphire Radeon RX 9070 XT Pure MSI RTX 5070 Gaming Trio White | 
| ATX Case | MSI Prospect 700R | 
| Power Supply | Kolink Regulator Gold ATX 3.0 1200W | 
| Storage | TeamGroup T-Force Cardea A440 M.2 PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD 4TB | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 25H2 | 
| Display Driver | AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.8.1 GeForce Game Ready Driver 610.88 | 
Benchmarks
007 First Light
First up is 007 First Light, where the 9070 XT dominates, outperforming the RTX 5070 by 36% to 46% across all tested configurations. It easily maintains more than 100 fps at 1440p and delivers a playable 57 fps at 4K Ultra, where the RTX 5070 falls behind at just 42 fps.
Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight
Testing with LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, we see the 9070 XT hold a consistent single-to-double-digit advantage over the RTX 5070. It maintains a 4% lead at 1440p using both presets, widening to an 8% to 13% advantage at 4K, alongside notably stronger 1% low performance.
Pragmata
Pragmata strongly favors the 9070 XT across all tested configurations. The Radeon GPU commands a decisive 31% to 32% lead using the standard Max Quality preset, widening that advantage to nearly 40% with Ray Tracing Max Quality enabled. Even at 4K, it sustains 76 fps.
The Outer Worlds 2
In The Outer Worlds 2, the 9070 XT maintains a solid lead over the RTX 5070 across all tests. It delivers a 31% to 37% advantage using the standard High Quality preset and remains comfortably ahead by 16% to 17% once the Very High preset with Ray Tracing Max is enabled.
Arc Raiders
In Arc Raiders, the 9070 XT consistently outpaces the RTX 5070, delivering a 22% performance advantage at 1440p using Static RT and a 30% margin at 4K. With RT Epic enabled, the 9070 XT maintains a solid 14% advantage at both resolutions.
Assassin's Creed Shadows
In Assassin's Creed Shadows, the 9070 XT holds a commanding 28% to 38% lead over the RTX 5070 across both presets and resolutions. With the heavier ray-tracing workload at 1440p using the Ultra High preset, the Radeon GPU manages 55 fps compared with just 40 fps for the RTX 5070, making the 9070 XT 38% faster.
Battlefield 6
In Battlefield 6, the 9070 XT beats the RTX 5070 by 18% to 22% at 1440p, widening that lead to 40% to 42% at 4K. It sustains a smooth 63 fps at 4K using the Overkill preset, whereas the RTX 5070 trails at just 45 fps.
Marvel Rivals
In Marvel Rivals, the 9070 XT consistently outpaces the RTX 5070 across all tested settings. It holds an 11% to 20% lead using the Medium quality preset, but stretches those margins to 24% to 30% when Lumen is enabled at Ultra Quality, reaching 84 fps at 1440p.
Crimson Desert
In Crimson Desert, the 9070 XT consistently leads the RTX 5070 by 13% to 22%. It delivers a comfortable 86 fps at 1440p using the Cinematic preset versus 75 fps for the RTX 5070, while also holding an 18% to 22% advantage at 4K across both presets.
F1 25
The 9070 XT also comes out comfortably ahead in F1 25, outperforming the RTX 5070 by roughly 30% using the rasterized High Quality preset. With ray tracing enabled at Ultra High quality, the Radeon GPU maintains a consistent 12% advantage at both 1440p and 4K.
Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty
The 9070 XT maintains a massive 43% to 50% lead in rasterized testing and at 1440p with ray tracing enabled in Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty. At 4K using Ray Tracing Ultra, the RTX 5070 collapses to an unplayable 9 fps average, allowing the 9070 XT to pull ahead by nearly 190%.
Call of Duty: Black Ops 7
The 9070 XT leads convincingly in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7, beating the RTX 5070 by up to 45% using the Basic settings. With Extreme RT enabled, the Radeon GPU maintains a comfortable 28% advantage at 1440p and remains 16% faster at 4K.
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
In Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the 9070 XT outperforms the RTX 5070 by 25% to 36% across both quality presets. At 1440p using the Epic preset, the 9070 XT delivers a smooth 64 fps average compared with 49 fps on the RTX 5070.
Borderlands 4
In Borderlands 4, the 9070 XT outperforms the RTX 5070 across the board, leading by 27% to 38%. At 1440p using the Badass preset, the 9070 XT achieves 55 fps compared with 40 fps on the RTX 5070, maintaining a similarly large advantage at 4K.
Doom: The Dark Ages
In Doom: The Dark Ages, the 9070 XT holds a massive 29% to 50% lead using the standard Ultra Nightmare preset. However, enabling full path tracing shifts the balance at 1440p, allowing the RTX 5070 to pull ahead by 32%, with 25 fps versus 19 fps for the Radeon GPU.
Dying Light: The Beast
In Dying Light: The Beast, the 9070 XT maintains a 7% to 12% lead in rasterized performance, which expands to a 22% to 29% advantage once ray tracing is enabled. It reaches 62 fps at 1440p Ultra RT compared with 51 fps for the RTX 5070.
Forza Horizon 5
In Forza Horizon 5, the 9070 XT puts in another strong showing, outpacing the RTX 5070 by 31% to 37% across all tested configurations. It easily exceeds 200 fps at 1440p Ultra and still delivers 114 fps at 4K using the Max preset.
Forza Horizon 6
The 9070 XT also performs extremely well in Forza Horizon 6, outpacing the RTX 5070 by 36% to 38% using the Extreme preset. With ray tracing enabled, the Radeon GPU remains firmly ahead, holding a 29% to 34% lead across both resolutions.
Final Fantasy XVI
Final Fantasy XVI heavily favors the 9070 XT, which commands a massive 50% to 57% performance advantage over the RTX 5070 across all tested presets and resolutions. It comfortably sustains 103 fps at 1440p Ultra, while the RTX 5070 manages just 66 fps.
Ghost of Tsushima: Director's Cut
In Ghost of Tsushima: Director's Cut, the 9070 XT commands a decisive 26% to 37% lead over the RTX 5070 across all tested presets. At 4K Very High, the Radeon GPU delivers a smooth 78 fps average, whereas the RTX 5070 trails at 57 fps.
God of War Ragnarök
God of War Ragnarök also strongly favors the 9070 XT, which leads the RTX 5070 by 28% to 36% across both quality presets. At 1440p High, it delivers 143 fps versus 112 fps for the RTX 5070, with that sizable advantage carrying through to 4K Ultra.
Hell is Us
In Hell is Us, the 9070 XT convincingly outpaces the RTX 5070 by 26% to 30% across the board. The Radeon GPU achieves 86 fps at 1440p Ultra compared with 68 fps on the RTX 5070, with a similar advantage maintained at 4K.
Delta Force
In Delta Force, the 9070 XT consistently outpaces the RTX 5070 by 14% to 25% across all tested configurations. At 1440p using the Ultimate preset, the Radeon card delivers 184 fps on average compared with 151 fps for the RTX 5070.
PUBG: Battlegrounds
In PUBG: Battlegrounds, the 9070 XT consistently beats the RTX 5070 across both presets. It delivers a 14% to 22% advantage at 1440p, though the margin narrows to 6% at 4K. Across all tests, the Radeon card also provides significantly stronger and more consistent 1% lows.
Counter-Strike 2
In Counter-Strike 2, the 9070 XT leads by 30% to 40% using the Medium preset and holds a slight edge at 1440p Very High. At 4K Very High, however, the RTX 5070 moves ahead by 10%, delivering 158 fps.
Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege X
The 9070 XT delivers a consistent 14% to 19% advantage over the RTX 5070 in Rainbow Six Siege X across both resolutions and quality presets. It easily exceeds 200 fps at 1440p Ultra+ and sustains more than 100 fps at 4K.
Warframe
In Warframe, the 9070 XT consistently outpaces the RTX 5070 across all tested settings. It holds a 15% to 23% lead at 1440p, widening to 22% to 26% at 4K, while also delivering substantially stronger 1% low performance.
Overwatch
Overwatch is an exceptionally close contest between the two GPUs. The RTX 5070 holds a slight 1% to 4% lead using the Medium preset, while the 9070 XT takes a 3% advantage at 1440p Epic. At 4K Epic, both graphics cards deliver exactly 137 fps.
Hunt: Showdown 1896
In Hunt: Showdown 1896, the 9070 XT maintains a solid 21% to 25% performance advantage over the RTX 5070. Using the Medium preset, it reaches 245 fps at 1440p, while at 4K Ultra it delivers 55 fps compared with 44 fps for the RTX 5070.
Helldivers 2
In Helldivers 2, the 9070 XT maintains a steady 19% to 23% lead over the RTX 5070 across both tested resolutions and presets. At 1440p Ultra, the Radeon card delivers 124 fps compared with 104 fps for the GeForce GPU.
Naraka: Bladepoint
In Naraka: Bladepoint, the 9070 XT leads by 14% to 23% in standard rasterization across both resolutions. With ray tracing enabled, the gap narrows considerably, with the 9070 XT holding a 4% edge at 1440p before the RTX 5070 takes a negligible one-frame lead at 4K.
Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced
In Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced, both cards run into the engine's frame-rate cap at 1440p Very High. Once the resolution or ray-tracing workload is increased, the 9070 XT pulls ahead, maintaining a consistent 6% to 11% lead over the RTX 5070.
War Thunder
In War Thunder, the 9070 XT holds an 18% to 22% advantage using the Movie quality preset. With Ray Tracing Ultra enabled, the Radeon card widens its lead considerably, outperforming the RTX 5070 by 34% at 1440p and 39% at 4K.
Baldur's Gate 3
Baldur's Gate 3 delivers substantial wins for the 9070 XT, which beats the RTX 5070 by up to 44% at 1440p Ultra. More notably, the Radeon card delivers more than double the 1% low performance of the RTX 5070 at 1440p using both presets.
Windrose
In Windrose, the 9070 XT delivers a convincing performance win, leading the RTX 5070 by 21% to 27% at 1440p. At 4K, that advantage expands to as much as 37% using the Epic preset, where the Radeon card maintains a smooth 78 fps average.
Ark: Survival Ascended
Ark: Survival Ascended strongly favors the 9070 XT, which beats the RTX 5070 by roughly 46% to 52% across all tests. At 1440p Epic, the Radeon card delivers 38 fps versus just 25 fps for the RTX 5070, alongside significantly stronger 1% lows.
Red Dead Redemption 2
Red Dead Redemption 2 heavily favors the 9070 XT, which beats the RTX 5070 by 29% to 36% across all tests. It sustains an impressive 83 fps average even at 4K Ultra, while also delivering substantially stronger 1% low performance.
Fortnite
In Fortnite Performance Mode, both GPUs become CPU-limited at 1440p before the RTX 5070 takes a 5% lead at 4K. Switching to Epic Ray Tracing reverses the result, with the 9070 XT leading by 5% to 11%.
Resident Evil Requiem
In Resident Evil Requiem, the 9070 XT commands a decisive 26% to 35% lead across all tested configurations. Enabling Ray Tracing High does little to change the picture, with the Radeon GPU remaining roughly 29% to 30% faster than the RTX 5070.
Mafia: The Old Country
In Mafia: The Old Country, the 9070 XT leads by 29% to 42% using the Medium preset. At Epic quality, the RTX 5070 runs into severe memory limitations, allowing the 9070 XT to deliver nearly double the frame rate at 1440p and more than twice the performance at 4K.
Halo Infinite
In Halo Infinite, the 9070 XT consistently outperforms the RTX 5070 across all tests. It commands a 32% to 36% lead using the Medium preset and maintains a healthy 19% to 26% advantage with Ultra Quality and ray-traced shadows enabled.
Monster Hunter Wilds
The 9070 XT maintains a steady 22% to 27% advantage over the RTX 5070 in Monster Hunter Wilds. It achieves 81 fps at 1440p Ultra with Ray Tracing High enabled and still delivers a very playable 49 fps average at 4K Ultra RT.
Cities: Skylines II
In Cities: Skylines II, the 9070 XT leads the RTX 5070 across all tests. At 1440p Medium, it holds a 33% advantage, though the margin tightens significantly at 4K High Quality, where both GPUs deliver roughly 31 to 32 fps.
Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
In Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, the 9070 XT holds a comfortable 10% to 20% performance lead over the RTX 5070. It delivers 106 fps at 1440p Ultra Quality and maintains a playable 62 fps average at 4K Ultra, where the RTX 5070 falls further behind.
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
The 9070 XT maintains a strong 30% to 33% rasterization lead in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. With Ray Tracing Ultra enabled, the Radeon GPU remains ahead, posting a 16% advantage at 1440p and a 28% margin at 4K.
Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2
In Space Marine 2, performance is very close at 1440p, where the 9070 XT holds a slim 4% to 6% lead. At 4K, however, the Radeon card stretches its advantage to 14% using the Ultra preset and 16% on Medium.
Starfield
In Starfield, the 9070 XT holds a decisive 28% to 44% lead over the RTX 5070 across all tested settings. It delivers a solid 86 fps at 1440p Ultra and maintains a playable 58 fps average at 4K Ultra, leaving the RTX 5070 well behind.
Star Wars Outlaws
In Star Wars Outlaws, the 9070 XT leads by 17% to 26% using the Medium preset. With RTX Direct Lighting Ultra enabled, the Radeon GPU maintains a 9% lead at 1440p, but pulls dramatically ahead at 4K, where the RTX 5070 runs into severe memory limitations.
Marvel's Spider-Man 2
In Spider-Man 2, the 9070 XT outpaces the RTX 5070 by 29% to 33% using the Very High rasterized preset. Even with Ray Tracing Ultimate enabled, the Radeon GPU remains ahead, leading by 24% at 1440p and 20% at 4K.
Stalker 2: Heart of Chornobyl
In Stalker 2, the 9070 XT maintains an 11% to 12% lead at 1440p across both quality presets. At 4K, that margin expands to 18% using the Epic preset and 22% on Medium, accompanied by noticeably stronger 1% low performance.
Indiana Jones and the Great Circle
In Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, the 9070 XT leads by 19% to 25% using the standard Supreme preset. However, enabling Full Ray Tracing shifts the advantage to Nvidia, allowing the RTX 5070 to pull ahead by 10% at 1440p and 19% at 4K.
Performance Summary
Across our 52-game average, the 9070 XT is comfortably faster than the RTX 5070. It delivers a 24% higher average frame rate at 1440p, with that advantage increasing slightly to 25% at 4K. The Radeon GPU also delivers substantially stronger 1% lows overall.
Cost Per Frame
Before wrapping up, here's a look at the cost-per-frame data. Based on our 1440p results, the RTX 5070 carries a 37% premium on a cost-per-frame basis, with that margin increasing slightly to 39% at 4K. That makes the 9070 XT substantially better value at current prices.
As a side note, in Australia the 9070 XT and RTX 5070 are currently priced about the same, making the Radeon GPU roughly 25% better value in terms of cost per frame.
AMD Wins on Performance, VRAM, and Value
There isn't much more to analyze here. Features such as DLSS don't come close to justifying the kind of price premium required to buy an RTX 5070, and I can't envision a gaming scenario where I would choose it over the cheaper 9070 XT, which in my opinion is simply the better all-round buy.
Even at price parity, the 9070 XT is a much stronger proposition. Not only is it generally much faster, but you also get 16GB of VRAM, a particularly valuable commodity right now. The RTX 5070's 12GB buffer has always been somewhat questionable, and when the card also carries a price premium, it becomes very difficult to recommend.
I genuinely can't come up with a realistic justification for why a gamer would pay more for the RTX 5070 than the 9070 XT.
In my view, the RTX 5070 was Nvidia's last reasonably viable GeForce GPU, and even that is no longer true at current prices. The RTX 5070 Ti is now priced at more than $1,100, making it roughly 50% more expensive than the 9070 XT for a similar level of performance. Meanwhile, the RTX 5080 has been a poor value proposition for some time, and current asking prices of around $1,500 only make matters worse. And then there's the RTX 5090.
In fact, while we were putting this benchmark together, RTX 5060 Ti 16GB pricing climbed to around $750, with many models already at or above $800. That puts it at roughly the same price as the RTX 5070 and, more importantly, above the 9070 XT. That means in the space of just a few weeks, the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB went from around $580 to roughly $800, an increase of almost 40%.
None of this comes entirely as a surprise. The speed of the increase is still remarkable, but we warned that higher GeForce pricing was coming. At this point, GeForce pricing is so distorted that Radeon RX 9070 and RX 9060 series GPUs are among the few sensible options left for gamers shopping in this part of the market. If you need a new graphics card, grabbing an RDNA 4 model while pricing remains relatively reasonable may be the clever move.
